definition_zh: 向日葵；葵花；（常大写）向日葵州（美国堪萨斯州的别称）
definition_en: a tall plant with a large round yellow flower whose dark centre is full of edible seeds, which turns to face the sun
core_image: 一人多高的茎顶着巨大的黄色花盘，花盘正中是密密麻麻的瓜子
scene: 夏末，整片田野的黄花盘齐刷刷地朝向东边的朝阳。At the end of summer, the whole field of sunflowers turned to face the rising sun.
sceneCN: 这里 sunflower 是「向日葵」（第 1 个义项：会追着太阳转的高大黄花植物）；句意：夏末，整片向日葵田都转向升起的太阳。

pos.zh: 向日葵；葵花；向日葵州

collocations.zh: 普通向日葵（学名常用说法）

derivatives.zh: 由第二个成分独立成词，义为「花」
与颜色词合成，义为「向日葵般的明黄色」
与 oil 合成，义为「葵花籽油」

senses.title: A tall flower that follows the sun
senses.definition: a tall plant with a very large round yellow flower and dark seed-filled centre, grown for its seeds and oil
senses.definitionCN: 一种高大的植物，花盘巨大、花冠黄色、中心深色且充满种子，种子与油都可利用
senses.example: The sunflower grew taller than the garden fence in one summer.
senses.exampleCN: 一个夏天里，这株向日葵长得比花园篱笆还高。
senses.why: The name joins sun and flower, because the young head of the plant turns to follow the sun across the sky.
senses.whyCN: 这个名字由 sun（太阳）与 flower（花）合成，因为幼嫩的花盘会追随太阳在天空移动。

senses.title: The flower head itself
senses.definition: the big round flowering head of this plant, with yellow petals around a packed centre
senses.definitionCN: 这种植物巨大的圆形花头，黄色花瓣围着一圈密实的中心
senses.example: She put a single sunflower in a glass vase on the table.
senses.exampleCN: 她把一朵向日葵插在桌上的玻璃瓶里。
senses.why: People meet the plant through its head, so the same noun names the cut flower in a market or a vase.
senses.whyCN: 人们通过花盘认识这种植物，所以同一个名词也指市场上、花瓶里的切花。

senses.title: The seeds and their oil
senses.definition: the edible seeds of this plant, or the cooking oil pressed from them
senses.definitionCN: 这种植物可食用的种子，或由它们榨成的食用油
senses.example: Farmers press sunflower oil from the seeds after the harvest.
senses.exampleCN: 收割之后，农民用这些籽榨出葵花籽油。
senses.why: Because the seeds are the main harvest, the plant name spreads to the product sold in shops.
senses.whyCN: 由于种子是主要收成，植物名就顺势指代商店里出售的成品。

senses.title: The bright yellow colour
senses.definition: the strong warm yellow of the petals, used to describe paint, fabric or light
senses.definitionCN: 花瓣那种浓烈的暖黄色，用于形容涂料、布料或光
senses.example: She painted the kitchen door a loud sunflower yellow.
senses.exampleCN: 她把厨房的门刷成了醒目的向日葵黄。
senses.why: The colour is so striking that the flower name itself becomes the shade, as with rose or violet.
senses.whyCN: 这种颜色极其抢眼，花名本身就成了色名，就像 rose 和 violet 一样。

senses.title: A nickname for Kansas
senses.titleCN: 向日葵州（堪萨斯州别称）
senses.definition: the nickname of the American state of Kansas, often written with a capital letter
senses.definitionCN: 美国堪萨斯州的别称，通常大写开头
senses.example: Kansas is known as the Sunflower State on its licence plates.
senses.exampleCN: 堪萨斯州的牌照上印着「向日葵州」的称呼。
senses.why: Where the crop covers the fields, the flower becomes an emblem and the name turns into a place nickname.
senses.whyCN: 在当地田野遍布这种作物的地方，它就成了一种标志，名字也变成了地方别称。

intro.en: Sunflower is an English compound built from sun and flower, which later borrowed the plant name from the Americas.
intro.cn: sunflower 是由 sun 与 flower 构成的英语复合词，后来借用了来自美洲的植物名。

items.en: Sun and flower belong to the native Germanic word stock of English.
items.cn: sun 与 flower 分别来自英语本土词与借词来源，都是很早就有的词。

items.en: The Latin name helianthus joins helios, the sun, and anthos, a flower.
items.cn: 拉丁属名 helianthus 由 helios（太阳）与 anthos（花）合成。

items.en: Greek writers used the same idea for plants whose heads follow the sun.
items.cn: 古希腊作者已用类似的构词指称花头追随太阳的植物。

items.en: The compound sunflower enters English after the American plant reaches Europe.
items.cn: 这种美洲植物传入欧洲后，复合词 sunflower 进入英语。

items.en: The word spreads to seed, oil, colour and place nicknames such as the Sunflower State.
items.cn: 现代英语中，这个词扩展到籽、油、颜色以及向日葵州一类地方别称。

note.en: Sunflower is a sun compound, close to its two parts and to other large garden flowers.
note.cn: sunflower 是带 sun 的复合词，与它的两个成分以及其它大朵园艺花卉相邻。

entries.definition: the star that gives light and heat to the earth
entries.definitionCN: 太阳

entries.definition: the coloured part of a plant that bears the seeds
entries.definitionCN: 花；花朵

entries.definition: a strong warm yellow like the petals of this flower
entries.definitionCN: 向日葵般的明黄色

entries.definition: a small wild flower with white petals and a yellow centre
entries.definitionCN: 雏菊（白瓣黄心的野花）

entries.definition: a garden flower with bright orange or yellow heads
entries.definitionCN: 万寿菊；金盏花

entries.definition: a tree or shrub with small white or yellow flowers
entries.definitionCN: 洋槐；金合欢（与日晷的 gnomon 无直接关联，但同样以花形命名）

normalIntro.en: Sunflower is sun plus flower: a flower that behaves as if it belonged to the sun.
normalIntro.cn: sunflower 是 sun 加 flower：一朵仿佛属于太阳的花。

normal.en: The sun leads and the flower follows, so the two words sit side by side in one name.
normal.cn: 太阳在前领路，花朵在后跟随，两个词就这样并排组成一个名字。

normal.en: Latin helianthus has the same meaning, helios for sun and anthos for flower.
normal.cn: 拉丁属名 helianthus 意思相同：helios 是太阳，anthos 是花。

normal.en: The seeds are the food, sunflower oil is the product, and sunflower yellow is the colour.
normal.cn: 籽是食物，葵花籽油是产品，向日葵黄是颜色。

normal.en: Kansas is the Sunflower State, so the crop became a nickname.
normal.cn: 堪萨斯被称为向日葵州，这种作物成了地方别称。

normal.en: Remember the spelling: one n in sun, and the two words merge without a hyphen.
normal.cn: 记住拼写：sun 只有一个 n，两个词直接连写，不加连字符。

abstract.en: Picture a head taller than a person, a wide yellow ring around a dark seeded hub.
abstract.cn: 想象一个比人还高的花头，一整圈宽宽的黄色花瓣围着深色的花心。

abstract.en: Picture a glass vase on a table holding one bright round flower.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上的玻璃瓶里插着一朵明亮圆润的花。

abstract.en: Picture a press squeezing golden oil out of a dark pile of seeds.
abstract.cn: 想象榨油机从一大堆深色籽里榨出金黄的油。

examples.en: Emily planted sunflowers along the south wall for the bees.
examples.cn: 艾米丽在南墙边种了向日葵，给蜜蜂当花源。

examples.en: A single sunflower can carry hundreds of seeds in its centre.
examples.cn: 一朵向日葵的花心可以容纳上百粒籽。

examples.en: The sunflower harvest provides both seeds and cooking oil.
examples.cn: 向日葵的收成既提供瓜子，也提供食用油。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「三福漏斗」——花瓣像漏斗一样围住花心，一朵就福气满满；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语 sun（太阳，古英语 sunne）+ flower（花，借自拉丁语 flos、古法语 flor），复合指「向着太阳的花」，与拉丁属名 helianthus（helios 太阳 + anthos 花）同构。

sensesIntro.en: Sunflower names the plant, then its flower head, its seeds and oil, its colour, and finally a state nickname.
sensesIntro.cn: sunflower 先指植株，再指花盘、籽与油、颜色，最后指一个州别称。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wide yellow ring around a dark centre of seeds.
core.cn: 核心意象：一圈宽宽的黄瓣，围着一团深色的籽。

branches.en: The whole plant is the basic botanic sense.
branches.cn: 整株植物是最基本的植物学义项。

branches.en: The head is the part people cut and carry home.
branches.cn: 花盘是人们剪下带回家的部分。

branches.en: Seeds and oil turn a plant into a product.
branches.cn: 籽与油把植物变成了产品。

branches.en: The colour and the state nickname both borrow the flower as a sign.
branches.cn: 颜色义与州别称义都把这种花当作标志来借用。

branches.en: The plant is known by its round head in fields and vases alike.
branches.cn: 无论在田野还是花瓶里，人们都靠圆圆的花头认出这种植物。

intro.en: Sunflower is a clear English compound, with sun and flower as the two living parts and a small set of compounds around it.
intro.cn: sunflower 是清晰的英语复合词，sun 与 flower 是两个活的成分，周围还有一小组复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin flower words include flos and flora, while the botanical name helianthus joins Greek helios and anthos.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中表示花的词有 flos 与 flora，植物学名 helianthus 则由希腊语 helios 与 anthos 合成。

items.example: Sun names the light the plant follows.
items.exampleCN: sun 指明这种植物追随的光。

items.example: Flower gives the general item.
items.exampleCN: flower 给出所属的大类。

items.example: Flos is the Latin source of flower.
items.exampleCN: flos 是 flower 的拉丁来源。

items.meaning: the goddess of flowers, the plants of a region
items.example: Flora shares the same flower root.
items.exampleCN: flora 共享同一个「花」词根。

items.example: The form helio- appears in helianthus.
items.exampleCN: 词形 helio- 出现在 helianthus 中。

items.example: The form -anthus ends many plant names.
items.exampleCN: 词形 -anthus 是许多植物名的结尾。

items.meaning: a tall yellow flower that follows the sun
items.example: Sunflower joins a noun of light with a noun of bloom.
items.exampleCN: sunflower 把表示光的词与表示绽放的词拼在一起。

items.example: The ending -s forms sunflowers.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -s 构成复数 sunflowers。

items.meaning: a small grain from which a plant grows
items.example: The seed sense gives sunflower seeds.
items.exampleCN: 「种子」义项构成 sunflower seeds。

latinEntries.meaning: flowers, the plants of a region

definition_zh: 取代；替代；接替；废止；替代旧事物
definition_en: to take the place of something older, often because the new thing is better, newer, or now formally valid
core_image: 新文件盖在旧文件上方：旧的一张被压在下面，不再作数
scene: 办公室里，律师把新合同放在旧合同之上，宣布旧的一张即时作废。The lawyer places the new contract over the old one and says that it supersedes all previous versions.
sceneCN: 这里 supersede 是「取代、废止」（第 1 个义项：新事物接替旧事物并使之失效）；句意：律师把新合同放在旧合同之上，并说它取代此前所有版本。

pos.zh: 取代；替代；接替；废止

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「取代；废止」
动词现在分词作定语，义为「取代性的；起替代作用的」
rare，由动词加 -able 构成，义为「可被取代的」

senses.title: To take the place of something older
senses.definition: to replace something older, usually because the new thing is better or more current
senses.definitionCN: 取代较旧的事物，通常因为新的更好或更合当下
senses.example: Digital maps have superseded paper road atlases.
senses.exampleCN: 数字地图已经取代了纸质公路地图册。
senses.why: The prefix super- means above, so the newer thing is literally placed over the old one and covers it.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 super- 意为「在上方」，新事物被实实在在地放在旧事物上面并把它盖住。

senses.title: To make something no longer valid
senses.definition: to make a law, rule, or clause no longer apply, because a newer one covers the same ground
senses.definitionCN: 因为有了覆盖同样内容的新法新规，使旧法旧规不再适用
senses.example: The new regulation supersedes the rule issued last year.
senses.exampleCN: 新条例废止了去年发布的规则。
senses.why: A document laid on top of another hides it completely, and in law this image became the formal act of cancelling an older provision.
senses.whyCN: 一份文件盖住另一份就等于把它藏起来，在法律中这一画面变成正式让旧条款失效的动作。

senses.title: To be surpassed in a contest
senses.definition: to surpass an earlier record or achievement, as used in sports and technical writing
senses.definitionCN: 在体育与技术写作中表示超越先前纪录或成绩
senses.example: Timing systems were superseded by satellite measurement.
senses.exampleCN: 计时系统被卫星测量所超越。
senses.why: From covering the old, the word drifts into standing higher than it, which is the competitive sense.
senses.whyCN: 由「盖住旧物」引申为「站得更高」，于是生出竞赛中胜过的意思。

intro.en: Supersede comes straight from Latin supersedere, to sit above, built from super, above, and sedere, to sit.
intro.cn: supersede 直接来自拉丁语 supersedere（坐在上方），由 super（在上）与 sedere（坐）构成。

items.en: Sedere means to sit, and super means above.
items.cn: sedere 意为坐，super 意为在上方。

items.en: Supersedere combines them, literally to sit above something.
items.cn: supersedere 将二者合在一起，字面是坐在某物上方。

items.en: The legal phrase supersedere aliqua re means to abstain from some matter.
items.cn: 法律用语 supersedere aliqua re 意为对某事不予处理。

items.en: The verb enters English meaning to put aside or set aside.
items.cn: 该动词进入英语时意为搁置、搁下。

items.en: The sense of replacing or invalidating an older thing becomes dominant.
items.cn: 取代或使旧事物失效的含义逐渐成为主流。

note.en: Supersede belongs to a family of Latin sedere words, and in meaning it overlaps with replace, supplant, and override.
note.cn: supersede 属于拉丁语 sedere 词族，在意义上与 replace、supplant、override 有重叠。

entries.definition: matter that settles at the bottom of a liquid
entries.definitionCN: 沉淀物；沉积物

entries.definition: a period of sitting or meeting
entries.definitionCN: 会议；一段时间

entries.definition: calm and unhurried, composed
entries.definitionCN: 沉着稳重的，只是词根同出 sedere

entries.definition: to take the position of something else
entries.definitionCN: 替换；接替

entries.definition: to take the place of, especially by force or trickery
entries.definitionCN: 排挤掉；取代

entries.definition: to cancel the effect of an earlier rule or decision
entries.definitionCN: 推翻；凌驾于

normalIntro.en: See super and sit inside the word: the new sits above the old and hides it.
normalIntro.cn: 看词里的 super 与 sit：新的坐在旧的上面，把旧的盖住。

normal.en: Super means above and sedere is Latin for sit.
normal.cn: super 表示在上，sedere 是拉丁语的「坐」。

normal.en: The phrase be superseded by is the most common passive form.
normal.cn: 被动短语 be superseded by 是最常见的用法。

normal.en: A covering letter should not supersede the main report.
normal.cn: 附函不应取代主报告本身。

normal.en: Legal clauses often say this agreement supersedes all earlier ones.
normal.cn: 法律条款常说本协议取代先前所有协议。

normal.en: Compare replace: replace is neutral, supersede adds the idea that the old one is out of date.
normal.cn: 对比 replace：replace 中立，supersede 多了「旧的已过时」的意味。

abstract.en: Picture a stack of sheets where the newest sheet hides the page beneath it.
abstract.cn: 想象一摞纸，最上面那张新纸把下面那页完全遮住。

abstract.en: Picture a king seated on a throne built on top of an older throne.
abstract.cn: 想象一位国王坐的宝座建在更旧的宝座之上。

abstract.en: Picture a champion stepping onto a higher podium than the previous season.
abstract.cn: 想象冠军登上比上赛季更高的领奖台阶。

examples.en: The latest software update supersedes the version in the manual.
examples.cn: 最新的软件更新取代了手册中的版本。

examples.en: New evidence superseded the theory that had dominated the field.
examples.cn: 新证据取代了曾主导该领域的理论。

examples.en: These instructions supersede any verbal agreement.
examples.cn: 这些说明取代任何口头约定。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「super 坐」——把 super（在上）与「坐」连起来：新的坐在旧的上面，就把旧的取代了；这只是拆词联想，与真实词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 super（在上）+ sedere（坐）→ supersedere（坐在上方；搁置）→ 英语 supersede，核心义「凌驾于上而取代」。

sensesIntro.en: Supersede begins as a physical image of sitting above, turns into the legal act of cancelling what lies below, and then extends to beating an earlier record.
sensesIntro.cn: supersede 先是「坐在上方」的画面，转为法律上让下层条文作废的动作，再引申为在成绩上胜过旧纪录。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a new sheet laid over an old one.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张新纸盖在旧纸之上。

branches.en: Covering the old thing is the everyday sense of replacing it.
branches.cn: 把旧物盖住就是日常所说的取代。

branches.en: Hiding what lies below becomes the legal sense of voiding an older rule.
branches.cn: 遮住下层引申为法律上让旧规失效。

branches.en: Standing higher becomes the competitive sense of beating a record.
branches.cn: 站得更高就引申为竞赛中打破纪录。

branches.en: A new law replaces an old one by formally cancelling it.
branches.cn: 新法通过正式废止旧法来完成取代。

branches.en: Both voiding a clause and beating a record involve something older losing its place.
branches.cn: 废止条款与打破纪录都涉及旧事物失去位置。

intro.en: Supersede is a Latin compound, with super- on top and the sedere family behind it.
intro.cn: supersede 是拉丁语复合词，上面是前缀 super-，背后是 sedere 词族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin preposition super means above, and the verb sedere means to sit.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语介词 super 意为在上方，动词 sedere 意为坐。

items.example: Super- sets the position of being above.
items.exampleCN: super- 设定「在……之上」的位置。

items.example: Sedere supplies the sitting image.
items.exampleCN: sedere 提供「坐」的画面。

items.example: Supersedere is the direct source.
items.exampleCN: supersedere 是直接来源。

items.example: Supersede is the only common verb with a single d here.
items.exampleCN: 英语中 supersede 是这一词根唯一常见的单 d 拼法。

items.meaning: the root is written -sede only here
items.example: Precede and proceed use the same root with c.
items.exampleCN: precede 与 proceed 用同样的词根却写作 c。

items.example: The suffix -ion turns the verb into a noun.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ion 把动词变成名词。

items.example: The past participle is common in passive clauses.
items.exampleCN: 过去分词常见于被动从句。

items.example: Sedentary keeps the literal sitting sense.
items.exampleCN: sedentary 保留字面上的「坐」。

items.example: Session also descends from sedere.
items.exampleCN: session 同样源自 sedere。

items.example: To settle is to sit down at the bottom.
items.exampleCN: settle 就是坐在底部。

definition_zh: 超声速的；超音速的；超音速飞行
definition_en: moving faster than the speed of sound, or relating to such movement
core_image: 战机冲破音障的那一刻，身后炸开一团白色的音爆云
scene: 试飞员把操纵杆向前推到底，飞机越过音障，机身被一圈白雾包裹。The test pilot pushes the stick forward, and the fighter jet becomes supersonic, wrapped in a ring of white cloud.
sceneCN: 这里 supersonic 是「超音速的」（第 1 个义项：速度超过音速）；句意：试飞员把操纵杆向前推到底，战机达到超音速，机身被一圈白雾包裹。

pos.zh: 超声速的；超音速的；超过声速的
超音速；超音速飞行

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加复数词尾 -s 构成，义为「超声速学；超音速特性」
sub-（在下方）+ sonic，义为「亚声速的」
hyper-（超出）+ sonic，义为「高超音速的」，通常指五倍音速以上

senses.title: Faster than the speed of sound
senses.definition: travelling or designed to travel faster than sound travels through the air
senses.definitionCN: 以超过声音在空气中传播的速度行进，或专为此速度而设计
senses.example: Concorde carried passengers at supersonic speed.
senses.exampleCN: 协和客机以超音速运送旅客。
senses.why: Latin super means above, so an object moving above the speed of sound is literally over that limit.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 super 意为「在上、超过」，速度超过音速的物体字面上就处在这一界限之上。

senses.title: Belonging to sound beyond hearing
senses.definition: in older technical writing, describing sound waves above the range of human hearing
senses.definitionCN: 在较早的技术文献中，指超出人耳听觉范围的声波
senses.example: Older manuals used supersonic for waves above hearing.
senses.exampleCN: 较早的手册用 supersonic 指人耳听不到的声波。
senses.why: Readers first took sonic to mean sound in general, so above sound could also mean beyond what people hear.
senses.whyCN: 早期读者把 sonic 理解为泛指「声音」，于是「高于声音」也就可以指「超出听觉」。

senses.title: Aircraft treated as a noun
senses.titleCN: 超音速飞机；超音速交通
senses.definition: used as a noun, the aircraft or travel that breaks the sound barrier
senses.definitionCN: 作名词时指突破音障的飞机或这类飞行服务
senses.example: Engineers worry about the noise of supersonics over cities.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师担心超音速飞机在城市上空的噪音。
senses.why: Once the adjective was tied to jets, newspapers shortened it to a noun for the whole class of them.
senses.whyCN: 自从这一形容词与喷气机绑定，报纸就把它缩略成名词，指代这一类飞机。

intro.en: Supersonic is a modern coinage, joining Latin super, above, to the Latin root sonus, sound, plus the scientific adjective ending -ic.
intro.cn: supersonic 是近现代人造词，把拉丁语 super（在上）接在拉丁词根 sonus（声音）上，再加科学形容词词尾 -ic。

items.en: Super means above or beyond, and sonus means sound.
items.cn: super 意为在上或超过，sonus 意为声音。

items.en: The compound adjective supersonicus appears in Latin scientific prose far later.
items.cn: 复合形容词 supersonicus 是后来才在拉丁科技术语中出现的。

items.en: The adjective is coined from super and sonic in the century of measurement.
items.cn: 这个词在科学计量时代由 super 与 sonic 组合而成。

items.en: With aviation the word narrows to speeds above the speed of sound.
items.cn: 随着航空发展，这个词收窄为超过音速的速度。

items.en: The noun use for jets and travel is common in journalism.
items.cn: 新闻文体中常用作名词，指喷气机与这类飞行。

note.en: Supersonic shares the sonic root and sits on a scale of speed that runs from subsonic to hypersonic.
note.cn: supersonic 与 sonic 同根，处在从亚音速到高超音速的速度刻度上。

entries.definition: relating to sound waves
entries.definitionCN: 与声波有关的

entries.definition: sound-based underwater detection
entries.definitionCN: 声呐；水下声呐探测

entries.definition: to hold more of a substance than normal
entries.definitionCN: 使过饱和，同用前缀 super-

entries.definition: slower than the speed of sound
entries.definitionCN: 亚音速的；比音速慢的

entries.definition: moving at five times the speed of sound or more
entries.definitionCN: 高超音速的

entries.definition: moving at a speed close to that of sound
entries.definitionCN: 跨音速的

normalIntro.en: Super means above and sonic means of sound, so supersonic sits just above the sound barrier.
normalIntro.cn: super 表示在上，sonic 表示声音，所以 supersonic 就停在音障之上一点。

normal.en: The prefix super- keeps the same job as in supersede.
normal.cn: 前缀 super- 与 supersede 中作用相同，都表示在上或超过。

normal.en: The root sonic appears in sonar and in ultrasonic.
normal.cn: 词根 sonic 也出现在 sonar 与 ultrasonic 中。

normal.en: Supersonic flight is a standard IELTS topic about transport.
normal.cn: supersonic flight 是雅思交通话题中的常见说法。

normal.en: Compare hypersonic, which is several times faster again.
normal.cn: 对比 hypersonic，它又是好几倍的超音速。

normal.en: The noun supersonics names the study of speeds above sound.
normal.cn: 名词 supersonics 指研究超音速的学科。

abstract.en: Picture a jet punching through a white ring of vapour.
abstract.cn: 想象一架喷气机穿过一圈白色水汽云。

abstract.en: Picture a sound wave left far behind, never catching up.
abstract.cn: 想象声波被远远甩在后面，再也追不上。

abstract.en: Picture a thin line in the sky drawn above the noise of the city.
abstract.cn: 想象天空中被画在对城市噪音之上的一条细线。

examples.en: Supersonic aircraft were banned over land because of the noise.
examples.cn: 由于噪音问题，超音速飞机被禁止在陆地上空飞行。

examples.en: The missile accelerates to supersonic speed within seconds.
examples.cn: 导弹在几秒内加速到超音速。

examples.en: Developing supersonic travel remains an engineering challenge.
examples.cn: 发展超音速飞行仍是一项工程挑战。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「super 声音」——把 super（超级）接上「声音」，就是声音之上、比声音还快的超音速；这只是拆词联想，与真实词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 super（在上、超过）+ sonus（声音）→ 英语 sonic（声音的）+ 前缀 super- → supersonic，核心义「在声音之上」。

sensesIntro.en: Supersonic first names anything moving above the speed of sound, then refers to hearing and to the jets themselves.
sensesIntro.cn: supersonic 先指速度高于音速的一切事物，随后涉及听觉范围，最后直接指代这类喷气机。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a jet breaking through a ring of vapour.
core.cn: 核心意象：喷气机撞穿一圈水汽云。

branches.en: Speed above sound is the defining technical sense.
branches.cn: 速度超过声音是这个词的核心技术义。

branches.en: Older usage placed supersonic beyond hearing.
branches.cn: 较早的用法把 supersonic 放在听觉之外。

branches.en: The noun names the aircraft that fly this fast.
branches.cn: 作名词时指以这个速度飞行的飞机。

branches.en: Every supersonic jet exists to break the sound barrier.
branches.cn: 每一架超音速飞机都是为突破音障而造。

branches.en: Beyond hearing and beyond the speed of sound both share the prefix super.
branches.cn: 超出听觉与超出音速都靠前缀 super 表达。

intro.en: Supersonic is built from the prefix super- and the root -son- plus the adjective ending -ic.
intro.cn: supersonic 由前缀 super-、词根 -son- 与形容词词尾 -ic 拼成。

latinIntro.en: Latin super means above, and sonus means sound, so the compound literally reads above sound.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 super 意为在上，sonus 意为声音，所以这个复合词字面上就是「高于声音」。

items.example: Super- places the word above a limit.
items.exampleCN: super- 把词置于某一界限之上。

items.example: The root -son- appears in sonic and sonar.
items.exampleCN: 词根 -son- 出现在 sonic 与 sonar 中。

items.example: The ending -ic marks a technical adjective.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ic 标示科技术语形容词。

items.example: Sonic is the base of the compound.
items.exampleCN: sonic 是复合词的基干。

items.example: Sub- reverses the direction.
items.exampleCN: sub- 把方向反过来。

items.example: Hyper- adds the idea of excess.
items.exampleCN: hyper- 加上过分超出的意思。

items.example: Ultra- also means beyond.
items.exampleCN: ultra- 同样表示超出。

items.example: The ending -s plural hardens it into a subject.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -s 把它固化为学科名。

items.example: Trans- marks crossing.
items.exampleCN: trans- 标示跨越。

items.example: Sonar is an acronym from the same root.
items.exampleCN: sonar 是同根词缩略成的首字母词。

definition_zh: 迷信的；相信迷信的；因迷信而产生的
definition_en: believing that lucky charms, omens, or rituals can change what happens, or coming from such a belief
core_image: 一个人站在门槛上不敢跨过去，嘴里念着一句护身的口诀
scene: 旅店没有门牌十三号，电梯也跳过这一层，前台解释说是客人坚持要这样。The hotel has no room thirteen and the lift skips that floor, because guests hold superstitious beliefs about the number.
sceneCN: 这里 superstitious 是「迷信的」（第 1 个义项：相信吉利或不吉的征兆能带来好运或厄运）；句意：旅店没有十三号房，电梯也跳过那一层，因为客人对这个数字有迷信的念头。

pos.zh: 迷信的；相信迷信的；因迷信而起的

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 superstitio 直接借入，义为「迷信；迷信行为」
由形容词加副词词尾 -ly 构成，义为「迷信地」
由形容词加 -ness 构成，义为「迷信性」

senses.title: Believing in lucky and unlucky signs
senses.definition: believing that certain actions, numbers, or objects bring good or bad luck, without a rational reason
senses.definitionCN: 没有理性依据地相信某些动作、数字或物品会带来好运或厄运
senses.example: Sailors are famously superstitious about whistling at sea.
senses.exampleCN: 水手在海上吹口哨会招灾，这是出了名的迷信。
senses.why: The Latin noun superstitio meant an unreasonable awe or dread, and the adjective inherited the idea of standing in awe of what cannot be explained.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语名词 superstitio 意为不合理的敬畏或畏惧，形容词继承了「对无法解释之物心存敬畏」的意思。

senses.title: Coming from superstition
senses.titleCN: 因迷信而起的；迷信性的
senses.definition: describing an act, fear, or custom that grows out of such beliefs rather than out of evidence
senses.definitionCN: 描述某个行为、恐惧或习俗源自这类信念，而非源自证据
senses.example: The rule about black cats began as a superstitious custom.
senses.exampleCN: 关于黑猫的禁忌起初是一种迷信习俗。
senses.why: Once the adjective described people, it easily moved to the things those people do, so a fear or ritual can be superstitious too.
senses.whyCN: 形容词先描写人，随后自然转到这些人做的事上，于是恐惧或仪式也可以称为迷信的。

senses.title: Devoted with excessive scruple
senses.titleCN: 过分拘谨地信奉的（古义）
senses.definition: an older literary sense of being over scrupulous in religious observance
senses.definitionCN: 较古的文学用法，指在宗教仪式上过分拘谨虔诚
senses.example: Early writers called a worshipper superstitious for keeping every minor rite.
senses.exampleCN: 早期作者把每个小仪式都一丝不苟的信徒称为过分拘泥的。
senses.why: Latin super- plus stare, to stand, suggested standing over or beyond the proper measure of worship.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 super- 与 stare（站立）让人联想到站得过分、超出应有的礼节尺度。

intro.en: Superstitious comes from Latin superstitiosus, beside the noun superstitio, whose exact origin is disputed.
intro.cn: superstitious 来自拉丁语 superstitiosus，与名词 superstitio 并列，其确切来源尚有争议。

items.en: Super means above, and stare means to stand.
items.cn: super 意为在上，stare 意为站立。

items.en: One older account explains superstitio as a standing by or over survivors.
items.cn: 有一种较旧的解释把 superstitio 说成「站在幸存者身旁或之上」。

items.en: Another account links it to superstitem esse, meaning to outlive someone.
items.cn: 另一种说法把它与 superstitem esse（活得比某人更久）联系起来。

items.en: A further view sees super- plus stare as standing beyond due measure.
items.cn: 还有观点把 super- 与 stare 解作「站得超出应有的尺度」。

items.en: Superstitiosus passes into English as superstitious, keeping the sense of empty fear.
items.cn: superstitiosus 传入英语成为 superstitious，保留「无谓畏惧」之义。

items.en: Modern English extends it from religious fear to ordinary lucky and unlucky habits.
items.cn: 现代英语把它从宗教畏惧推广到日常的吉利与不吉习惯。

note.en: Superstitious is the adjective of superstition, and it stands in contrast with rational and scientific attitudes.
note.cn: superstitious 是 superstition 的形容词形式，常与理性、科学的态度形成对照。

entries.definition: a belief that luck comes from signs or charms
entries.definitionCN: 迷信；迷信行为

entries.definition: in a superstitious manner
entries.definitionCN: 以迷信的方式

entries.definition: the quality of being superstitious
entries.definitionCN: 迷信的性能；形容词加 -ness 构成的名词

entries.definition: beyond the powers of nature
entries.definitionCN: 超自然的

entries.definition: too ready to believe things
entries.definitionCN: 轻信的

entries.definition: forbidden by custom or religion
entries.definitionCN: 禁忌的

normalIntro.en: Superstitious carries the Latin family super plus stare, in the same cluster as superstition and supernatural.
normalIntro.cn: superstitious 属于 super 加上 stare 的拉丁词族，与 superstition、supernatural 同在一簇。

normal.en: The noun is superstition and the adverb adds -ly.
normal.cn: 名词是 superstition，副词再加 -ly 变成 superstitiously。

normal.en: Note the double s at the end: the adjective ends in -stition transformed to -stitious.
normal.cn: 注意词尾的拼写由 -stition 变成 -stitious。

normal.en: The common phrase is superstitious about something, not at something.
normal.cn: 常用短语是 superstitious about，而不是 superstitious at。

normal.en: Super- here means beyond, as in supernatural and supersonic.
normal.cn: 这里的 super- 表示超出，与 supernatural、supersonic 一致。

normal.en: Compare rational, the everyday opposite in writing about belief.
normal.cn: 写作中对比 rational，它常作迷信的对立面。

abstract.en: Picture a person frozen on a doorstep, refusing to cross.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人僵在门槛上，怎么也不肯迈过去。

abstract.en: Picture a lucky coin rubbed smooth in a pocket.
abstract.cn: 想象口袋里一枚被摩挲得发亮的幸运硬币。

abstract.en: Picture a temple full of worshippers standing too long in awe.
abstract.cn: 想象一间庙里，众人因敬畏而久久站立。

examples.en: Many athletes are superstitious about the clothes they wear.
examples.cn: 许多运动员对自己穿什么衣服有迷信的讲究。

examples.en: It is a superstitious custom to avoid sitting thirteen people at a table.
examples.cn: 一桌不坐十三个人是一种迷信习俗。

examples.en: Poverty and poor schooling often keep superstitious practices alive.
examples.cn: 贫穷与教育不足常让迷信做法得以延续。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「super 事多」——把 super（超级）与「事多」串起来：讲迷信的人总觉得禁忌太多、事事都要讲究；这只是谐音联想，与真实词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 super-（在上、超出）+ stare（站立）→ superstitio（不合理的敬畏；迷信）→ superstitiosus → 英语 superstitious；确切来源有几种假说，一般认为与「站立」有关。

sensesIntro.en: Superstitious first describes people who believe in signs, then the habits born of that belief, and lastly an older literary sense of excessive ritual devotion.
sensesIntro.cn: superstitious 先描写相信征兆的人，再描写由这种信念产生的习惯，最后还有古旧的用法，指对仪式过分拘谨的虔诚。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: someone halted at a threshold, muttering a charm.
core.cn: 核心意象：有人在门槛前停步，低声念着护身口诀。

branches.en: Believing in lucky signs is the main everyday sense.
branches.cn: 相信吉凶征兆是日常最主要的义项。

branches.en: Acts born of that belief are also called superstitious.
branches.cn: 由这类信念产生的行为也称为迷信的。

branches.en: The oldest sense is excessive scruple in worship.
branches.cn: 最古老的义项是对仪式过分拘谨的虔诚。

branches.en: A superstition and the rituals it produces travel together.
branches.cn: 迷信观念与它催生的仪式总是相伴而行。

branches.en: Both born-of-belief acts and over-scrupulous rites show unmeasured fear.
branches.cn: 源自信念的行为与过分拘谨的仪式都体现出没有节度的畏惧。

intro.en: Superstitious gathers the Latin prefix super- and the verb stare into superstitio, then adds a Latin adjective ending.
intro.cn: superstitious 把拉丁语前缀 super- 与动词 stare 合成 superstitio，再加拉丁语形容词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin super means above, stare means to stand, and superstitio names an unreasonable awe.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 super 意为在上，stare 意为站立，superstitio 则指不合理的敬畏。

items.example: Super- carries the idea of over or beyond.
items.exampleCN: super- 带着「过分、超出」之意。

items.example: Stare supplies the standing image.
items.exampleCN: stare 提供「站立」的画面。

items.example: Superstitio is the immediate source.
items.exampleCN: superstitio 是直接来源。

items.example: Superstitiosus means full of such awe.
items.exampleCN: superstitiosus 表示充满这种敬畏。

items.example: The ending -ous forms the English adjective.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ous 构成英语形容词。

items.example: The ending -ion builds the noun superstition.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ion 构成名词 superstition。

items.example: The ending -ly builds superstitiously.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 superstitiously。

items.example: Supernatural shares the prefix and mood.
items.exampleCN: supernatural 共享前缀与语境。

items.example: Superhuman shows super- meaning beyond.
items.exampleCN: superhuman 显示 super- 表「超出」。

items.example: Supersede also begins with super- above.
items.exampleCN: supersede 同样以 super- 的「在上」开头。

definition_zh: 上层建筑；（建筑的）上部结构；甲板以上的船楼；（马克思主义）上层建筑；（体育设施的）看台
definition_en: the part of a building, ship, or other structure that rises above its base or deck, and in Marxist theory the institutions and ideas that rest on the economic base
core_image: 桥墩上层层垒起的钢梁与桥面，压在看不见的基座之上
scene: 清晨的薄雾里，工人沿着桥墩向上爬。Crews welded the steel superstructure onto the concrete piers before dawn.
sceneCN: 这里 superstructure 是「桥梁的上部结构」（第 1 个义项：建在基础或基座之上的主体部分）；句意是工人们在天亮前把钢结构上层架焊接到混凝土桥墩上。

pos.zh: 名词：上层建筑；上部结构；甲板以上的建筑；看台

collocations.zh: 船上建筑（甲板以上的船楼）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀 -al 构成，义为「上层建筑的；上层结构的」
由本词去掉名词后缀构成，义为「在……之上建造；加建上层」
由前缀 sub-「在下」加 structure 构成，义为「下部结构；基础」，与 superstructure 相对
由本词加 -less「没有」构成，多见于技术与文学评述，义为「没有上层结构的」

senses.title: The upper part above the base
senses.definition: the part of a building, bridge, or other structure that stands above its foundation, base, or ground level
senses.definitionCN: 建筑、桥梁等位于地基、基座或地面标高以上的部分
senses.example: The old warehouse sits on a stone base, and the timber superstructure above it has rotted.
senses.exampleCN: 那座旧仓库建在石头基座上，上面的木质上部结构已经腐烂。
senses.why: super- means above and structura means building, so the noun literally names the building that is placed on top of something else.
senses.whyCN: super- 意为「在上」，structura 意为「建造」，所以这个词字面上就是「架在别的东西上面的那层建造物」；这是从「基础之上」这个空间核心意象直接长出来的第一层含义。

senses.title: The upper decks of a ship
senses.titleCN: 船上建筑；甲板以上的船楼
senses.definition: the cabins, bridge, and other structures on the upper decks of a ship, distinct from the hull
senses.definitionCN: 船体上部甲板上的舱室、驾驶台等建筑，与船体本身相对
senses.example: The captain climbed to the superstructure to watch the harbour lights.
senses.exampleCN: 船长登上上层船楼，望着港口的灯火。
senses.why: A ship already has a watertight shell, the hull; anything built on its deck is a building on top, the same layering image at sea.
senses.whyCN: 船的船体本身就是那个密封的外壳，甲板上再盖起来的舱室和驾驶台就是「架在船体之上的一层」，空间层次意象原封不动搬到了船上。

senses.title: The institutions resting on an economic base
senses.titleCN: 上层建筑（政治、法律、意识形态）
senses.definition: in Marxist theory, the political, legal, religious, and cultural institutions and ideas that arise from and legitimise the economic base
senses.definitionCN: 马克思主义理论中建立在经济基础之上并为之服务的政治、法律、宗教与文化制度及观念
senses.example: Marx argued that changes in the economic base would eventually transform the legal superstructure.
senses.exampleCN: 马克思认为，经济基础的变化最终会改造法律上层建筑。
senses.why: Marxist writers took the builder metaphor and made it social: if the economy is the foundation, then law, politics, and ideas are the floors built upon it, so this sense keeps the same image but shifts from concrete to institutional.
senses.whyCN: 马克思主义作者把建筑比喻搬到社会领域：经济是地基，法律、政治与观念就是在地基上垒起的楼层；核心意象相同，只是从具体的砖石变成了制度与观念，这就是第三层含义。

senses.title: The raised spectator deck
senses.definition: the raised building or seating deck from which spectators watch a race or match, especially at a racecourse or stadium
senses.definitionCN: 设在场地边上供观众观看比赛或赛马的抬高建筑与座席
senses.example: From the top of the superstructure, fans could see the whole track.
senses.exampleCN: 从看台顶层，观众能看清整条赛道。
senses.why: In racing and stadium language the seating block is another building raised on a base, so the general upper-building sense narrows to a spectator-facing deck.
senses.whyCN: 赛马场与体育场里，成排的座席同样是「架在基座之上的一栋建筑」，于是泛指的上部建筑义缩小到面向观众的那个抬高的座席层。

intro.en: Superstructure is a Latin-English hybrid: the Latin prefix super-, above, is joined to the English noun structure, which comes from Latin struere, to build.
intro.cn: superstructure 是拉丁语与英语的混合构词：拉丁语前缀 super-（在上）接到英语名词 structure 上，而 structure 又源于拉丁语 struere（建造）。

items.en: Super means above or over, and struere means to build or pile up; the two are not combined in a single Latin word.
items.cn: super 意为在上、在上方，struere 意为建造、堆叠；不过拉丁语里并没有把两者合用的这一个词。

items.en: Etymology notes list a Latinate form superstructura, with the verb superstruere, meaning to build upon; both describe a layer added on top of an existing base.
items.cn: 词源资料收录了一个拉丁化形式 superstructura，以及动词 superstruere，意为「在上面建造」；两者都表示在已有底座之上加建的一层。

items.en: The noun appears in English in the early seventeenth century as a technical word for the upper part of a building or ship.
items.cn: 该名词在十七世纪初进入英语，作为技术词指建筑物或船体上部的结构。

items.en: Bridge, railway, and ship building made the word common, distinguishing the part above the deck or foundation from the substructure below.
items.cn: 桥梁、铁路与造船业让这个词流行起来，用来区分甲板或地基之上的部分与下方的下部结构。

items.en: Hegel and then Marx used the base and superstructure image for society, with the economist Marx giving the sense its widest currency.
items.cn: 黑格尔与马克思先后用「基础与上层建筑」的比喻描述社会，而经济学家马克思让这个义项最为流传。

items.en: Modern English keeps the engineering and philosophical senses side by side, and adds a sporting one for racecourse accommodation.
items.cn: 现代英语让工程义与哲学义并行，并增加了指赛马场看台建筑的体育义项。

note.en: The first group splits the word into super- and structure and collects its opposite and its relatives; the second group gathers nouns that also name a level above something else but come from different roots.
note.cn: 第一组把词拆成 super- 与 structure，并收入它的反义词与同类词；第二组是同样表示「某物之上的一层」但词根不同的名词。

entries.definition: the building itself or the way its parts are arranged; the plain noun under superstructure
entries.definitionCN: 建筑物或各部分的组合方式；superstructure 背后不带前缀的普通名词

entries.definition: the foundations or lower part of a building; sub- means under and reverses super-
entries.definitionCN: 建筑的根基或下部；sub-「在下」正是 super- 的反面

entries.definition: relating to a superstructure, especially the social institutions resting on an economy
entries.definitionCN: 上部结构的；（社会）上层建筑的

entries.definition: the basic systems a country runs on; infra- means below, the mirror of super-
entries.definitionCN: 国家运转所依赖的基础设施；infra-「在下」与 super- 互为镜像

entries.definition: the supporting frame or the system of rules and ideas inside which something operates
entries.definitionCN: 支撑框架；运作所依托的规则与观念体系

entries.definition: a large impressive building, or metaphorically a complex system built up over time
entries.definitionCN: 宏伟建筑；比喻指长期建立起来的复杂体系

entries.definition: a private room on a ship, one room inside the ship superstructure
entries.definitionCN: 船舱；上层船楼里的一间房

entries.definition: the solid base under a building, the layer that a superstructure rests on
entries.definitionCN: 地基；承载上部结构的底层

normalIntro.en: Read the word as super plus structure: the structure placed above. Once the base is fixed by one prefix, the whole family of above, under, and beside words falls into place.
normalIntro.cn: 把词读成 super 加 structure，即「放在上面的那层结构」。只要用一个前缀把「底座」固定住，上、下、旁这一整族词都会自动归位。

normal.en: super- means above, as in a supervisor standing over the work.
normal.cn: super- 意为「在上」，正如 supervisor 站在工作之上看着。

normal.en: structure comes from Latin struere, to build; a superstructure is a build upon a build.
normal.cn: structure 源于拉丁语 struere「建造」，所以 superstructure 就是「建在建造物之上的建造物」。

normal.en: Its opposite is the substructure under it.
normal.cn: 它的反面就是垫在下面的 substructure（下部结构）。

normal.en: Infrastructure, built in front of everything else, is the same root with a different prefix.
normal.cn: infrastructure 是最先就位的那层基建，同一个词根，只是换了前缀。

normal.en: In Marxist writing the economic base supports the superstructure of law, politics, and ideas.
normal.cn: 在马克思主义写作里，经济基础托着法律、政治与观念构成的上层建筑。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge: the piers are hidden in the water, the steel superstructure rides on top.
abstract.cn: 想象一座桥：桥墩埋在水下，钢制上部结构骑在它们之上。

abstract.en: Picture a ship whose deck carries a white block of cabins, a building on a float.
abstract.cn: 想象一艘船，甲板上顶着一块白色的舱室楼，像浮在水上的建筑。

abstract.en: Picture society as a house: workshops on the ground floor, courts and parliaments stacked upstairs.
abstract.cn: 把社会想象成一栋房子：底下是工坊，楼上叠着法院与议会。

examples.en: Engineers inspected the superstructure of the bridge after the storm.
examples.cn: 风暴过后，工程师检查了桥梁的上部结构。

examples.en: The ferry has a modern superstructure but an ageing hull.
examples.cn: 这艘渡轮上层船楼很现代，船体却已老旧。

examples.en: Some historians argue that the legal superstructure of the empire outlived its economy.
examples.cn: 一些历史学家认为，帝国的法律上层建筑比它的经济基础存续得更久。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「速扑 + 结构」——速速扑上去叠好的结构，就是堆在底座之上的上层建筑；这只是谐音拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语前缀 super-（在上）+ 拉丁语 struere（建造，名词 structura 意为建造物）→ 英语 structure → 十七世纪初英语 superstructure，核心义「架在底座之上的那层建造物」。

sensesIntro.en: Superstructure starts as the concrete part of a building above its base, extends to the same layer on a ship, then to the institutions that rest on an economic base, and finally narrows to a racecourse spectator deck.
sensesIntro.cn: superstructure 先指建筑物基础之上的实体部分，再扩展到船体甲板之上的建筑，然后转移为架在经济基础之上的制度观念，最后缩小到赛马场与球场的看台建筑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a steel frame lifted onto a stone base.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座架在石头基座上的钢架。

branches.en: The everyday sense names the concrete part above a foundation.
branches.cn: 日常义指的是地基之上的实体部分。

branches.en: The marine sense moves the same layer onto a ship deck.
branches.cn: 海事义把同一层次搬到了船甲板上。

branches.en: The philosophical sense turns the builder image into social institutions.
branches.cn: 哲学义把建筑比喻转成了社会制度。

branches.en: The sporting sense narrows the raised building to spectator seating.
branches.cn: 体育义把抬高的建筑缩小为观众座席。

branches.en: Both the bridge frame and the grandstand are structures raised on a base.
branches.cn: 桥架与看台都是建在基座上的抬高建筑。

intro.en: Superstructure pairs the Latin prefix super- with the Latin-derived English word structure, and the whole family of over, under, and beside words shares that second half.
intro.cn: superstructure 由拉丁语前缀 super- 与拉丁词源的英语名词 structure 组成，上、下、旁一族词都共享后半截。

latinIntro.en: Latin super means above, over; struere means to build or pile up; superstruere means to build on top of something.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 super 意为在上、在上方；struere 意为建造、堆叠；superstruere 意为在别的东西上面建造。

items.example: The prefix super- marks a higher position.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 super- 标记更高的位置。

items.example: Struere is the building verb behind structure.
items.exampleCN: struere 是 structure 背后的「建造」动词。

items.meaning: a building or the arrangement of parts
items.example: Structure supplies the second half of the word.
items.exampleCN: structure 提供了这个词的后半截。

items.example: Superstructure is the direct target of this entry.
items.exampleCN: superstructure 是本词条的目标词。

items.meaningCN: 由 -al 构成的形容词：上层结构的
items.example: The suffix -al turns it into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -al 把它变成形容词。

items.example: Sub- is the mirror of super-.
items.exampleCN: sub- 是 super- 的镜像。

items.example: Substructure is the opposite layer.
items.exampleCN: substructure 是相反的那一层。

items.example: Infra- gives another kind of lower layer.
items.exampleCN: infra- 给出另一种下层。

items.example: The suffix -al builds superstructural from the noun.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -al 由名词构成 superstructural。

definition_zh: 监督的；管理的；监管的；负责监管员工的；指导性的
definition_en: relating to the work of watching over people, work, or an activity to make sure it is done properly
core_image: 工头站在脚手架旁，一边看一边指点工人怎样干活
scene: 新来的工头在工地上来回走动，检查每个工人的操作是否合规。She has a supervisory role at the plant and reports every accident directly.
sceneCN: 这里 supervisory 是「监督性的、负责监督的」（第 1 个义项：负责看管工作与员工是否按规矩完成的）；句意是她在工厂担任监督职务，任何事故都要直接上报。

pos.zh: 形容词：监督的；管理的；负责监管的；指导性的

collocations.zh: 监督角色；监督管理职能

derivatives.zh: 基础动词，义为「监督；管理；指导」
由动词省略 -or 加 -ion 构成，义为「监督；管理」
由 supervise 加 -or 构成，义为「监督者；主管」
由 supervisor 加 -ial 构成，义为「监督者的」，比 supervisory 少见
由 supervise 加过去分词词尾构成，义为「受到监督的；有人看管的」

senses.title: Concerned with watching over others at work
senses.titleCN: 监督性的；负责看管工作
senses.definition: relating to the job of watching over other staff and their work to ensure it is done correctly
senses.definitionCN: 与看管其他员工及其工作、确保按规定完成有关的
senses.example: Only staff with supervisory duties are allowed in the control room.
senses.exampleCN: 只有负有监督职责的人员才允许进入控制室。
senses.why: super- means above and videre means to see, so the adjective describes the role of the one who looks over the work from a higher position.
senses.whyCN: super- 意为「在上」，videre 意为「看」，所以这个词描述的是「从上往下看着工作」的那种角色；看管的画面加上形容词词尾就得到「监督性的」这一层含义。

senses.title: Officially in charge
senses.definition: having the position of being in charge of a part of an organisation or a team of people
senses.definitionCN: 拥有主管某个部门或某组人员的正式职位
senses.example: He was promoted to a supervisory position after two years on the line.
senses.exampleCN: 他在流水线上干了两年后被提升为主管岗位。
senses.why: From watching the work it is a short step to owning the responsibility for it, so the adjective also marks a formal rank above the workers.
senses.whyCN: 从「看着工作」到「对工作负责」只差一步，因此这个词也用来标记高于普通员工的正式职级，即管理、主管的。

senses.title: Mounted in a watchtower
senses.definition: relating to an agency or committee whose legal duty is to check that rules are followed
senses.definitionCN: 与依法负责检查规则是否被遵守的机构或委员会有关的
senses.example: The bank faces a fine from the supervisory authority for weak controls.
senses.exampleCN: 由于风控不力，这家银行面临监管机构的罚款。
senses.why: Public agencies that check compliance are watchtowers for whole industries, so the same seeing-from-above image becomes the regulatory, official sense.
senses.whyCN: 为整个行业检查合规状况的公共机构就像瞭望塔，于是「从高处看」的同一幅画面变成了官方的监管含义，即监管的。

senses.title: Guiding a student or trainee
senses.definition: relating to the guidance given to a student, trainee, or research candidate by a senior person
senses.definitionCN: 与资深人员对研究生、受训者或论文候选人给予的指导有关的
senses.example: Her supervisory meetings with the doctoral students are held every other week.
senses.exampleCN: 她每两周与博士生开一次指导会。
senses.why: A supervisor also watches how a person grows in skill, so the word covers advice and coaching as well as checking.
senses.whyCN: supervisor 还看一个人如何一点点长本事，所以这个词除了检查，也覆盖指点与带教，即指导性的。

intro.en: Supervisory comes from supervise, which joins Latin super-, above, and videre, to see, then borrows the Latin adjective ending -ory through the noun supervisor.
intro.cn: supervisory 来自 supervise，由拉丁语 super-（在上）与 videre（看）组成，再经名词 supervisor 借入拉丁语形容词词尾 -ory。

items.en: Super means above and videre means to see; classical Latin supervisee and supervidere are formation parallels rather than the direct source of the English word.
items.cn: super 意为在上，videre 意为看；古典拉丁语里的 supervisee、supervidere 只是同构形式，并不是英语词的直接来源。

items.en: Medieval Latin supervisor meant an overseer or inspector, a person appointed to look over work.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 supervisor 指监工或检查者，即被派去查看工作的人。

items.en: English takes supervisor as a noun for a person who watches over members of the clergy or a district of the church.
items.cn: 英语借入 supervisor，指各级教会或教区中负责监察的神职与巡察人员。

items.en: The verb supervise appears in the late sixteenth century, and from it come the agent noun and the general sense of overseeing work.
items.cn: 动词 supervise 在十六世纪后期出现，并由此派生出施事名词以及泛指的「监督工作」含义。

items.en: Factories, railways, and schools turn supervision into an everyday workplace duty, and the adjective supervisory follows the noun.
items.cn: 工厂、铁路与学校把 supervision 变成日常的工作职责，形容词 supervisory 也随之从名词派生。

items.en: Whether supervisory followed supervisor or supervise is not documented; either way the form keeps the Latin suffix -orius intact.
items.cn: supervisory 究竟由 supervisor 还是 supervise 派生，资料未载；无论哪条路径都完整保留了拉丁后缀 -orius。

note.en: The first group is the word family: verb, noun, and agent noun that share the same super- plus videre core. The second group holds adjectives that also describe authority or check-up but come from other roots.
note.cn: 第一组是同一词族：共享 super- 加 videre 核心的动词、名词与施事名词；第二组是同样表示权力或检查、但词根不同的形容词。

entries.definition: to watch over people or work and make sure things are done properly
entries.definitionCN: 监督；管理；指导

entries.definition: a person whose job is to oversee a team or a piece of work
entries.definitionCN: 监督者；主管

entries.definition: the act of overseeing people, work, or a process
entries.definitionCN: 监督；管理

entries.definition: relating to a supervisor; a longer and less common alternative to supervisory
entries.definitionCN: 监督者的；作为同义替代词的罕见形容词

entries.definition: carried out under somebody else watchful eye
entries.definitionCN: 在他人看管下进行的

entries.definition: relating to planning, organising, and running work rather than watching it
entries.definitionCN: 管理的；与计划组织工作有关的

entries.definition: relating to the running of an office, records, and routine procedures
entries.definitionCN: 行政的；与办公事务和程序有关的

entries.definition: relating to the official bodies that set and enforce rules
entries.definitionCN: 监管的；与执行规则的官方机构有关的

entries.definition: the noun of watching and checking; a near synonym of supervision
entries.definitionCN: 监督；检查；与 supervision 近义的名词

normalIntro.en: Supervisory is supervision wearing an adjective ending. The prefix says from above, the stem says see, and the suffix says having the quality of.
normalIntro.cn: supervisory 就是给 supervision 换上一个形容词词尾：前缀表示「在上」，词干表示「看」，词尾表示「具有……性质的」。

normal.en: super- means above, as in superstructure or superior.
normal.cn: super- 意为「在上」，如 superstructure、superior。

normal.en: Latin videre means to see, and it also gives vision and visible.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 videre 意为「看」，vision 与 visible 也出自同一个词干。

normal.en: The suffix -ory means having the quality of, as in advisory or obligatory.
normal.cn: -ory 表示「具有……性质的」，如 advisory、obligatory。

normal.en: The word marks a role, not the person: a supervisor does supervisory work.
normal.cn: 这个词标记的是一种职能而不是人：supervisor 从事 supervisory 工作。

normal.en: At work the gap between supervisory and managerial is that one checks, the other plans.
normal.cn: 在工作场合，supervisory 与 managerial 的差别在于前者检查、后者规划。

abstract.en: Picture a second pair of eyes hovering above a workbench.
abstract.cn: 想象有一双额外的眼睛悬在工作台上方。

abstract.en: Picture the row of seats on the factory floor where the chief sits and sees everything.
abstract.cn: 想象工厂地面上那排高脚座，工头坐在那里什么都看得见。

abstract.en: Picture a checklist clipped to a clipboard, one tick for every rule followed.
abstract.cn: 想象夹在写字板上的检查表，每遵守一条规则就多一个勾。

examples.en: She took on supervisory duties when the department head left.
examples.cn: 部门主管离开后，她承担起了监督管理的职责。

examples.en: The supervisory board meets four times a year.
examples.cn: 监事会每年开四次会。

examples.en: New nurses work under supervisory guidance for the first month.
examples.cn: 新护士头一个月在指导教师的带领下工作。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「super 看着你」——super 高你一等，visor 像头上一顶察看用的帽檐，合起来就是站着看你干活，也就是监督性的；这只是谐音拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语前缀 super-（在上）+ 拉丁语 videre（看）→ 中世纪拉丁语 supervisor（监察者）→ 英语 supervisor → supervise → 形容词 supervisory（-ory 表性质），核心义「在上方看着」。

sensesIntro.en: Supervisory moves from the core act of watching work, to holding a rank above workers, to the legal checking done by official agencies, and to the guidance of a student by a senior teacher.
sensesIntro.cn: supervisory 从「看着工作」的核心动作出发，先指拥有高于普通员工的职级，再指官方机构的法定检查，最后指资深教师对学生的指导。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a foreman standing on scaffolding and watching the crew.
core.cn: 核心意象：工头站在脚手架上看着下面的工人。

branches.en: Watching staff at work is the core job sense.
branches.cn: 在工作场所看管员工是核心的职能义。

branches.en: Being in charge is the rank that goes with the watching.
branches.cn: 管理职务是与「看管」相连的职级义。

branches.en: Official checking turns the image into regulation.
branches.cn: 官方检查把画面转成了监管义。

branches.en: Guiding a student keeps the watchful image in teaching.
branches.cn: 指导学生把看护的画面留在了教学场景里。

branches.en: A supervisory post both involves watching and carries formal authority.
branches.cn: 监督性岗位既包含看管，也带着正式权力。

intro.en: Supervisory is built from three pieces: the prefix super-, the seeing root vid, and the adjective ending -ory, with supervise, supervisor, and supervision sharing the middle.
intro.cn: supervisory 由三部分组成：前缀 super-、表示「看」的词根 vid- 与形容词词尾 -ory；中间的 supervise、supervisor、supervision 共享同一词干。

latinIntro.en: Latin super means above, videre means to see, and the suffix -orius marks a quality; the stems supervisee and supervidere show the same two elements put together.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 super 意为在上，videre 意为看，-orius 标记性质；supervisee、supervidere 这类词干显示了两者拼合的同构方式。

items.example: The prefix super- sets the viewer above the work.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 super- 把观看者放在工作之上。

items.example: The root vid- also hides in vision and visible.
items.exampleCN: 词根 vid- 也藏在 vision 与 visible 里。

items.example: To supervise is to look over the work.
items.exampleCN: supervise 就是从上往下看着工作。

items.example: A supervisor is the person who does it.
items.exampleCN: supervisor 是做这件事的人。

items.example: Supervision is the act itself.
items.exampleCN: supervision 是动作本身。

items.example: The suffix -or forms supervisor.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -or 构成 supervisor。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或结果的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ion forms supervision.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ion 构成 supervision。

items.example: The suffix -ory forms supervisory.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ory 构成 supervisory。

items.meaningCN: 由 -al 构成的罕见形容词：监督者的
items.example: The suffix -al gives a rare rival form.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -al 给出一个罕见的同义形式。

items.example: The participle -ed forms supervised.
items.exampleCN: 分词词尾 -ed 构成 supervised。

latinEntries.example: The stem shows the two elements combined.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 这个词干展示了两者的拼合。

latinEntries.meaning: one who sees; that which sees

definition_zh: 取代；替代；（尤指）挤掉原有的东西而占其位；排挤
definition_en: to take the place of someone or something, especially by overreaching or displacing them, so that the old one is pushed out
core_image: 一个人踩掉原先站在台上的那位，自己站到台中央
scene: 旧式打字机被电脑悄悄挤走，办公室一夜之间全换了。Within a decade, cheap printers supplanted the copying firm that once served the town.
sceneCN: 这里 supplant 是「取代、挤掉」（第 1 个义项：用更新或更有力的东西把原有的东西排挤出去）；句意是十年之内，廉价打印机取代了那家曾经服务全镇的复印公司。

pos.zh: 及物动词：取代；替代；排挤

derivatives.zh: 由动词加施事后缀 -er 构成，义为「取代者；取而代之的人」
由现在分词转化成的名词，义为「取代；排挤」
由动词加 -ation 构成的罕见名词，义为「取代行为」
由过去分词构成的形容词，义为「被取代的；已被挤掉的」

senses.title: To take the place of something
senses.definition: to replace someone or something, usually because the new thing is more effective, and push the old one aside
senses.definitionCN: 用更新、更有力的事物换掉原有的事物，并把旧的排挤到一边
senses.example: Electric drills quickly supplanted hand tools on the site.
senses.exampleCN: 电钻很快在工地上取代了手工工具。
senses.why: The Latin prefix sub-, under, plus planta, sole of the foot, literally describes stepping under someone, a stepping that pushes the other out of place.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语前缀 sub-（在下）加 planta（脚掌）字面上就是「踩到别人脚下」，这一踩就会把原来的那位挤走；核心意象直接给出「取代」这一层含义。

senses.title: To unseat an incumbent
senses.titleCN: 取代在任者；把某人赶下位
senses.definition: to replace a person in a post or position, often by clever or unfair means
senses.definitionCN: 常以高明或不光彩的手段顶替某个职位上的人
senses.example: His rivals planned to supplant him at the head of the party.
senses.exampleCN: 他的对手们盘算着在党内把他从领导位置上挤走。
senses.why: Stretching a foot under a seated rival and lifting them off the seat is the old political image of supplanting, so the word keeps a personal and slightly hostile flavour.
senses.whyCN: 把脚伸到坐着的人底下再一抬，是古代政治里「把对手掀下座位」的画面，所以这个词带着针对人、且略带敌意的一层。

senses.title: To displace a species or idea
senses.titleCN: 排挤；挤占（其他物种或观念的位置）
senses.definition: to displace another species, custom, or language by spreading into its territory or field
senses.definitionCN: 通过侵入其地盘或领域而把别的物种、风俗或语言挤出原位
senses.example: Invasive weeds have supplanted much of the native grass.
senses.exampleCN: 入侵杂草已排挤掉大部分本地牧草。
senses.why: Ecology borrowed the verb because a stronger plant crowded onto a rival place reads exactly like a new ruler installed on a rival throne.
senses.whyCN: 生态学借用这个动词，因为强势植物挤占对手地盘，读起来就像新统治者坐上对手的王座。

senses.title: To be mistaken for a substitute
senses.definition: to be wrongly used instead of the verb substitute, which means to put one thing in place of another rather than to push an old one out
senses.definitionCN: 被误用为 substitute（用一件东西替换另一件），而本词的含义是排挤并占位，而非单纯替用
senses.example: Careful writers keep supplant, which means replace, apart from substitute.
senses.exampleCN: 细心的作者会把意为「取代」的 supplant 与 substitute 区分开。
senses.why: This is a usage point rather than a separate sense: the near homophone substitute belongs to the same Latin word, which meant to substitute or take the place of, which is why the two are confused, though only supplant carries the pushing-out edge.
senses.whyCN: 这不是一个独立义项，而是用法提醒：近音的 substitute 出自同一个拉丁语词，原义就是「替换、顶替」，这正是两者易混的原因，但只有 supplant 带「挤走」的锋利边缘。

intro.en: Supplant comes from Latin supplantare, to trip up or overthrow, from sub-, under, and planta, the sole of the foot: to get a foot under someone and make them fall.
intro.cn: supplant 来自拉丁语 supplantare，意为「绊倒、推翻」，由 sub-（在下）与 planta（脚掌）组成：把脚伸到别人底下，让对方跌倒。

items.en: Planta means the sole of the foot, and supplantare means to trip someone up.
items.cn: planta 意为脚掌，supplantare 意为把某人绊倒。

items.en: Vulgar Latin kept the tripping verb as supplantare with the same sense.
items.cn: 俗拉丁语保留了表示「绊倒」的动词 supplantare，含义不变。

items.en: Old French has the verb supplanter in the same tripping sense.
items.cn: 古法语有同义的动词 supplanter，仍表示绊倒。

items.en: English borrows the word from Old French in the thirteenth century, first in the sense to trip up or overthrow.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪从古法语借入这个词，最初表示绊倒或推翻。

items.en: By the sixteenth century the word settles on the modern sense of displacing or taking the place of a person or thing.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，这个词固定为现代含义：取代或顶替某人某物。

items.en: The twentieth century extends supplant to plants, languages, and technologies overtaking rivals.
items.cn: 二十世纪把 supplant 扩展到植物、语言与技术挤占并取代对手。

note.en: The first group shares the supplant stem or the Latin -plantare root, including the near homophone substitute that causes most confusion. The second group holds near synonyms with the same take-the-place-of meaning.
note.cn: 第一组共享 supplant 词干或拉丁 -plantare 词根，其中近音的 substitute 最易混淆；第二组是同样表示「顶替占位」的近义词。

entries.definition: a person or thing that replaces another, often by pushing it out
entries.definitionCN: 取代者；取而代之的人或物

entries.definition: the act of taking the place of something else
entries.definitionCN: 取代；排挤

entries.definition: the act of supplanting; a rare noun formed on the verb
entries.definitionCN: 取代行为；由动词构成的罕见名词

entries.definition: to put one thing in the place of another; it shares the Latin situs root, not planta, so it is only close in sound
entries.definitionCN: 用一件东西换掉另一件；词根是 situs 而非 planta，只是发音相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to put a new thing in the place of an old one, the plain neutral verb
entries.definitionCN: 用新的替换旧的，最中性的动词

entries.definition: to force something out of its usual place, close to supplant in ecology
entries.definitionCN: 迫使某物离开原位，与 supplant 的生态义接近

entries.definition: to take over from something older because it is better or newer
entries.definitionCN: 因更好或更新而取代旧事物

entries.definition: to seize a position or power that belongs to someone else
entries.definitionCN: 篡夺属于他人的职位或权力

normalIntro.en: Split supplant into sub plus plant: a plant puts its foot under a rival and pushes. The image of a physical shove is what separates the word from the neutral replace.
normalIntro.cn: 把 supplant 拆成 sub 加 plant：一株植物把脚伸到对手底下再一推。这个「推」的画面正是它区别于中性的 replace 的关键。

normal.en: The prefix sub- means under, as in submarine or submerge.
normal.cn: 前缀 sub- 意为「在下」，如 submarine、submerge。

normal.en: Latin planta means the sole of the foot, and it also gives plant.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 planta 意为脚掌，plant「植物」也出自它。

normal.en: So supplant is literally to plant a foot under someone and trip them.
normal.cn: 所以 supplant 字面就是「把脚伸到别人脚下把他绊倒」。

normal.en: The common passive is be supplanted by, used for old technologies and species.
normal.cn: 最常见的是被动结构 be supplanted by，多用于旧技术与物种。

normal.en: Keep it apart from substitute, which is stronger in sound and neutral in meaning.
normal.cn: 把它与 substitute 分开：后者发音更重，含义却是中性的「替代」。

abstract.en: Picture a challenger stepping onto a podium while the old winner stumbles off.
abstract.cn: 想象挑战者踏上领奖台，而旧赢家踉跄着退下去。

abstract.en: Picture a fast weed winding its roots under a garden plant and taking its patch of light.
abstract.cn: 想象一株疯长的杂草把根伸到园中植株底下，抢走它那片阳光。

abstract.en: Picture a fax machine carried out of an office as a printer is wheeled in.
abstract.cn: 想象传真机被搬出办公室，打印机正被推了进来。

examples.en: Streaming services have largely supplanted DVDs in most households.
examples.cn: 在大多数家庭中，流媒体服务已在很大程度上取代了 DVD。

examples.en: The young general was accused of trying to supplant the king.
examples.cn: 那位年轻的将军被指控企图取代国王。

examples.en: Foreign species can supplant native plants in a few seasons.
examples.cn: 外来物种可能只需几个季节就会排挤掉本地植物。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「撒一片」——把新种子撒满整片地，旧的苗就被挤掉了，也就是取代；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 sub-（在下）+ planta（脚掌）→ 拉丁语 supplantare（绊倒；推翻）→ 俗拉丁语 supplantare → 古法语 supplanter → 十三世纪英语 supplant（绊倒、推翻）→ 十六世纪固定为「取代」，核心义「在下面伸脚把对手挤走」。

sensesIntro.en: Supplant begins with the physical act of tripping someone, narrows to pushing a person out of a post, then spreads to things that displace others, and finally appears in a usage note against the sound-alike substitute.
sensesIntro.cn: supplant 从「伸脚绊人」的动作出发，先缩小为「把人挤下职位」，再扩展到挤占他物的事物，最后在用法提醒中与近音的 substitute 相对照。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a foot slid under a rival to tip them off the stage.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只脚滑到对手底下，把他从台上掀下去。

branches.en: Taking the place of a thing is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 取代一件东西是日常义项。

branches.en: Unseating a person keeps the political edge of the tripping image.
branches.cn: 把人挤下位保留了绊倒画面的政治色彩。

branches.en: Displacing a species or idea extends the shove to nature and culture.
branches.cn: 排挤物种与观念把这一推延伸到自然与文化。

branches.en: The usage sense keeps the verb apart from its sound-alike substitute.
branches.cn: 用法义把它与近音的 substitute 区分开来。

branches.en: A thing and a person are both removed from their place by a stronger rival.
branches.cn: 物与人都是被更强的对手挤出原位的。

intro.en: Supplant is built on the Latin prefix sub- and the plant root that also gives plant and plantation, with an English family of supplanter, supplanting, and supplantation around it.
intro.cn: supplant 建立在拉丁语前缀 sub- 与 plant 词根之上，plant、plantation 同出此根；英语围绕它又长出 supplanter、supplanting、supplantation。

latinIntro.en: Latin sub means under, planta means the sole of the foot, and supplantare means to trip up; the image of a foot slipped under a rival survives in every modern use.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sub 意为在下，planta 意为脚掌，supplantare 意为绊倒；一只脚滑到对手底下的画面保留在现代每一种用法里。

items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 加上「做事的人」。
