definition_zh: 柔软的；柔韧的；灵活的；易弯的
definition_en: able to bend or move easily without breaking, and quick to adapt
core_image: 一根打湿的柳条被弯成弧形，松手后恢复原状
scene: 体操运动员把腰向后弯成一个完整的弧。The gymnast was supple enough to bend backwards into a full arc.
sceneCN: 这里 supple 是「柔软的、易弯的」（第 1 个义项：身体或材料能轻易弯曲而不折断）；句意：这名体操运动员身体足够柔韧，能向后弯成一个完整的弧。

pos.zh: 柔软的；柔韧的；易弯的
（比喻）灵活的；适应力强的

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「柔韧性；灵活性」
旧用法或方言中保留的同源形容词形式，义为「柔软的；灵活的」，现代英语少见（存疑说明）

senses.title: Easily bent without breaking
senses.definition: describing a material or body that bends easily and smoothly without cracking
senses.definitionCN: 形容材料或身体能够轻易而顺畅地弯曲，不易开裂
senses.example: New leather shoes need wax to stay supple.
senses.exampleCN: 新皮鞋需要上蜡才能保持柔软。
senses.why: The Latin source suggests bending under control and giving way without damage, which is exactly the image of a pliant rod.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源暗示「受控地弯曲、让步而不损坏」，这正是柔韧枝条的画面。

senses.title: Moving with easy grace
senses.definition: describing a body or limbs that move easily, smoothly, and with grace
senses.definitionCN: 形容身体或四肢活动轻松、流畅，姿态优雅
senses.example: Dancers need supple limbs and strong ankles.
senses.exampleCN: 舞者需要柔韧的四肢和强健的脚踝。
senses.why: If a thing can bend freely, the body that bends so easily moves gracefully, so the physical quality becomes a sign of grace.
senses.whyCN: 东西能自由弯曲，身体弯曲得如此轻松，动作就显得优雅，于是这一物理属性成为优雅的标志。

senses.title: Willing to bend to others
senses.definition: willing to yield to other people and not fixed or stubborn in view
senses.definitionCN: 愿意顺他人之意，不固执己见
senses.example: Years of service had made him supple in temper.
senses.exampleCN: 多年的服务生涯使他的性情变得柔顺。
senses.why: A mind that bends instead of breaking is read as yielding, so the flexible object becomes a picture of a compliant person.
senses.whyCN: 会弯而不断的精神被读作让步，于是「柔软的东西」就成了「顺从的人」的图景。

senses.title: Quick and agile of mind
senses.definition: describing a mind or voice that turns easily and responds quickly to new situations
senses.definitionCN: 形容头脑或嗓音能轻松变化，迅速应对新情况
senses.example: Age had not dimmed her supple mind.
senses.exampleCN: 岁月并未让她那灵活的头脑变得迟钝。
senses.why: The bending of the body is transferred to the mind, where flexibility means the ability to adapt on the spot.
senses.whyCN: 身体的弯折被转用到头脑上，灵活性就变成了随机应变的能力。

senses.title: Adaptable to changing needs
senses.definition: describing a system, plan, or structure that can be changed easily as needs alter
senses.definitionCN: 形容制度、计划或结构能随需要变化而轻易调整
senses.example: A supple tax system can absorb sudden changes.
senses.exampleCN: 一个灵活可调的税制能够适应突发的变动。
senses.why: Something supple can take many shapes on demand, so an abstract rule that can bend becomes adaptable.
senses.whyCN: 柔韧之物能按需改变形状，因此能弯的抽象规则就是可调整的规则。

senses.title: Soft and pleasant to hear
senses.definition: describing a sound or voice that is soft, smooth, and pleasing
senses.definitionCN: 形容声音或嗓音柔和、圆润、悦耳
senses.example: Her supple voice filled the small room.
senses.exampleCN: 她柔和的嗓音充满了那间小屋。
senses.why: A smooth surface bends sound gently, so the word for pliant things is used for sounds that flow without roughness.
senses.whyCN: 平滑的表面能温柔地托住声音，于是形容柔韧之物的词被用来形容流畅无糙的声音。

senses.title: Loose and relaxed in texture
senses.definition: describing soil or cloth that is loose, yielding, and not firm
senses.definitionCN: 形容土壤或布料疏松、易于形变而不坚硬
senses.example: The gardener worked the supple earth with bare hands.
senses.exampleCN: 园丁徒手翻动着松软的泥土。
senses.why: The core sense of yielding to pressure also covers things that give way under the hand, such as soil and fabric.
senses.whyCN: 「受压让步」的核心义也涵盖在手下一按就变形的东西，如泥土和布料。

senses.title: In flexible quantity
senses.titleCN: （旧用法）可变动数量的；不足的
senses.definition: in older use, describing an amount that is yielding or less than firm and exact
senses.definitionCN: 在旧用法中形容数量可让步或不够确定、严格
senses.example: The old manuscript counts the term as supple, as though the number of months could bend.
senses.exampleCN: 那份旧手稿把期限写得含混，仿佛月份数目也可以弯曲变动。
senses.why: A quantity that bends instead of being fixed is not exact, and the historical uses of the word for trade measures show this drifting sense.
senses.whyCN: 可弯而不固定的数量并不精确，这个词在旧时商贸尺度中的用法正体现了这种漂移的义项。

intro.en: Supple came through Old French souple from Latin supplex, which means bending down or suppliant.
intro.cn: supple 经古法语 souple 传入，源头是拉丁语 supplex，意为俯身下拜、恳求。

items.en: Supplex describes one who bends low before a superior, made of sub- under and a form related to bending.
items.cn: supplex 指在高位者面前俯身的人，由 sub-（在下）与表示弯曲的形式构成（确切构词来源不确定）。

items.en: Speakers start using supplicem for things that fold or yield, not only for people kneeling.
items.cn: 使用者开始把 supplicem 用于可折叠、可让步的东西，不再只指下跪的人。

items.en: The reconstructed form supplis is thought to shift the meaning toward pliant and flexible (a reconstruction).
items.cn: 一般认为重构形式 supplis 使词义转向「柔顺的、可弯的」（此为重构形式）。

items.en: Souple carries the sense of pliant, soft, and yielding into French.
items.cn: souple 把「柔顺、柔软、可让步」的含义带入法语。

items.en: The word enters English from French and applies to leather, limbs, and temper.
items.cn: 该词由法语进入英语，被用于皮革、肢体与脾性。

items.en: The sense extends to minds, systems, voices, and soil.
items.cn: 现代英语中词义进一步扩展到头脑、制度、嗓音与土壤。

note.en: Supple shares a bend-and-yield image with pliant, limber, and lithe, and is easy to confuse with supply and with its own noun suppleness.
note.cn: supple 与 pliant、limber、lithe 共享「弯曲、让步」的意象，也容易与 supply 以及自身的名词形式 suppleness 混淆。

entries.definition: the quality of being pliant and easily bent
entries.definitionCN: 由形容词加 -ness 构成的名词，义为柔韧性、灵活性

entries.definition: to provide what is needed
entries.definitionCN: 提供、供给；与 supple 只是拼写开头相近，词源不同（supply 来自拉丁语 supplere，supple 来自 supplex）

entries.definition: something added to complete or improve
entries.definitionCN: 增补物、补充；与「柔软」无关，只是拼写相近，词源不同（来自拉丁语 supplere）

entries.definition: easily bent or influenced
entries.definitionCN: 易弯的；易受影响的

entries.definition: able to bend and move the body easily
entries.definitionCN: 身体柔软、动作灵活的

entries.definition: thin, graceful, and moving easily
entries.definitionCN: 纤细而动作优雅灵活的

normalIntro.en: Supple pictures bending under control: the body, the leather, and the temper all give way and return.
normalIntro.cn: supple 描绘受控的弯曲：身体、皮革与脾性都能让步而后复原。

normal.en: Something supple bends without breaking.
normal.cn: supple 的东西弯曲而不断裂。

normal.en: Supple leather becomes soft after wearing.
normal.cn: supple leather 指的是越穿越软的皮革。

normal.en: A yoga teacher calls the spine supple when it bends easily.
normal.cn: 瑜伽老师把容易弯曲的脊柱称作 supple。

normal.en: A supple mind adapts quickly.
normal.cn: a supple mind 指反应快、能变通的头脑。

normal.en: The noun is suppleness, not supply, and the two must not be mixed.
normal.cn: 名词形式是 suppleness 而不是 supply，两者不能混用。

abstract.en: Picture a wet willow branch bent into a ring and springing back.
abstract.cn: 想象一根湿柳条被弯成圆环，松手后弹回原状。

abstract.en: Imagine a dancer folding and unfolding like a ribbon.
abstract.cn: 想象一位舞者像丝带一样折起又展开。

abstract.en: Think of a mind that bows to a good argument and then straightens again.
abstract.cn: 想象一个被好论据说服而低头、随后又挺直起来的头脑。

examples.en: The old leather book cover was still supple after a century.
examples.cn: 这本旧羊皮书封面过了一个世纪依然柔软。

examples.en: Pilates keeps the muscles supple and the posture upright.
examples.cn: 普拉提能让肌肉保持柔韧，让体态挺拔。

examples.en: A supple negotiation style helps when plans change suddenly.
examples.cn: 当计划突然改变时，灵活的谈判方式很有帮助。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「撒坡」——沿着撒满软土的小坡滑下去，身体软绵绵地弯着；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 supplex（俯身下拜、恳求，由 sub- 在下 + 弯曲义成分构成，确切构词来源不确定）→ 俗拉丁语重构形式 supplis → 古法语 souple → 英语 supple；核心义由「俯身」转为「可弯、柔顺」。

sensesIntro.en: Supple starts with a bending body or material, then extends to a yielding temper, an agile mind, adaptable systems, soft sounds, loose soil, and old uses for inexact amounts.
sensesIntro.cn: supple 从可弯的身体或材料出发，扩展到柔顺的脾性、敏捷的头脑、可调整的制度、柔和的嗓音、疏松的土壤，以及旧时表示数量不确的用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wet willow branch bent into an arc and springing back.
core.cn: 核心意象：湿柳条被弯成弧，松手即复原。

branches.en: Physical pliancy covers leather, skin, soil, and cloth.
branches.cn: 物理层面的柔韧覆盖皮革、皮肤、土壤与布料。

branches.en: Graceful bodily movement grows out of pliancy.
branches.cn: 优雅的肢体动作源自柔韧。

branches.en: A yielding person is pictured as a bending thing.
branches.cn: 顺从的人被想象为可弯之物。

branches.en: Flexibility of mind and systems is an abstract bending.
branches.cn: 头脑与制度的灵活是抽象的弯曲。

branches.en: Smooth sound and inexact amount both inherit the soft-yielding image.
branches.cn: 柔和的嗓音与不确的数量都继承了「柔和让步」的意象。

intro.en: Supple is a borrowing, with its own derived noun suppleness and a familiar look-alike supply that belongs to another root.
intro.cn: supple 是一则借词，自身派生名词为 suppleness，而形近的 supply 属另一词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplex means bending down or suppliant, and is built on sub- plus a component linked to bending.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 supplex 意为俯身、恳求，由 sub- 与一个与弯曲相关的成分构成。

items.example: Supplex supplies the kneeling image.
items.exampleCN: supplex 提供俯身下拜的画面。

items.example: Sub- sets the low posture of supplex.
items.exampleCN: sub- 体现 supplex 的低姿态。

items.example: Old French spreads the pliant meaning.
items.exampleCN: 古法语传播了「柔顺」的含义。

items.example: Supple keeps the physical sense.
items.exampleCN: supple 保留物理上的「易弯」义。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms suppleness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 suppleness。

items.example: Suppleness names the quality.
items.exampleCN: suppleness 表示这种性质。

items.example: The suffix -er forms suppler.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成比较级 suppler。

items.meaningCN: 表示「具有某种性质的」法语形容词词尾
items.example: The ending marks the French adjective shape.
items.exampleCN: 这一词尾保留了法语形容词的形态。

definition_zh: 补充的；增补的；附加的；（角度）互补的
definition_en: added to something else to complete it, extend it, or make it better
core_image: 一幅画旁边另挂一小幅纸片，上面补着画里没画完的一角
scene: 论文正文之后附上了补充图表。The paper ends with a set of supplementary charts.
sceneCN: 这里 supplementary 是「补充的、附加的」（第 1 个义项：为补全主体而额外添加的）；句意：论文最后附了一组补充图表。

pos.zh: 补充的；增补的；附加的
（数学，指角）互补的

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 supplementum 直接借入，作名词义为「补充物、增刊」，作动词义为「补充」
动词 supplement 加 -tion 构成，义为「补充；增补」
由形容词加 -ly 构成的副词形式，旧式拼写，义为「作为补充地」

senses.title: Added to complete something
senses.definition: added to something in order to complete it or fill a gap in it
senses.definitionCN: 为补全某物或填补其空缺而额外添加的
senses.example: The textbook has a supplementary workbook.
senses.exampleCN: 这本教科书配有一本补充练习册。
senses.why: The Latin verb supplere means to fill up what is lacking, so the adjective names what tops something up to fullness.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 supplere 意为「把缺少的填满」，因此这个形容词指把某物补足到完整状态的东西。

senses.title: Additional but not essential
senses.definition: extra and helping, but not needed for the main thing to work
senses.definitionCN: 额外的、起辅助作用的，但主体离开它也能运转
senses.example: Use the supplementary notes only if you want more detail.
senses.exampleCN: 只有想了解细节时才需要看附加注释。
senses.why: If the original can stand alone, anything added to it is by definition secondary, so completing turns into mere extra.
senses.whyCN: 既然主体本身能独立成立，加在它上面的东西自然就是次要的，「补全」由此转为「多余附加」。

senses.title: Provided in a separate list
senses.titleCN: （文件、试卷等）附加的；另行提供的
senses.definition: given on a separate sheet, list, or schedule that goes with the main document
senses.definitionCN: 写在单独的一页、清单或附表上，与主文件配套提供
senses.example: Supplementary questions are printed on the back page.
senses.exampleCN: 附加题印在试卷的背面。
senses.why: The added part is physically put elsewhere and attached, so the word comes to describe separate pages and schedules.
senses.whyCN: 补加的部分被放在别处再附上来，这个词于是用来形容独立的页面与附表。

senses.title: Extra payment for the same work
senses.definition: describing an added charge, allowance, or payment that tops up a standard amount
senses.definitionCN: 形容为补足标准额度而追加的收费、津贴或款项
senses.example: The council raised a supplementary charge for large bins.
senses.exampleCN: 市政委员会对大号垃圾桶加收了补充费用。
senses.why: Money added to fill a shortfall is the same filling image in a financial setting.
senses.whyCN: 为填补缺额而加的钱是同一「填满」意象在财务场景中的体现。

senses.title: Two angles that make a straight line
senses.definition: in geometry, describing an angle that completes another to a total of one hundred and eighty degrees
senses.definitionCN: 在几何中，形容一个角与另一个角相加恰好等于一百八十度
senses.example: The two angles shown are supplementary.
senses.exampleCN: 图中所示的两个角互补。
senses.why: Geometry takes the completing idea literally: one angle fills up exactly what the other lacks up to a straight line.
senses.whyCN: 几何学把这个「补全」的概念照字面使用：一个角恰好填满另一个角到成一条直线所缺的量。

senses.title: Explaining further
senses.titleCN: 补充说明的；辅助解释的
senses.definition: describing remarks, evidence, or material that adds further explanation rather than replacing the main account
senses.definitionCN: 形容补充进一步解释的话、证据或材料，而不是取代主要叙述
senses.example: Her supplementary remarks clarified the last paragraph.
senses.exampleCN: 她补充的几句话把最后一段解释清楚了。
senses.why: Explaining more is adding what the listener still lacks, the same filling action in the field of speech.
senses.whyCN: 多说一些就是添上听者仍缺少的信息，这是「填满」在言语领域的同一动作。

senses.title: Secondary in status
senses.definition: describing a role, task, or source that supports a main one but ranks below it
senses.definitionCN: 形容起辅助作用但地位低于主体的功能、任务或来源
senses.example: A dictionary is a supplementary source, not the primary one.
senses.exampleCN: 词典是辅助来源，而不是第一手来源。
senses.why: Once something is only the add-on, it is also subordinate, so the adjective carries a ranking as well as a filling image.
senses.whyCN: 一样东西一旦只是外加的，地位也就随之为下，所以这个形容词既含「填满」意象又含等级意味。

senses.title: Used for making up a deficiency
senses.titleCN: （正式）补缺的；用于弥补不足的
senses.definition: in formal or legal use, describing an action or rule that makes up for a lack or a missing step
senses.definitionCN: 在正式或法律用法中，形容弥补缺漏或缺失步骤的行为、规则
senses.example: The court applied supplementary rules to recover the cost.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭适用了补缺规则来追回费用。
senses.why: Law and administration turn to the word when something is missing and has to be filled in by a further measure.
senses.whyCN: 法律与行政在有所缺失、必须用另一措施填补时才用这个词。

intro.en: Supplementary comes from Late Latin supplementum, something that fills up a gap, built on supplere and used by the church for a part of the prayer book.
intro.cn: supplementary 来自晚期拉丁语 supplementum（用来填满空缺之物），由 supplere 构成，教会曾用它指祈祷书中的附加部分。

items.en: Suppleo means to make full or fill up, formed from sub- and a root related to plenus, full.
items.cn: suppleo 意为「补满、填满」，由 sub- 与和 plenus（充满的）相关的词根构成。

items.en: Supplementum names something that fills a gap or completes a whole.
items.cn: supplementum 指填补空缺、补全整体的东西。

items.en: The church uses supplementum for extra parts of the service book.
items.cn: 中世纪教会用 supplementum 指礼拜书中的附加部分。

items.en: The noun supplement enters English first, and the adjective follows it.
items.cn: 名词 supplement 先进入英语，形容词随后出现。

items.en: Rival endings -al and -ary both appear, and -ary wins in the adjective.
items.cn: 17 世纪时 -al 与 -ary 两种词尾并存，最终 -ary 在形容词中胜出。

items.en: The word spreads to schools, budgets, geometry, and publishing.
items.cn: 现代英语中该词扩展到学校、预算、几何与出版领域。

note.en: Supplementary is the adjective of supplement, and it is easily confused with complementary, whose extra part is not a gap filler but a beautifying partner.
note.cn: supplementary 是 supplement 的形容词形式，也容易与 complementary 混淆：后者的「添」不是补缺，而是相得益彰的搭配。

entries.definition: something added to complete or improve something else
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「补充物」，动词义为「补充」；是本词条的基础词

entries.definition: combining well in a way that makes each better
entries.definitionCN: 互补的、相得益彰的；与 supplementary 拼写相近，前缀不同，词源不同（complementum 来自 complere）

entries.definition: an alternative adjective form of the same noun
entries.definitionCN: 同源词：同一名词的另一种形容词形式，用法与 supplementary 基本相同

entries.definition: extra, more than was already there
entries.definitionCN: 额外的、附加的

entries.definition: more than the usual or needed amount
entries.definitionCN: 额外的；另外的

entries.definition: giving help or support to a main body
entries.definitionCN: 辅助的、备用的

normalIntro.en: Supplementary keeps the Latin filling image: it names what is added to fill a gap, then drifts to mere extra and to geometry.
normalIntro.cn: supplementary 保留拉丁语「填满」的意象：指为填补空缺而添加之物，之后又滑向「纯粹额外」与几何用法。

normal.en: Supplementary material comes in addition to the main text.
normal.cn: supplementary material 指正文之外另附的材料。

normal.en: A supplementary exam lets a student resit a failed paper.
normal.cn: supplementary exam 即补考，让考砸的学生再考一次。

normal.en: Supplementary is the adjective, supplement is the noun or verb.
normal.cn: supplementary 是形容词，supplement 是名词或动词。

normal.en: Two supplementary angles add up to a straight line.
normal.cn: 两个 supplementary angles 相加正好成一条直线，即补角。

normal.en: Compare complementary: complementary means fitting well together, not filling a gap.
normal.cn: 对比 complementary：它指「搭配相得益彰」，而不是「填补空缺」。

abstract.en: Picture a loose page pinned beside a finished painting to fill the missing corner.
abstract.cn: 想象在画完的画旁钉上一张纸片，补上缺掉的那一角。

abstract.en: Imagine a cup of water topped up precisely to the brim.
abstract.cn: 想象一杯水被精确地添到杯口。

abstract.en: Think of two angles leaning together until their edges form one straight line.
abstract.cn: 想象两个角彼此倚靠，直到两条边连成一条直线。

examples.en: The ministry issued a supplementary budget after the floods.
examples.cn: 洪水过后，该部委发布了追加预算。

examples.en: Supplementary exercises are posted online each Friday.
examples.cn: 补充练习每周五在网上发布。

examples.en: If one angle is fifty degrees, its partner must be a hundred and thirty to be supplementary.
examples.cn: 若一个角是五十度，要使两者互补，另一个角就必须是一百三十度。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「撒普力门特瑞」——把东西「撒」在普力门前，再一点点往里填；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 supplere（补满，sub- + plenus 充满相关词根）→ supplementum（填补空缺之物；附加部分）→ supplement（名词）→ supplement + -ary → supplementary；核心义「把缺的填上」。

sensesIntro.en: Supplementary begins with filling a gap, then spreads to optional extras, separate sheets, added money, completing angles, extra explanation, lowered rank, and legal make-up rules.
sensesIntro.cn: supplementary 从「填补空缺」出发，扩展到可选的额外内容、另附的单页、追加的款项、互补的角、补充的解释、较低的等级地位以及法律的补缺规则。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small page pinned beside a finished picture to fill its missing corner.
core.cn: 核心意象：在已完成的画旁钉一张小纸片，补上缺掉的一角。

branches.en: Filling a gap in content or explanation is the core sense.
branches.cn: 填补内容或解释上的缺漏是核心义项。

branches.en: What is merely added also ranks lower than the main thing.
branches.cn: 仅属外加的东西地位也低于主体。

branches.en: Separate sheets and attached pages are the physical setting.
branches.cn: 独立单页与附表是这一义项的物理场景。

branches.en: Money that tops up a shortfall is the financial setting.
branches.cn: 补足缺额的款项是财务场景中的用法。

branches.en: Geometry and law take the completing idea in technical form.
branches.cn: 几何与法律把「补全」的概念用作技术术语。

intro.en: Supplementary is the adjective of the Latin loan supplement, and the suffix -ary turns the noun into a describing word beside a competing -al form.
intro.cn: supplementary 是拉丁语借词 supplement 的形容词形式，-ary 后缀把名词变为描写词，另有一个竞争的 -al 形式并存。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplere means to fill up, from sub- (from below, in addition) plus a root tied to plenus, full.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 supplere 意为补满，由 sub-（从下面、补充）加上与 plenus（满的）相关的词根构成。

items.example: Suppleo supplies the image of topping up.
items.exampleCN: suppleo 提供「添满」的意象。

items.example: Sub- marks the additive movement.
items.exampleCN: sub- 表示「另外添加」的方向。

items.example: Plenus lies behind the completing sense.
items.exampleCN: plenus 是「补全」义的来源。

items.example: Supplementum is the direct source.
items.exampleCN: supplementum 是直接来源。

items.meaningCN: 表示结果或事物的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ment forms supplement.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ment 构成 supplement。

items.example: The suffix -ary forms supplementary.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ary 构成 supplementary。

items.example: The suffix -al gives the rival form supplemental.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -al 给出并存的另一形式 supplemental。

items.meaningCN: 动作或过程的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -tion forms supplementation.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -tion 构成 supplementation。

items.meaningCN: 以某种方式的副词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ly forms supplementally.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 supplementally。

definition_zh: 支持的；给予鼓励的；起支撑作用的
definition_en: giving help, encouragement, or physical strength to someone or something
core_image: 一只手从下方托住快要倒塌的墙，同时朝墙后的人点头鼓劲
scene: 父母总是鼓励她追逐自己的梦想。Her parents were always supportive of her dreams.
sceneCN: 这里 supportive 是「给予支持的、鼓励的」（第 1 个义项：在情感上鼓励并愿意帮忙）；句意：她的父母一直支持她追逐梦想。

pos.zh: 支持的；鼓励的；给予帮助的
起支撑作用的；有支撑力的

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 supportare 经古法语进入英语的基础词，名词义为「支持、支撑」，动词义为「支撑、支持」
动词加 -er 构成，义为「支持者、拥护者」
形容词加 -ness 构成，义为「支持性；乐于支持的态度」

senses.title: Giving emotional encouragement
senses.definition: giving someone help, encouragement, or approval so that they feel able to continue
senses.definitionCN: 在情感上给予对方帮助、鼓励或认可，使其有信心继续下去
senses.example: Her friends were supportive during the difficult year.
senses.exampleCN: 在艰难的那一年里，朋友们一直支持她。
senses.why: The Latin verb supportare means to carry from below, and emotional help carries a person when they cannot carry themselves.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 supportare 意为「从下面托起承载」，情感上的帮助正是在人撑不住时从下面托着他。

senses.title: Approving of a plan or cause
senses.definition: showing agreement with an idea, plan, or cause and willing to back it
senses.definitionCN: 表示赞同某种观念、计划或事业，并愿意声援
senses.example: The board was supportive of the merger.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会支持这项并购。
senses.why: Agreement turns the physical back-up into a public stance, so to be supportive is to stand behind a proposal.
senses.whyCN: 赞同把身体上的「支撑」变成公开立场，「支持」就是站在提案背后。

senses.title: Providing practical help
senses.titleCN: 给予实际帮助的；起支撑作用的（作用层面）
senses.definition: actively giving resources, time, or effort that help another person or body to function
senses.definitionCN: 主动提供资源、时间或努力，帮助他人或机构正常运转
senses.example: The role is supportive rather than leading.
senses.exampleCN: 这个角色起辅助作用，而不是主导作用。
senses.why: Carrying from below means doing the work that keeps the higher part upright, hence practical help rather than talk.
senses.whyCN: 从下面托举就是要做让上方保持直立的工作，因此是实打实的帮衬而非空话。

senses.title: Holding something up physically
senses.titleCN: （实物）起支撑作用的；有支撑力的
senses.definition: describing a structure, bandage, or frame that holds another part up or keeps it in place
senses.definitionCN: 形容结构、绷带或框架托住另一部分或使其固定
senses.example: The doctor wrapped a supportive bandage around the ankle.
senses.exampleCN: 医生在脚踝处缠上了起支撑作用的绷带。
senses.why: This is the literal reach of the word: something under a weight, taking the strain so the thing above does not fall.
senses.whyCN: 这是字面义：承重之物在下方分担压力，使上方之物不倒。

senses.title: Helping someone adjust
senses.titleCN: （教育、医疗）支持性的；援助性的
senses.definition: describing teaching, therapy, or care that helps people cope and adjust rather than cure or test them
senses.definitionCN: 形容帮助人们适应与应对的辅导、治疗或照护，而不是治病或考核
senses.example: She attends a supportive group for new mothers.
senses.exampleCN: 她参加一个面向新手妈妈的支持小组。
senses.why: When the aim is not to fix but to hold someone steady, the caring profession borrows the carrying image.
senses.whyCN: 当目的不是「修好」而是「让人稳住」，关怀行业就借用了这个托举意象。

senses.title: Strengthening a claim
senses.definition: describing evidence or findings that back up and strengthen an argument or hypothesis
senses.definitionCN: 形容为某一论证或假设提供依据、加以增强的证据或研究结果
senses.example: The study offers supportive evidence for the theory.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究为该理论提供了支持性证据。
senses.why: An argument left on its own may fall, and evidence underneath holds it up, the same load-bearing picture applied to reasoning.
senses.whyCN: 论证孤立时可能坍塌，底下的证据把它托住，这是承重画面在推理上的应用。

senses.title: Warm and welcoming in style
senses.definition: describing an atmosphere or manner that is warm, respectful, and welcoming
senses.definitionCN: 形容氛围或态度温暖、尊重、让人感到被接纳
senses.example: The staff created a supportive atmosphere in the clinic.
senses.exampleCN: 医护人员在诊室里营造出体贴友好的氛围。
senses.why: A supportive place is one that lifts people gently out of discomfort, so the word also marks tone and mood.
senses.whyCN: 一个 supportive 的地方能温和地托起人的不适感，因此这个词也形容语气与氛围。

senses.title: Keeping prices or values firm
senses.titleCN: （经济）支撑性的；起托底作用的
senses.definition: in economics, describing a price, value, or policy that holds a level up or prevents a fall
senses.definitionCN: 在经济学中形容托住某一价位或政策水平、防止其下跌
senses.example: A supportive policy kept the small farms alive.
senses.exampleCN: 一项托底政策让小农场得以存活。
senses.why: Markets have levels that fall when nothing holds them up, so the carrying image is used for prices kept from dropping.
senses.whyCN: 市场价位无人托住便会下跌，因此托盘意象被用于防止下跌的价格。

intro.en: Supportive is built on support, a verb carried from Old French into English from Latin supportare, to bring up from below.
intro.cn: supportive 建立在 support 之上，而 support 由古法语传入英语，源自拉丁语 supportare，意为「从下面托上来」。

items.en: Supportare means to carry or bring up from below, from sub- under and portare to carry.
items.cn: supportare 意为从下面托起、承载，由 sub-（在下）与 portare（搬运）构成。

items.en: The vulgar form supportare keeps the physical carrying sense.
items.cn: 俗拉丁语形式 supportare 保留物理上的承载义。

items.en: Supporter means to hold up, carry, or bear.
items.cn: 古法语 supporter 意为托起、承载、忍受。

items.en: The verb support enters English in the thirteenth and fourteenth centuries.
items.cn: 动词 support 在十三至十四世纪进入英语。

items.en: The adjective supportive is added later and spreads to moods, policies, and care.
items.cn: 形容词 supportive 出现较晚，随后扩展到情绪、政策与照护领域。

note.en: Supportive shares the carry-from-below root with support, supporter, and supportiveness, and sits beside encouraging and helpful in meaning.
note.cn: supportive 与 support、supporter、supportiveness 共享「从下面托起」的词根，在意义上又和 encouraging、helpful 相邻。

entries.definition: to hold up, bear, or give help
entries.definitionCN: 支撑、承载；支持；是本词条的基础词

entries.definition: a person who backs a person, team, or cause
entries.definitionCN: 支持者、拥护者；由动词加 -er 构成

entries.definition: the quality of giving support
entries.definitionCN: 支持性、乐于支持的态度；由形容词加 -ness 构成

entries.definition: giving someone confidence and hope
entries.definitionCN: 令人鼓舞的；给予信心的

entries.definition: giving practical help
entries.definitionCN: 有帮助的；实用的

entries.definition: showing that you understand and care about another troubled person
entries.definitionCN: 同情的；体贴理解的

normalIntro.en: Supportive is a hand under a weight: it carries, it encourages, and it keeps a claim, a price, or a bandage in place.
normalIntro.cn: supportive 是一只托在重物下方的手：既承载、又鼓劲，还能托住论点、价格或绷带。

normal.en: To be supportive of someone is to stand behind them.
normal.cn: be supportive of someone 就是站在某人身后撑着他。

normal.en: A supportive family helps a student keep going.
normal.cn: a supportive family 让一个学生能坚持下去。

normal.en: Supportive comes from support plus the suffix -ive.
normal.cn: supportive 由 support 加后缀 -ive 构成。

normal.en: Supportive evidence backs up an argument.
normal.cn: supportive evidence 指为论点撑腰的证据。

normal.en: Compare supportive with supportable: the second means able to be endured.
normal.cn: 对比 supportive 与 supportable：后者意思是「可忍受的」。

abstract.en: Picture a hand under a sagging wall and a nod to the person behind it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手托住下陷的墙，同时向墙后的人点头鼓劲。

abstract.en: Imagine a friend walking beside you with a steady palm on your back.
abstract.cn: 想象一个朋友走在你身旁，手掌稳稳搭在你背上。

abstract.en: Think of a pole propping up a young tree until it stands on its own.
abstract.cn: 想象一根木桩撑着小树，直到它能独立站稳。

examples.en: A supportive colleague can turn a bad week into a bearable one.
examples.cn: 一位支持你的同事能把糟糕的一周变得可以忍受。

examples.en: The scheme was designed to be supportive of small businesses.
examples.cn: 该计划旨在支持小企业。

examples.en: He wore a supportive brace for six weeks after the injury.
examples.cn: 受伤之后，他穿戴了六周的支撑护具。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑟波特福」——在瑟瑟的风里，是朋友「波」动的手把你「托」住；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 sub-（在下）+ portare（搬运）→ supportare（从下面托起）→ 俗拉丁语 → 古法语 supporter → 英语 support → support + -ive → supportive；核心义「在下面托住」。

sensesIntro.en: Supportive begins with physical carrying, then grows into emotional encouragement, approval, practical help, medical and educational care, evidence that backs a claim, a caring atmosphere, and prices held up.
sensesIntro.cn: supportive 从物理上的托举出发，发展为情感鼓励、认同支持、实际帮助、医护与教育中的援助性照护、为论点撑腰的证据、体贴的氛围以及被托住的价位。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand under a tilting wall, steadying it and cheering the person behind.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手托住倾斜的墙，同时为墙后的人鼓劲。

branches.en: Emotional encouragement and warm tone are the human centre.
branches.cn: 情感鼓励与温和氛围是这一义项的人情中心。

branches.en: Approving a plan and backing a claim are public stances.
branches.cn: 赞同计划与为论点撑腰都是公开立场。

branches.en: Practical help and professional care make the help concrete.
branches.cn: 实际帮助与专业照护让「支持」落到实处。

branches.en: The literal sense stays in physical props and bandages.
branches.cn: 字面义保留在实物支撑与绷带上。

branches.en: Economies also need prices that are held from below.
branches.cn: 经济中同样需要从下方托住的价位。

intro.en: Supportive is support plus the adjective suffix -ive, with a family built on the Latin verb supportare.
intro.cn: supportive 是 support 加形容词后缀 -ive 构成，词族以拉丁语动词 supportare 为基底。

latinIntro.en: Latin supportare joins sub- (under) and portare (to carry), giving the image of carrying from below.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 supportare 把 sub-（在下）与 portare（搬运）结合，构成「从下面承载」的意象。

items.example: Portare supplies the carrying image.
items.exampleCN: portare 提供承载的意象。

items.example: Sub- keeps the support underneath.
items.exampleCN: sub- 表明支撑的东西在下方。

items.meaning: to bring up from below, hold up
items.example: Supportare is the remote source.
items.exampleCN: supportare 是远源。

items.example: French carries the verb into English.
items.exampleCN: 法语把这个动词带入英语。

items.example: Support keeps both the physical and the social sense.
items.exampleCN: support 兼有物理与社会两重含义。

items.example: The suffix -er forms supporter.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 supporter。

items.meaningCN: 表示「倾向于……的」形容词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ive forms supportive.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ive 构成 supportive。

items.meaningCN: 表示「以某种方式」的副词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ly forms supportively.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 supportively。

items.meaningCN: 表示性质、状态的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ness forms supportiveness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 supportiveness。

definition_zh: 镇压；（情感或反应的）抑制；压制；抑制；（病症的）控制；（激素分泌的）抑制
definition_en: the act of stopping something from continuing, being shown, or developing, especially by force or willpower
core_image: 一只手掌从上方把一股正向上冒的东西硬生生按下去
scene: 抗议的人群冲上广场，当局立刻出动警力把这场运动按了下去。The government used emergency powers to secure the suppression of the protest.
sceneCN: 这里 suppression 是「镇压」（第 1 个义项：用强力制止群体行动）；句意：政府动用紧急权力确保这场抗议被镇压下去。

pos.zh: 镇压；抑制；压制；抑制（生理）；控制

derivatives.zh: 压制；抑制；压抑；由拉丁语 sub（在下）与 premere（压）构成的核心动词
压制性的；抑制性的，动词加 -ive 构成
抑制器；抑制基因，动词加施事后缀 -or 构成
抑制剂（如止咳药），动词加 -ant 构成

senses.title: The forcible crushing of a movement
senses.definition: the use of force by an authority to put an end to a protest, revolt, or organized group
senses.definitionCN: 当局动用强力制止抗议、叛乱或有组织的群体
senses.example: Border guards were accused of the brutal suppression of the march.
senses.exampleCN: 边防人员被指粗暴镇压了这场游行。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to press down from below, so an authority pushing a rising crowd back down gives the political sense.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词本义是「从下方压住」，当局把向上涌起的人群压回去，就生出了政治上的镇压义。

senses.title: The holding down of a feeling
senses.definition: the deliberate keeping of an emotion, impulse, or reaction under control or hidden
senses.definitionCN: 有意把情绪、冲动或反应控制住或隐藏起来
senses.example: Years of emotional suppression left him unable to cry at the funeral.
senses.exampleCN: 多年的情绪压抑使他在葬礼上哭不出来。
senses.why: A feeling rises like pressure, and the person presses it back down, so the same downward pressure turns inward.
senses.whyCN: 情绪像压力一样往上升，当事人把它按回去，于是同一个「向下压」的动作转向了内心。

senses.title: The keeping back of information
senses.definition: the keeping of facts, evidence, or news from being known or published
senses.definitionCN: 不让他人知道或发表事实、证据与消息
senses.example: The court ordered the suppression of the witnesses names.
senses.exampleCN: 法院下令不得公开证人的姓名。
senses.why: Information wants to spread outward, and suppression presses it back inside the holders hands.
senses.whyCN: 信息本要向外传播，suppression 却把它按回持有者手里。

senses.title: The restraint of a symptom or process
senses.definition: the stopping or slowing of a disease, growth, fire, or other process
senses.definitionCN: 使疾病、生长、火势等过程停止或减慢
senses.example: Early suppression of the fire kept the whole forest from burning.
senses.exampleCN: 及早遏制火势使整片森林免于烧毁。
senses.why: Medical and technical usage keeps the literal image, since a germ, a flame, or a weed is physically held down.
senses.whyCN: 医学与技术用法保留字面意象，因为病菌、火焰、杂草确实是被压住的。

senses.title: The blocking of an immune or nervous response
senses.definition: the medical reduction of the activity of the immune system or of a nerve signal
senses.definitionCN: 医学上降低免疫系统活动或阻断神经冲动的过程
senses.example: Doctors induced immune suppression before the transplant.
senses.exampleCN: 移植手术前医生诱导了免疫抑制。
senses.why: Here the body presses down on its own defences, so the term names a controlled, deliberate quieting of activity.
senses.whyCN: 这里身体对自己的防御系统「向下压」，于是这个词指一种受控而刻意的活动抑制。

senses.title: The holding back of a body fluid
senses.definition: the withholding of urine, tears, or another body fluid
senses.definitionCN: 抑制尿液、眼泪等体液的排出
senses.example: The report described a suppression of urine over the past day.
senses.exampleCN: 报告记录了患者过去一天的尿潴留。
senses.why: The oldest concrete layer survives in medicine, where the body holds back what should flow out.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的具象层次在医学用法中留存下来，指身体憋住本该排出的东西。

intro.en: Suppression comes from Latin suppressio, a pressing down, from sub, under, and premere, to press.
intro.cn: suppression 来自拉丁语 suppressio（向下压），由 sub（在下）与 premere（压）构成。

items.en: Premere means to press, squeeze, or push hard.
items.cn: premere 意为压、挤、用力推。

items.en: Supprimere means to press down or press under.
items.cn: supprimere 意为向下压、压到下面。

items.en: Suppressio names the act of pressing something down.
items.cn: suppressio 指把某物压下去的动作。

items.en: The word first appears in English medical and legal writing.
items.cn: 该词最早出现在英语的医学与法律文字中。

items.en: Political usage extends it to the crushing of revolts and of publications.
items.cn: 政治用法把它扩展到对叛乱与出版物的镇压。

items.en: Psychology and medicine add the suppression of feelings and of the immune response.
items.cn: 心理学与医学又加上了对情绪和免疫反应的抑制义。

note.en: Suppression shares the pressing root of suppress, and its near neighbours are repression, oppression, and censorship.
note.cn: suppression 与 suppress 共享「下压」词根，近义词有 repression、oppression 与 censorship。

entries.definition: to stop something by force or willpower
entries.definitionCN: 压制；抑制

entries.definition: acting to hold something down
entries.definitionCN: 抑制性的；压制性的

entries.definition: a device or gene that blocks an activity
entries.definitionCN: 抑制器；抑制基因

entries.definition: the use of force or pressure to control people, often with a psychological sense
entries.definitionCN: 压制；压抑，常带心理学色彩

entries.definition: cruel and unjust treatment by those in power
entries.definitionCN: 压迫；暴政

entries.definition: the official removal of content from media
entries.definitionCN: 审查制度

normalIntro.en: Suppression is a pressing down: the prefix sub supplies the downward motion and the root premere supplies the press.
normalIntro.cn: suppression 就是一次「下压」：前缀 sub 给出向下的方向，词根 premere 给出「压」的动作。

normal.en: Sub means under and premere means to press, so suppression is pressing under.
normal.cn: sub 表示在下，premere 表示压，所以 suppression 就是把东西压到下面。

normal.en: The verb suppress gives the noun suppression, and it keeps the doubled p.
normal.cn: 动词 suppress 变成名词 suppression 时要保留双写的 p。

normal.en: Immune suppression uses the same word for the body pressing down its own defences.
normal.cn: immune suppression 用同一个词表示身体压下自己的防御。

normal.en: Suppress the urge to spoil the answer: suppression is the act that follows.
normal.cn: suppress the urge 表示压下冲动，suppression 就是这一压制动作的名称。

normal.en: Compare repression: repression is often unconscious, suppression is usually deliberate.
normal.cn: 对比 repression：repression 多指无意识的压抑，suppression 多指有意的克制。

abstract.en: Picture a palm flattening a column of smoke back onto the ground.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手掌把一股往上冒的烟硬压回地面。

abstract.en: Imagine a hand on a chest that will not let a sobbing breath escape.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手按在胸口，不肯让一声呜咽漏出来。

abstract.en: Think of a folder stamped confidential and locked in a drawer.
abstract.cn: 想象一份盖着机密的文件夹被锁进抽屉里。

examples.en: The regime was condemned for the suppression of peaceful dissent.
examples.cn: 该政权因镇压和平异见而受到谴责。

examples.en: Suppression of the infection at an early stage saved her eyesight.
examples.cn: 在早期抑制感染保住了她的视力。

examples.en: Long and hard suppression of grief made the news hit him all the harder.
examples.cn: 长久而勉强的悲伤压抑让这个消息对他打击更大。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「下压」——suppress 听起来像「摁住」，把往上冒的东西一把摁下去，记住压制的画面；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 sub-（在下）+ premere（压）→ supprimere（向下压）→ suppressio → 古法语 suppression → 英语 suppression，核心义「从上方压下去」。

sensesIntro.en: Suppression starts with an authority pressing a rising crowd down, then turns inward to feelings, then to information, and finally to symptoms and body processes held back.
sensesIntro.cn: suppression 先从当局把涌起的人群压下去讲起，再转向内心情绪的压抑，然后是信息的隐瞒，最后是症状与身体过程的抑制。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pressing a rising column down flat.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把向上冒起的一股东西按平。

branches.en: Political force is the public sense.
branches.cn: 政治强力是公共层面的义项。

branches.en: Inner restraint is the personal sense.
branches.cn: 内心克制是个人层面的义项。

branches.en: Hiding facts is the legal and journalistic sense.
branches.cn: 隐匿事实是法律与新闻层面的义项。

branches.en: Medicine uses the same image for symptoms, immune response, and body fluids.
branches.cn: 医学用同一意象表示症状、免疫反应与体液滞留。

branches.en: All three involve an agent with power holding something back or down.
branches.cn: 三者都涉及一个有力量的主体把某物按住或藏起。

intro.en: Suppression is built from the Latin prefix sub, the root premere, and the noun ending -ion.
intro.cn: suppression 由拉丁语前缀 sub、词根 premere 与名词词尾 -ion 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin supprimere means to press down, made of sub, under, and premere, to press.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 supprimere 意为向下压，由 sub（在下）与 premere（压）构成。

items.example: The prefix sub- becomes sup- before p.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 sub- 在 p 前写作 sup-。

items.example: Premere supplies the pressing image.
items.exampleCN: premere 提供「压」的意象。

items.meaning: to press down, to hold back
items.example: Supprimere joins the prefix to the pressing root.
items.exampleCN: supprimere 把前缀与「压」的词根连在一起。

items.example: Suppressio is the noun form of the verb.
items.exampleCN: suppressio 是动词的名词形式。

items.meaning: to put an end to something by force
items.example: Suppress carries the verb sense into English.
items.exampleCN: suppress 把动词义带入英语。

items.meaning: the act or process of doing something
items.meaningCN: 表示动作或过程的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ion turns suppress into suppression.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ion 把 suppress 变成 suppression。

items.meaning: having the nature of doing something
items.meaningCN: 表示具有某种作用的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ive forms suppressive.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ive 构成 suppressive。

items.meaning: a thing or person that acts
items.meaningCN: 表示施事者或器具的词尾
items.example: The suffix -or forms suppressor.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -or 构成 suppressor。

items.meaning: a thing that performs an action
items.meaningCN: 表示起某种作用的物的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ant forms suppressant.

definition_zh: 冲浪；乘浪；浪花；冲浪运动；（在网上）浏览；冲浪
definition_en: to ride on waves on a board, or to move from page to page on the internet without a fixed goal
core_image: 一个人站在冲浪板上，顺着浪头滑向岸边
scene: 天刚亮，海面涌起整齐的长浪，年轻人抱着板子跑向浪区。At dawn the boys grab their boards and surf until the tide turns.
sceneCN: 这里 surf 是「冲浪」（第 1 个义项：站在冲浪板上乘浪滑行）；句意：天刚亮男孩们抓起冲浪板一直冲到潮水转向。

pos.zh: 冲浪；在网上浏览
浪花；拍岸浪；冲浪运动

冲浪运动；网上浏览，动名词转化而来的名词
冲浪板，surf 与 board 复合而成

senses.title: To ride on waves with a board
senses.definition: to stand or lie on a board and move along the face of a breaking wave
senses.definitionCN: 站在或趴在冲浪板上，顺着碎浪的斜面滑行
senses.example: They surf every morning before the wind gets up.
senses.exampleCN: 他们每天早晨在起风之前冲浪。
senses.why: The word comes from the breaking waves of the Indian Ocean coast, and the verb names riding that moving water.
senses.whyCN: 这个词源自印度洋海岸的拍岸浪，动词义就是乘着这种流动的水滑行。

senses.title: The broken water of a shoreline
senses.definition: the mass of white water that breaks against the shore or a reef
senses.definitionCN: 拍打在岸边或礁石上散开的白色浪花
senses.example: The surf was too heavy for small boats to launch.
senses.exampleCN: 浪花太大，小船无法下水。
senses.why: The oldest noun sense names the white breaker itself, before any sport existed.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的名词义就指白色的拍岸浪本身，那时还没有冲浪运动。

senses.title: The sport of riding waves
senses.definition: the sport or activity of riding breaking waves on a board
senses.definitionCN: 用冲浪板乘碎浪滑行的运动或活动
senses.example: Surfing became an Olympic sport long after it spread from Hawaii.
senses.exampleCN: 冲浪从夏威夷传开很久之后才成为奥运项目。
senses.why: Once a whole culture formed around the board, the activity grew into a named sport with its own competitions.
senses.whyCN: 当冲浪板周围形成一整套文化之后，这项活动就成长为一个有名有赛事的运动项目。

senses.title: To move through pages online
senses.definition: to move from one web page or television channel to another without a fixed goal
senses.definitionCN: 没有明确目标地在网页或电视频道之间来回浏览
senses.example: She surfs the net for recipes whenever she is bored.
senses.exampleCN: 她一觉得无聊就上网找菜谱。
senses.why: Moving from link to link feels like gliding on an unknown wave, so the surfing image was borrowed for the internet.
senses.whyCN: 从一个链接划到另一个链接，感觉像在未知的浪上滑行，于是冲浪的意象被借用到互联网上。

senses.title: To ride on something moving fast
senses.definition: to ride or be carried along by something that is moving, such as a crowd or a wave of change
senses.definitionCN: 被移动中的事物带着向前，如人群或变化的浪潮
senses.example: Small shops are trying to surf the wave of online sales.
senses.exampleCN: 小店铺正努力乘上网络销售的浪潮。
senses.why: The physical image of balancing on a moving surface extends to any rise and fall a person can ride.
senses.whyCN: 在移动的表面上保持平衡这一实感，扩展到任何可随其起伏的事物上。

intro.en: Surf is generally traced to the waves of the Indian coast, later carried by sailors and settlers to Hawaii and beyond.
intro.cn: surf 一般认为源出印度海岸的拍岸浪，后来经水手与移民传到夏威夷等地。

items.en: The word is generally linked to Portuguese or a coastal Indian language, but no form is certain.
items.cn: 这个词一般被认为与葡萄牙语或印度沿海某语言有关，但具体词形尚不确定。

items.en: Sailors use surf for the white broken water near the Indian shore.
items.cn: 水手用 surf 称呼印度海岸附近破碎的白色浪花。

items.en: The noun spreads in whaling and trading speech along the Pacific.
items.cn: 这个名词随捕鲸与贸易用语在太平洋沿岸流传开来。

items.en: Hawaiian practice gives the English verb surf, to ride waves on a board.
items.cn: 夏威夷的传统带来英语动词 surf，意为用冲浪板乘浪。

items.en: Surfing grows into a global sport and youth culture.
items.cn: 冲浪成长为全球性运动与青年文化。

items.en: Since the nineties the verb also means to browse the internet.
items.cn: 自上世纪九十年代以来，这个动词也指上网浏览。

note.en: Surf is the water word behind the surfer family, and its near neighbours are wave, swell, and breaker.
note.cn: surf 是 surfer 这一词族背后的「水」词，近义词有 wave、swell 与 breaker。

entries.definition: a person who rides waves on a board
entries.definitionCN: 冲浪者；上网者

entries.definition: the sport of riding waves or of browsing online
entries.definitionCN: 冲浪运动；网上浏览

entries.definition: a long board used for riding waves
entries.definitionCN: 冲浪板

entries.definition: a raised line of water moving across the sea
entries.definitionCN: 波浪；海浪

entries.definition: a wave that turns white and falls near the shore
entries.definitionCN: 碎浪；拍岸浪

entries.definition: a long slow wave rolling across open water
entries.definitionCN: 涌浪；长浪

normalIntro.en: Surf is the white water at the coast, and the board and the browser both borrow its rolling motion.
normalIntro.cn: surf 是海岸边翻白的浪，冲浪板和浏览器都借用了它起伏滑行的动感。

normal.en: Surf plus -er makes surfer, the person who rides the water.
normal.cn: surf 加 -er 就是 surfer，在水上滑行的人。

normal.en: The past tense surfed doubles no letters and keeps the final f.
normal.cn: 过去式 surfed 不加倍写字母，结尾的 f 保留。

normal.en: Surf the net borrows the wave image for the movement between links.
normal.cn: surf the net 借用浪的意象来比喻在链接之间移动。

normal.en: A surfboard is simply a board for the surf, a plain compound.
normal.cn: surfboard 就是用于冲浪浪花的板子，是直白的复合词。

normal.en: Compare wave: a wave is any swell, while surf is the broken white water at the shore.
normal.cn: 对比 wave：wave 泛指波浪，surf 特指岸边破碎翻白的浪。

abstract.en: Picture a rider leaning into the curl of a blue wall of water.
abstract.cn: 想象冲浪者倾身贴着蓝色水墙的卷浪。

abstract.en: Hear the hiss of white foam sliding back over pebbles.
abstract.cn: 听白色泡沫从碎石上退回去时的沙沙声。

abstract.en: Imagine a click leading to another page, like a board sliding to the next wave.
abstract.cn: 想象一次点击引出下一个页面，像板子滑向下一道浪。

examples.en: He learned to surf on the north shore of the island.
examples.cn: 他在岛上的北岸学会了冲浪。

examples.en: The surf pounded the rocks all night long.
examples.cn: 浪花整夜拍打着礁石。

examples.en: Students often surf the web for hours while studying.
examples.cn: 学生们学习时常上网浏览好几个小时。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑟夫」——浪来了要像贴身贴着水面那样「顺」着滑；把 surf 与顺水滑行的手感绑在一起；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语 surf 一般认为源自印度沿海语言或葡萄牙语对拍岸浪的称呼（来源存疑）→ 英语「碎浪」→ 夏威夷冲浪带来动词义「乘浪」→ 现代引申为「网上浏览」。

sensesIntro.en: Surf begins as the broken white water at the shore, turns into the sport of riding it, and then stretches to any ride on a moving surface, including the internet.
sensesIntro.cn: surf 最初指岸边翻白的碎浪，接着变成乘浪的运动，再扩展到随任何移动表面滑行，包括互联网。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rider on a board gliding along a breaking wave.
core.cn: 核心意象：冲浪者踩着板顺着碎浪滑行。

branches.en: Riding the wave is the basic verb.
branches.cn: 乘浪滑行是基本动词义。

branches.en: The broken water itself is the oldest noun sense.
branches.cn: 破碎的浪花本身是最古老的名词义。

branches.en: The sport grew around the board.
branches.cn: 这项运动围绕冲浪板成长起来。

branches.en: Browsing online borrows the gliding motion.
branches.cn: 网上浏览借用了滑行的动感。

branches.en: All keep the sense of being carried by something that is moving.
branches.cn: 三者都保留了被移动之物带着前行的感觉。

intro.en: Surf is a plain English word, with no prefix, around which the surfer family grows by suffix and compounding.
intro.cn: surf 是一个没有前缀的普通英语词，surfer 词族通过加后缀和复合在它周围生成。

latinIntro.en: Surf has no confirmed Latin origin, so there are no Latin family words here.
latinIntro.cn: surf 没有确证拉丁语源头，因此这里不列拉丁同源词。

items.example: Surf first names the white water at the shore.
items.exampleCN: surf 最初指岸边翻白的浪。

items.example: Surf as a verb comes from the sport.
items.exampleCN: 作为动词的 surf 来自这项运动。

items.example: The suffix -er turns surf into surfer.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 把 surf 变成 surfer。

items.example: Surfer also means a person who browses online.
items.exampleCN: surfer 也指上网浏览的人。

items.meaning: the act or activity of doing something
items.meaningCN: 表示活动或过程的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ing forms surfing from surf.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 由 surf 构成 surfing。

items.example: Surfing also names online browsing.
items.exampleCN: surfing 也指网上浏览。

items.example: Board combines with surf in surfboard.
items.exampleCN: board 与 surf 复合成 surfboard。

items.example: Surfboard is a plain compound of two nouns.
items.exampleCN: surfboard 是两个名词组成的直白复合词。

items.meaning: able to be used in a certain way
items.example: The suffix -able forms surfable.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -able 构成 surfable。

definition_zh: 推测；猜测；臆测；推测的结论
definition_en: to form an opinion about something from incomplete evidence, or such an opinion itself
core_image: 隔着毛玻璃看一个影子，心里悄悄拼出一个答案
scene: 信封上的铅笔字被雨打湿了，收信人只能凭模糊的痕迹猜寄信的人。From the faded postmark the clerk could only surmise who had sent it.
sceneCN: 这里 surmise 是「推测」（第 1 个义项：凭不完整的线索形成看法）；句意：从模糊的邮戳上，职员只能推测这是谁寄的。

pos.zh: 推测；猜测；臆测
推测；猜测；臆测

derivatives.zh: 推测出的；被认为是……的，过去分词转化的形容词
推测；猜测，动名词化的名词
可推测的，加后缀 -able 构成

senses.title: To guess from incomplete evidence
senses.definition: to judge that something is likely true on the basis of hints rather than proof
senses.definitionCN: 凭线索而非确证判断某事可能为真
senses.example: From the empty chairs she surmised that the meeting was cancelled.
senses.exampleCN: 看到一排空椅子，她推测会议取消了。
senses.why: The old French verb means to accuse on fancy, and the sense softened into forming a judgement from slight signs.
senses.whyCN: 古法语动词本义是凭想象指控，后来语气变缓，指凭细小迹象形成判断。

senses.title: A guess rather than a fact
senses.definition: an opinion reached by guessing, often treated as uncertain
senses.definitionCN: 靠猜测得出的看法，通常被视为不确定
senses.example: That he had once lived abroad is pure surmise.
senses.exampleCN: 他曾在国外生活过，这纯粹是臆测。
senses.why: The act of guessing turns into the thing guessed, so the noun keeps the flavour of uncertainty.
senses.whyCN: 猜测的动作转化为被猜出的东西，于是名词始终带着不确定的味道。

senses.title: To suspect something not stated
senses.definition: to sense privately that a hidden fact is true or that someone has a certain intention
senses.definitionCN: 私下感到某个隐秘事实为真，或某人有某种意图
senses.example: I surmise that he knew about the plan long before we did.
senses.exampleCN: 我猜想他早就知道这个计划了。
senses.why: When the guesses concern motives, the verb shades into the quieter, private sense of suspecting.
senses.whyCN: 当猜测落在动机上，这个动词就渐渐带上「暗自疑心」的安静意味。

senses.title: A formal conjecture in writing
senses.definition: a reasoned conjecture put forward, especially in formal or learned prose
senses.definitionCN: 尤其在正式或学术文字中提出的有理由的推想
senses.example: Historians still debate that surmise about the lost city.
senses.exampleCN: 历史学家仍在争论关于那座失落城市的推想。
senses.why: In learned prose the guess gains weight and is offered as a reasoned, if unproven, opinion.
senses.whyCN: 在学术文字中，猜测获得了分量，成为一种有理据但未证实的看法。

intro.en: Surmise comes from Old French surmis, the past participle of surmettre, to accuse or suppose, ultimately from Latin supermittere.
intro.cn: surmise 来自古法语 surmis，即 surmettre（指控、假定）的过去分词，最终源于拉丁语 supermittere。

items.en: Supermittere is made of super, over, and mittere, to put or send.
items.cn: supermittere 由 super（在上）与 mittere（放、送）构成。

items.en: Supermittere is used in legal Latin for putting something on a charge.
items.cn: supermittere 在法律拉丁语中用于把某事加进指控。

items.en: Surmettre means to accuse or to put forward as likely.
items.cn: 古法语 surmettre 意为指控或提出某种可能。

items.en: The word enters English as a legal and general noun of suspicion.
items.cn: 该词以表示怀疑的法律与普通名词形式进入英语。

items.en: Surmise settles into the modern sense of guessing from signs.
items.cn: surmise 固定为凭迹象猜测的现代含义。

items.en: The verb keeps a formal, slightly cautious tone.
items.cn: 动词保持正式而略带谨慎的语气。

note.en: Surmise belongs with think, guess, and suppose, but keeps a more formal and cautious voice.
note.cn: surmise 与 think、guess、suppose 同属「想」这一义场，但语气更正式、更谨慎。

entries.definition: guessed from hints
entries.definitionCN: 推测出的

entries.definition: the act of guessing
entries.definitionCN: 推测；猜测

entries.definition: death or the end of something
entries.definitionCN: 死亡；终止，只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a guess formed from limited evidence
entries.definitionCN: 推测；猜测

entries.definition: to work out a conclusion by reasoning
entries.definitionCN: 推断；推理得出

entries.definition: to accept something as true without proof
entries.definitionCN: 假定；想当然地认为

normalIntro.en: Surmise is a light guess: super, over, plus mittere, to put, becomes the mental putting of a likely story over the facts.
normalIntro.cn: surmise 是一记轻判断：super（在上）加 mittere（放），就是往事实上盖一个心中以为可能的故事。

normal.en: Super means over and mittere means to put, so to surmise is to put a guess over the facts.
normal.cn: super 表示在上，mittere 表示放，所以 surmise 就是把猜测盖在事实之上。

normal.en: The noun and the verb share one spelling in English.
normal.cn: 这个词在英语里名词与动词拼写相同。

normal.en: Surmise often takes a that clause, as when we say we surmise that he knows.
normal.cn: surmise 后面常接 that 从句，表示推测某个内容。

normal.en: Compare assumption: an assumption is accepted without proof, a surmise is offered as a guess.
normal.cn: 对比 assumption：assumption 是不加证明就接受，surmise 是明说为猜测。

normal.en: Surmise tends toward formal writing, while guess suits everyday speech.
normal.cn: surmise 偏正式书面语，guess 更适合日常口语。

abstract.en: Picture a shadow behind frosted glass that you quietly name.
abstract.cn: 想象毛玻璃后有个影子，你悄悄给它取了名字。

abstract.en: Imagine a folded note with one blurred and one clear line.
abstract.cn: 想象一张折起的纸条，一行模糊，一行清楚。

abstract.en: Think of a detective who has an idea before any proof arrives.
abstract.cn: 想象一位侦探在证据到来之前心里已经有了想法。

examples.en: The police surmised that the thief had left by the back door.
examples.cn: 警方推测小偷是从后门离开的。

examples.en: Her answer was no more than a surmise built on rumour.
examples.cn: 她的回答不过是建立在传言上的臆测。

examples.en: We can only surmise why the letter was never posted.
examples.cn: 我们只能推测那封信为何从未寄出。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑟买兹」——像在集市上「买」东西，货没看清就先在心里买个答案，这就是猜；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 super（在上）+ mittere（放、送）→ supermittere（把某物加在指控上）→ 古法语 surmettre（指控；假定）→ 英语 surmise，核心义「未证实而作出的判断」。

sensesIntro.en: Surmise starts as a judgement formed from slight evidence, then names the guess itself, then turns to private suspicion, and finally takes on a formal, learned tone.
sensesIntro.cn: surmise 先指凭细小证据形成的判断，再指猜测本身，继而转向私下的疑心，最后带上正式学术的语气。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shadow behind frosted glass that the mind quietly names.
core.cn: 核心意象：毛玻璃后一个影子，心里悄悄给它取名。

branches.en: Judging from hints is the everyday verb.
branches.cn: 凭线索判断是日常的动词用法。

branches.en: The guess itself is the noun sense.
branches.cn: 猜测本身是名词义项。

branches.en: Suspecting a hidden fact is the private sense.
branches.cn: 疑心某个隐情是私下的义项。

branches.en: The formal conjecture is the written register.
branches.cn: 正式推想属于书面语层。

branches.en: All three describe an opinion offered without full proof.
branches.cn: 三者都描述在没有充分证据时提出的看法。

intro.en: Surmise carries the Latin elements super, over, and mittere, to put, through the Old French verb surmettre.
intro.cn: surmise 经古法语动词 surmettre，携带着拉丁语成分 super（在上）与 mittere（放、送）。

latinIntro.en: Latin supermittere combines super, over, with mittere, to put or send.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 supermittere 由 super（在上）与 mittere（放、送）组合而成。

items.example: The prefix super- appears as sur- in French forms.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 super- 在法语形式中写作 sur-。

items.example: Mittere is the root shared with mission and admit.
items.exampleCN: mittere 是与 mission、admit 共用的词根。

items.meaning: to put upon, to add to a charge
items.example: Supermittere joins the prefix to the putting root.
items.exampleCN: supermittere 把前缀与「放」的词根连在一起。

items.example: Surmettre carries the Latin verb into French.
items.exampleCN: surmettre 把拉丁语动词带入法语。

items.example: Surmis is the form that English adopted as a noun.
items.exampleCN: 英语把这个形式作为名词借用。

items.example: Surmise keeps the noun and verb senses together.
items.exampleCN: surmise 兼具名词与动词义。

items.meaningCN: 表示过去或完成的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ed forms the adjective surmised.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成形容词 surmised。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或过程的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ing forms the noun surmising.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成名词 surmising。

items.example: The suffix -able forms surmisable.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -able 构成 surmisable。

definition_zh: 监视；监控；暗中盯守；监控系统
definition_en: the careful watching of a person, place or activity, especially by police or authorities, and the equipment or systems used to do this
core_image: 高处的一只眼睛，居高临下地盯住街角里的每一个人
scene: 傍晚的街角，一枚摄像头缓缓转向路人，楼上有人盯着屏幕。For weeks the police kept the flat under close surveillance.
sceneCN: 这里 surveillance 是「监视、监控」（第 1 个义项：警方等长期盯着某人或某地）；句意为警方连续数周对这处公寓实施严密监视。

pos.zh: 名词：监视、监控；监控设备与监控体系

derivatives.zh: 由本词逆构而成，义为「监视、监控」
由本词加 -ant 构成，义为「监视者；监视的」
由本词与 capitalism 复合而成，义为「监控资本主义」
由本词加前缀 anti- 构成，义为「反监控的」

senses.title: Watching a person or place closely
senses.definition: the act of carefully watching a person, place or activity, especially by police, officials or a suspicious party
senses.definitionCN: 严密盯住某人、某地或某项活动，尤指警察、官方或有疑虑的一方的行为
senses.example: The detective kept the house under surveillance all night.
senses.exampleCN: 警探整夜监视着那栋房子。
senses.why: The core of the word is watching from above, and the earliest use is a watch kept on a suspect or a place.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的核心是居高临下地看，最早的用法就是盯住嫌疑人或某处。

senses.title: Electronic monitoring of a place
senses.definition: the use of cameras, phones, sensors or software to monitor people, traffic or a space continuously
senses.definitionCN: 用摄像头、电话、传感器或软件持续监视人员、交通或某个空间
senses.example: The mall bans anyone caught shoplifting by camera surveillance.
senses.exampleCN: 商场会禁止任何被摄像头监控拍到的偷窃者进入。
senses.why: The watching eye can be a machine, so surveillance became the name for camera and sensor systems that never blink.
senses.whyCN: 注视的眼睛可以由机器充当，于是 surveillance 成了永不眨眼的摄像头与传感器系统的名称。

senses.title: Medical watching for disease
senses.definition: the continuous observation of a disease, a patient or a health trend in order to detect changes early
senses.definitionCN: 持续观察某种疾病、病人或健康趋势，以便及早发现变化
senses.example: Public health teams track the flu through surveillance of hospital visits.
senses.exampleCN: 公共卫生团队通过监测医院就诊情况来追踪流感。
senses.why: In medicine nothing is criminal, yet the same act of watching is kept: watch a body or a population so that change cannot hide.
senses.whyCN: 医学里并没有罪犯，但同样的「看」被保留下来：盯住身体或人群，让变化无法隐藏。

senses.title: A state of being watched
senses.definition: the condition of being watched or followed, usually expressed in the phrase under surveillance
senses.definitionCN: 被盯住或跟踪的状态，常用短语 under surveillance 表达
senses.example: The suspect remained under surveillance for three more weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 嫌疑人在随后的三周里仍处于监视之下。
senses.why: The noun can name the ongoing state rather than the action, which is why English says under surveillance like under watch.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词也可以指持续的状态而非动作，所以英语说 under surveillance，就像说 under watch 一样。

senses.title: The systems that do the watching
senses.definition: the equipment, network or programme that carries out monitoring, such as cameras, drones or a tracking system
senses.definitionCN: 执行监控的设备、网络或方案，如摄像头、无人机或追踪系统
senses.example: The government spent millions expanding its surveillance network.
senses.exampleCN: 政府投入数百万扩大其监控网络。
senses.why: The watching eye is replaced by hardware, so the noun names the whole apparatus rather than a single act.
senses.whyCN: 注视之眼被硬件取代，于是这个名词指整套设备，而不再指某一次动作。

intro.en: Surveillance is a French noun built on the verb surveiller, to watch over, and it replaced the older English word survail with the same meaning.
intro.cn: surveillance 是法语名词，由动词 surveiller「看守」构成，它取代了英语中同义的旧词 survail。

items.en: Super means over and above, and vigilare means to keep awake and watchful; the two ideas give the image of watching from above.
items.cn: super 意为在上、在上方，vigilare 意为保持清醒、警醒；两者合起来就是「从上方看着」。

items.en: Surveiller, formed in Old French, meant to watch over or keep an eye on; the base is the stem teller, from Medieval Latin vigilare.
items.cn: surveiller 在古法语中形成，意为看守、留意；词干为 teller，来自中世纪拉丁语 vigilare。

items.en: The noun surveillance names the act of watching over someone, first in police and military use.
items.cn: 名词 surveillance 指看守某人的行为，最初用于警务和军事语境。

items.en: English borrowed surveillance in the early nineteenth century; dictionaries record it from about 1802 onward.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪初借入 surveillance，词典记录约自 1802 年起使用。

items.en: The twentieth century added camera surveillance, state surveillance and medical surveillance, and the verb surveil was later back-formed from the noun.
items.cn: 二十世纪出现了摄像头监控、国家监控与医学监测，动词 surveil 则是由该名词逆构而来。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words that share the Latin watching root vigilare; the near-meaning group gathers other kinds of watching, each with a different purpose or level of secrecy.
note.cn: 形近组收共享拉丁语「守望」词根 vigilare 的词；近义组收其他形式的「看」，目的与隐秘程度各不相同。

entries.definition: adjective meaning watchful and alert to danger
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「警觉的、警惕的」，与拉丁语 vigilare 同源。

entries.definition: a period of keeping awake to watch or pray
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「守夜、守候」，同源，指保持清醒以守望或祈祷的一段时间。

entries.definition: a verb later made by removing the ending from surveillance
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「监视」，是由本词去掉词尾逆构而来，属于 backward formation。

entries.definition: a common misspelling that wrongly drops the second letter after the ve; it is not a word
entries.definitionCN: 常见拼写错误，把 ve 之后的字母漏掉；这不是正确拼写，只是拼写与之相近。

entries.definition: the act of watching something carefully to learn about it; neutral and not usually secret
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「观察、注意」，指仔细观察以了解情况，语气中性，通常并不隐秘。

entries.definition: secret spying to obtain political or military information; a crime, unlike ordinary surveillance
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「间谍活动」，指为获取政治或军事情报而暗中侦察，比一般监视更具犯罪性质。

entries.definition: a police watch kept on a place, one instance of surveillance; informal in tone
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「警方布控蹲守」，指对某处的一次监视行动，语气较口语。

entries.definition: the checking of conditions over time, such as air quality or a patient, not of people
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「监测」，指长期跟踪状况如空气质量或病人状况，对象一般不是人。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the French origin, the Latin watching root and the phrases surveillance actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用其法语来源、拉丁语「守望」词根，以及 surveillance 实际出现的常见搭配。

normal.en: super plus vigilare: over plus to stay awake, so surveillance is watching over while staying awake.
normal.cn: super 加 vigilare：在上加保持清醒，所以 surveillance 就是保持清醒、从上往下看守。

normal.en: The same root appears in vigilant and vigil, so all three keep the image of staying awake on watch.
normal.cn: 同一词根见于 vigilant 与 vigil，三者都保留了「醒着守望」的意象。

normal.en: English says under surveillance, never in surveillance, because the person is placed beneath the watching eye.
normal.cn: 英语说 under surveillance，不说 in surveillance，因为被监视者处在那只眼睛的下方。

normal.en: A surveillance camera is the watching eye in machine form; video surveillance is the same eye recording.
normal.cn: surveillance camera 是机器形态的注视之眼；video surveillance 则是这同一只眼在录像。

normal.en: The verb surveil was cut back from the noun, so the verb is younger than the noun.
normal.cn: 动词 surveil 是从名词逆构出来的，因此比名词更晚出现。

abstract.en: Picture a single eye high on a wall, turning slowly to follow anyone who walks below.
abstract.cn: 想象一只眼睛高高挂在墙上，慢慢转动，跟着下方走过的人。

abstract.en: The eye can also be a lens: a small camera blinks a red light as it records a doorway.
abstract.cn: 那只眼睛也可以是一只镜头：一只小摄像头闪着红灯，录下一扇门。

abstract.en: In a clinic the same eye looks not for a criminal but for the first tiny change in a chart.
abstract.cn: 在诊所里，同一只眼睛不是找罪犯，而是找图表上第一处细微变化。

examples.en: The bank has installed more surveillance cameras near the cash machines.
examples.cn: 银行在取款机附近安装了更多监控摄像头。

examples.en: Journalists say that state surveillance has grown in recent years.
examples.cn: 记者们表示，近年来国家监控有所扩大。

examples.en: Doctors asked for closer surveillance of elderly patients in winter.
examples.cn: 医生要求冬季对老年病人进行更密切的医学监测。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「飒威兰斯」——摄像头一盏，威风地扫过整条街：监视、监控

root: 法语 surveiller「看守」→ surveillance；surveiller 由 super「在上」+ teller（源自中世纪拉丁语 vigilare「守夜、警醒」）构成，核心义「在上方看住」。

sensesIntro.en: Surveillance runs from a police watch on one person, through machine monitoring, medical watching, the state of being watched, to the systems that do the watching.
sensesIntro.cn: 从警方盯住一个人，到机器监控，再到医学监测、被监视的状态，以及执行监视的整套系统，义项连续展开。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an eye in a high place that follows whoever passes below.
core.cn: 核心意象：高处的一只眼睛，跟着下方走过的人转动。

branches.en: THE WATCH: one person or place is watched closely by police or officials.
branches.cn: 盯守线：警察或官员密切盯住某个人或某处。

branches.en: THE EYE AS MACHINE: cameras and sensors do the watching and never look away.
branches.cn: 机器线：摄像头与传感器承担观看，从不开小差。

branches.en: THE CLINIC: the same watching is aimed at a disease or a public health trend.
branches.cn: 诊所线：同样的看被转向某种疾病或公共卫生趋势。

branches.en: THE PERSON UNDER IT: the target of the watch lives under surveillance as a state.
branches.cn: 被看者线：被盯着的人以「处于监视之下」的状态生活。

branches.en: THE APPARATUS: cameras and tracking networks become a system with its own name, surveillance.
branches.cn: 设备线：摄像头与追踪网络成为有自己名字的整套系统，即 surveillance。

intro.en: Surveillance is built from the Latin super, the French surveiller, and the Latin watching root vigilare, with a small English family growing around it.
intro.cn: surveillance 由拉丁语 super、法语 surveiller 与拉丁语「守望」词根 vigilare 构成，英语再围绕它长出一个小词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin super means over or above, and vigilare means to stay awake; French put them together into surveiller.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 super 意为在上、在上方，vigilare 意为保持清醒；法语把两者合成 surveiller。

items.example: The prefix gives the idea of watching from above.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀给出「从上方看」的意思。

items.example: The watching root supplies the idea of keeping awake.
items.exampleCN: 「守望」词根提供保持清醒的意思。

items.example: French combined the two Latin pieces into this verb.
items.exampleCN: 法语把这两个拉丁语成分合成这个动词。

items.example: The noun was borrowed into English nearly unchanged.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词几乎原样借入了英语。

items.example: The verb was back-formed by cutting off the ending.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是去掉词尾逆构而成的。

items.meaning: a person who watches, or watchful
items.example: The suffix -ant marks the watcher.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ant 表示监视的人。

items.example: Vigilant shares the watching root.
items.exampleCN: vigilant 共享「守望」词根。

items.example: It forms the compound word for resistance to monitoring.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示「反对监控」的复合词。

items.example: This noun frequently follows surveillance in everyday phrases.
items.exampleCN: 在日常搭配中这个词经常跟在 surveillance 之后。

definition_zh: 易感性；易受感染的程度；易受影响；脆弱；敏感性
definition_en: the state of being likely to be harmed or influenced, the degree to which someone or something easily catches a disease or reacts to something, and a tender feeling that is easily hurt
core_image: 表面没有硬壳的柔软身体，一碰就留下印子
scene: 实验室里，医生把两组人放在同一间空调房观察反应。The study found that older people have a higher susceptibility to flu.
sceneCN: 这里 susceptibility 是「易感性、易受感染的程度」（第 1 个义项：容易染上疾病的状态）；句意为研究发现老年人对流感更易感。

pos.zh: 名词：易感性；易受影响；脆弱；敏感性

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉后缀 -ibility 加 -ible 构成，义为「易受影响的；易感染的」
由形容词 susceptible 加 -ly 构成，义为「易受影响地」
由形容词加否定前缀 in- 构成，义为「不受影响的；不易感染的」
由形容词加否定前缀 non- 构成，义为「不敏感的；不易感的」

senses.title: The state of catching a disease easily
senses.definition: the condition of being likely to catch an illness or infection, or the degree of that likelihood
senses.definitionCN: 容易染上疾病或感染的状态，以及这种可能性的大小
senses.example: Poor sleep raises susceptibility to colds.
senses.exampleCN: 睡眠不足会提高患感冒的可能性。
senses.why: A body with an opening takes the germ in, so the Latin idea of taking up becomes the medical idea of easy infection.
senses.whyCN: 身体有了缺口，病菌就被接了进去，于是拉丁语「接纳」的意思变成医学上「易受感染」。

senses.title: Being easily influenced or affected
senses.definition: the condition of being easily influenced, persuaded or affected by people, ideas or conditions
senses.definitionCN: 容易被人、观念或环境所影响、说服或打动
senses.example: Teenagers often show a high susceptibility to peer pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 青少年往往很容易受到同辈压力的影响。
senses.why: What a person easily receives from outside also shapes the mind, so the same word covers influence and persuasion.
senses.whyCN: 人轻易从外面接收到的东西也会塑造心智，所以同一个词也涵盖受影响与被说服。

senses.title: A tender feeling that is easily hurt
senses.definition: a sensitive or fragile feeling, often in the plural, that makes a person easy to hurt or offend
senses.definitionCN: 敏感而容易受伤的感受，常用复数，指某人容易被触动或冒犯
senses.example: He spoke carefully so as not to wound her susceptibilities.
senses.exampleCN: 他说话很小心，以免伤到她的敏感之处。
senses.why: The tenderest part of a person is a receiver that cannot close, which gives the plural sense of feelings easily wounded.
senses.whyCN: 一个人最柔嫩的部分是一个无法关闭的接收器，于是发展出复数义「容易被刺伤的感受」。

senses.title: How strongly a material reacts
senses.definition: a measure of how strongly a material or system responds to an outside force such as a magnetic field
senses.definitionCN: 衡量材料或系统对外力如磁场反应强弱的指标
senses.example: Iron shows a much higher magnetic susceptibility than copper.
senses.exampleCN: 铁的磁化率远高于铜。
senses.why: Matter that easily takes in a field is measured by how strongly it receives, so the noun became a scientific quantity.
senses.whyCN: 容易接纳磁场作用的物质，用「接收强弱」来度量，于是这个名词成了科学上的量。

senses.title: Being sensitive to light, chemicals or other damage
senses.titleCN: 对光、化学物质等的敏感性
senses.definition: the state of being easily damaged or changed by something physical, such as light, moisture or a chemical
senses.definitionCN: 容易被光、湿气或化学物质等物理因素损伤或改变的状态
senses.example: Silver mirrors were stored in dark cases because of their susceptibility to tarnish.
senses.exampleCN: 银镜因容易失去光泽而被存放在暗盒里。
senses.why: A surface that takes in light or moisture is the open receiver again, now applied to materials that damage easily.
senses.whyCN: 能吸收光或湿气的表面再次是那个敞开的接收器，只是这次落在容易受损的材料上。

intro.en: Susceptibility is the noun built on the Latin adjective susceptibilis, from suscipere, to take up or take into oneself.
intro.cn: susceptibility 是在拉丁语形容词 susceptibilis 基础上构成的名词，其来源是 suscipere「接住、接纳」。

items.en: Sub means under and capere means to take; sub capere gives the image of catching something and taking it into oneself.
items.cn: sub 意为在下，capere 意为拿取；两者合起来就是接住某物并把它纳入自身。

items.en: Suscipere meant to take up, undertake or receive, and later developed the sense of easily admitting a thing.
items.cn: suscipere 意为承担、接受，后来又发展出「容易接纳某事物」的意思。

items.en: Susceptibilis, easy to take in or affected by, appears in scholarly and later medical Latin.
items.cn: susceptibilis 意为「容易接纳、容易受影响的」，见于学术拉丁语，后来也见于医学拉丁语。

items.en: The noun susceptibility enters English in the seventeenth century as the quality of being susceptible.
items.cn: 名词 susceptibility 在十七世纪进入英语，指「易感受、易受影响」的性质。

items.en: Medicine speaks of susceptibility to infection; physics speaks of magnetic susceptibility; everyday speech speaks of wounded susceptibilities.
items.cn: 医学谈「易感性」，物理学谈「磁化率」，日常语言则说 somebody 的 susceptibilities 受到伤害。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the adjectives and verbs built on the same Latin taking root; the near-meaning group gathers words for vulnerability, likelihood and sensitivity.
note.cn: 形近组收基于同一拉丁语「拿取」词根的形容词与动词；近义组收表示脆弱、可能性和敏感的词。

entries.definition: adjective meaning likely to be affected or infected
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「易受影响的、易感染的」，是该名词的形容词形式。

entries.definition: an older adjective meaning receptive or able to take in
entries.definitionCN: 较古旧的形容词，义为「容易接受的」，与主词同源。

entries.definition: a person or thing that receives; shares capere but not the same prefix
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「接受者」，与 capere 同源但前缀不同。

entries.definition: the state of being open to harm or attack; more about weakness than about tendency
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「脆弱、易受攻击」，强调弱点与暴露，而非倾向性。

entries.definition: the tendency to suffer from something or be affected by it; formal and often medical
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「易患……的倾向」，语气正式，常用于医学语境。

entries.definition: the ability to notice or react to small changes; about response strength, not weakness
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「敏感性」，指对细微变化的察觉与反应能力，重点在反应强弱。

entries.definition: an inclination to a condition that is often inherited, such as a disease
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「(患病)倾向」，常指遗传而来的易患某种情况的倾向。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Latin neediness of taking in, the adjective pair with susceptible, and the fixed phrases of the noun.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用拉丁语「接纳」的词义需要、与 susceptible 的配对关系，以及该名词的固定搭配。

normal.en: Prefix plus root means carrying something up from below, so the word needs an open receiver.
normal.cn: 前缀加词根意为从下方接住，所以这个词需要一个敞开着的接收者。

normal.en: Susceptibility is the noun of susceptible, just as ability is the noun of able.
normal.cn: susceptibility 是 susceptible 的名词形式，正如 ability 是 able 的名词。

normal.en: The phrase susceptibility to is followed by a noun: susceptibility to infection, to stress or to heat.
normal.cn: 搭配 susceptibility to 后接名词：对感染、对压力、对热的易感。

normal.en: In physics the fixed term is magnetic susceptibility, the measure of how a material reacts to a magnet.
normal.cn: 在物理学中有固定术语 magnetic susceptibility，指材料对磁体反应的强弱。

normal.en: The plural is a set phrase for feelings that are easy to wound.
normal.cn: 复数形式 susceptibilities 指敏感的情感，如 wounded susceptibilities 表示情感受到伤害。

abstract.en: Picture a body with no hard shell, so a single raindrop leaves a mark on the skin.
abstract.cn: 想象一个没有硬壳的身体，一滴雨就能在皮肤上留下印子。

abstract.en: Imagine a dry sponge in a room where someone tilts a cup of water: the sponge takes in everything nearby.
abstract.cn: 想象房间里的干海绵，有人一歪杯子，海绵就把周围的水全吸进去。

abstract.en: Think of a snowflake settling on a raw palm, melting the instant it touches.
abstract.cn: 想象一片雪花落在没有保护的掌心上，一碰就化。

examples.en: Vaccines protect people by lowering their susceptibility to the virus.
examples.cn: 疫苗通过降低人们对病毒的易感性来保护他们。

examples.en: The report blames financial susceptibility to overseas shocks on a weak currency.
examples.cn: 报告把金融体系易受海外冲击影响归因于货币疲软。

examples.en: Physicists measured the magnetic susceptibility of the new alloy.
examples.cn: 物理学家测量了这种新合金的磁化率。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑟赛普特比丽提」——瑟缩着（瑟）接受（赛普特），比柔弱（比丽）还柔：易受影响、敏感

root: 拉丁语 suscipere「接住、接纳」由 sub「在下」+ capere「拿取」构成，派生形容词 susceptibilis 再构成名词 susceptibility，核心义「容易接纳外来之物」。

sensesIntro.en: Susceptibility applies the same open-to-taking image to a body that catches disease, a mind open to influence, a tender feeling, a material that reacts to a force, and a surface that reacts to light or chemicals.
sensesIntro.cn: susceptibility 把「敞开接纳」的同一意象用在五处：易染病的身体、易受影响的心智、敏感的情感、对外力起反应的物质，以及对光或化学物质起反应的表面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body without a hard shell that takes the next touch into itself.
core.cn: 核心意象：没有硬壳的身体，把下一次接触直接吸收进去。

branches.en: THE BODY: a person who easily takes in a germ has high susceptibility.
branches.cn: 身体线：容易接纳病菌的人易感性就高。

branches.en: THE MIND: the same open receiver takes in opinions and pressure from others.
branches.cn: 心智线：同样敞开的接收器会接收他人的观点与压力。

branches.en: THE FEELING: the most tender part of a person is a susceptibility easily touched.
branches.cn: 情感线：一个人最柔嫩的部分就是容易被触到的敏感之处。

branches.en: THE LAB: matter responds to an outside force, measured as a physical susceptibility.
branches.cn: 实验室线：物质对外力作出反应，并量化为物理上的敏感性。

branches.en: THE SURFACE: both a patient and a mirror are open to damage by external agents.
branches.cn: 表面线：病人与镜面都容易受到外来因素损伤。

intro.en: Susceptibility comes from the Latin verb suscipere and the adjective susceptibilis; English adds the noun suffix -ibility to make the abstract noun.
intro.cn: susceptibility 来自拉丁语动词 suscipere 与形容词 susceptibilis；英语加上名词后缀 -ibility 构成这个抽象名词。

latinIntro.en: The prefix sub, the root capere and the derived verb suscipere are all recorded Latin forms.
latinIntro.cn: 前缀 sub、词根 capere 与派生动词 suscipere 都是有文献记录的拉丁语形式。

items.example: The prefix gives the idea of taking up from below.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀给出「从下方接住」的意思。

items.example: The root describes holding something in the hand.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根描述把某物握在手中。

items.example: A prefix and a root here combine into this verb.
items.exampleCN: 这里一个前缀与一个词根合成了这个动词。

items.meaning: able to take in, easily affected
items.example: The adjective is the direct base of the English pair.
items.exampleCN: 形容词是英语这一对词的直接基础。

items.example: The adjective keeps the Latin shape almost complete.

definition_zh: 易受影响的；易感染的；易被……打动的；能够经受……的
definition_en: likely to be affected or harmed by something, easily infected by a disease, easily influenced or moved, or able to undergo a change
core_image: 一扇缺少门闩的窗子，外面一推就能打开
scene: 冬天的大学宿舍里，有人咳嗽不止，室友开始担心。Children who sleep badly are susceptible to colds all winter.
sceneCN: 这里 susceptible 是「易受……影响的、易感染的」（第 1 个义项：容易染上疾病）；句意为睡眠不足的孩子更容易患感冒。

pos.zh: 形容词：易受影响的；易感染的；易被……打动的；能够承受……的

forms.label: 比较级（用 more 构成）
最高级（用 most 构成）

由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「易受影响地」
