senses.title: Likely to be affected or harmed by something
senses.titleCN: 易受……影响的；易受损伤的
senses.definition: likely to experience harm or a negative effect because of a condition, a substance or a situation
senses.definitionCN: 由于某种条件、物质或处境而容易受到伤害或负面影响
senses.example: Young plants are very susceptible to frost.
senses.exampleCN: 幼苗非常容易受霜冻伤害。
senses.why: The two Latin pieces mean under and to take, so an object with no barrier simply takes the harm in.
senses.whyCN: 这两个拉丁语成分意为「在下」与「拿取」，因此没有任何屏障的对象会把伤害直接接进来。

senses.title: Easily infected by a disease
senses.definition: easily catching an illness or infection, often because of age, health or medicine
senses.definitionCN: 容易染病或感染，常因年龄、健康状况或用药所致
senses.example: Patients on this drug are more susceptible to infection.
senses.exampleCN: 服用这种药物的病人更容易受到感染。
senses.why: Taking in works inward as well, so a body that is open to an illness is open to every germ inside it.
senses.whyCN: 「接纳」是向内进行的，所以容易让外物进入的身体，也容易让病菌进入。

senses.title: Easily influenced or persuaded
senses.definition: easily influenced by other people, advertising or ideas, often because of youth or inexperience
senses.definitionCN: 容易受他人、广告或观念左右，常因年轻或缺乏经验
senses.example: Young readers are susceptible to advertising.
senses.exampleCN: 年轻读者容易受广告影响。
senses.why: What is open to a disease is open in the same way to a person, an advert or a rumour.
senses.whyCN: 对疾病敞开的东西，同样对某个人、一则广告或一个谣言敞开。

senses.title: Easily moved or touched
senses.definition: easily moved by feelings, beauty or kindness; often used with the word to
senses.definitionCN: 容易因情感、美好的事物或善意而感动，常与 to 连用
senses.example: She is susceptible to a good story.
senses.exampleCN: 她很容易被一个好故事打动。
senses.why: The door can be pushed from the inside too, so the same word describes being moved by feeling.
senses.whyCN: 这扇门也能从内侧被推开，所以同一个词也能描述被情感打动。

senses.title: Open to being treated or solved in a certain way
senses.definition: able to receive a particular treatment, solution or proof; a formal use usually followed by of
senses.definitionCN: 能够接受某种处理、解决办法或证明；正式用法，通常后接 of
senses.example: The problem is susceptible of a simple solution.
senses.exampleCN: 这个问题可以用一个简单的办法解决。
senses.why: In formal use the open door also admits a cure or a proof, which is why the adjective can take of.
senses.whyCN: 在正式用法中，敞开的门也接纳一种解决办法或证明，这就是它能够搭配 of 的原因。

intro.en: Susceptible comes from Late Latin susceptibilis, built on suscipere, to take up from below, which joins sub, under, and capere, to take.
intro.cn: susceptible 来自晚期拉丁语 susceptibilis，其基础是 suscipere「从下方接住」，由 sub「在下」与 capere「拿取」构成。

items.en: Capere, to take or seize, is one of the most productive Latin verbs and gives capture, receive and recipient.
items.cn: capere 意为拿、抓，是拉丁语中最能产的动词之一，capture、receive、recipient 都源于它。

items.en: Sub capere became suscipere, to take up, undertake or receive, with the d of the prefix folding into the s.
items.cn: sub 与 capere 合成 suscipere，意为接起、承担、接纳，前缀的 d 并入后面的 s。

items.en: Susceptibilis, able to take in or receive, appears in Late Latin and passes into medieval scholarly use.
items.cn: susceptibilis 意为「能够接纳、接受的」，见于晚期拉丁语，并进入中世纪的学术用法。

items.en: Renewed classical scholarship brought a Latin-derived adjective into French spelling, susceptibles in the plural.
items.cn: 文艺复兴时期的古典学研究让这个词以法语拼写重新出现，当时形式为复数的 susceptibles。

items.en: English records susceptible in the early seventeenth century, first meaning able to receive or admit something.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪初记录 susceptible，最初意为「能够接受或容纳某物」。

items.en: Science made it technical for infections, magnets and materials, so the everyday sense of easily affected grew alongside.
items.cn: 科学把它用作感染、磁体和材料的术语，与此同时「容易受影响」的日常义也随之发展。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the noun, adverb and plural forms of the same Latin taking root; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives for exposure, fragility and openness.
note.cn: 形近组收基于同一拉丁语「拿取」词根的名词、副词形式；近义组收表示暴露、脆弱与开放态度的形容词。

entries.definition: the noun for the quality of being susceptible
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「易感性、敏感性」，由本词加后缀直接构成。

entries.definition: the adverb, meaning in a way that shows being susceptible
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「易受影响地」，由本词加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: an older adjective meaning receptive or able to take in
entries.definitionCN: 较古旧的形容词，义为「容易接受的」，与主词同根。

entries.definition: a person or thing that receives; shares capere with a different prefix
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「接受者」，与 capere 同源、前缀不同，只是词根相近。

entries.definition: exposed to the risk of harm or attack; stresses weakness, not tendency
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「脆弱的、易受攻击的」，强调弱点与暴露，而非倾向性。

entries.definition: likely to do or suffer something because of habit or tendency
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「倾向于……的、易于……的」，强调习惯或倾向。

entries.definition: likely to experience something bad or have to do something; formal
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「易于……的、可能会……的」，语气正式，多指不利的事。

entries.definition: protected from a disease or not affected by something; the reverse of susceptible
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「免疫的、不受影响的」，是 susceptible 的反义词。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Latin taking root, the fixed preposition to, and the ordinary words this adjective pairs with.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用拉丁语「拿取」词根、固定的介词 to，以及这个形容词常搭配的普通词。

normal.en: Assume the prefix under and a root meaning to take, so the adjective means able to be taken in.
normal.cn: 把前缀理解为「在下」，词根理解为「拿」，于是这个形容词就是「能够被接进去的」。

normal.en: The same root gives capture and receive, all built on the idea of taking.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出 capture 与 receive，它们都建立在「拿取」这一概念上。

normal.en: Susceptible usually takes to, while a few formal uses take of, as in susceptible of proof.
normal.cn: susceptible 通常搭配 to，少数正式用法搭配 of，如 susceptible of proof。

normal.en: Compare with the Latin-based noun formed by replacing ible with ibility.
normal.cn: 对比把 ible 换成 ibility 后形成的拉丁名词形式，即它的名词。

normal.en: The phrase susceptible to infection is a standard medical pairing.
normal.cn: 短语 susceptible to infection 是医学中的标准搭配。

abstract.en: Picture a window without a latch: the wind only has to come close, and it opens.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇没有门闩的窗，风只要靠近一点，它就打开。

abstract.en: Imagine a sick patient in a thin blanket, ready for any germ that passes by.
abstract.cn: 想象一个病人盖着薄毯，随时准备接受路过的每一个病菌。

abstract.en: Think of a child watching a bright poster and believing every word on it at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子看着鲜艳的海报，立刻相信上面的每一个字。

examples.en: Some crops are more susceptible to drought than others.
examples.cn: 有些作物比别的作物更容易受旱。

examples.en: People with weak lungs are susceptible to chest infections.
examples.cn: 肺部虚弱的人容易患胸部感染。

examples.en: The young and the lonely are especially susceptible to online scams.
examples.cn: 年轻人和孤独的人尤其容易落入网络诈骗。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑟赛普特不」——瑟缩着（瑟）把东西全接下来（赛普特），一点都「不」设防：易受影响的

root: 拉丁语 suscipere「接住、接纳」由 sub「在下」+ capere「拿取」构成，晚期拉丁语形容词 susceptibilis 演变为英语 susceptible，核心义「易被接进来的」。

sensesIntro.en: One open window serves five uses: harming a body, infecting a patient, shaping a mind, moving a heart, and letting a problem be solved.
sensesIntro.cn: 一扇敞开的窗有五种用法：伤害身体、感染病人、左右心智、打动人心，以及让问题得以被解决。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a window without a latch that any push can open.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇没有门闩的窗，任何推力都能把它打开。

branches.en: THE BODY OR CROP: whatever is exposed is easily hurt by weather, heat or medicine.
branches.cn: 身体或作物线：暴露在外的对象容易被天气、热度或药物伤害。

branches.en: THE GATE: harm walks in through an open gate, so infection follows naturally.
branches.cn: 大门线：伤害从敞开的大门走进来，于是感染随之而来。

branches.en: THE MIND: what is open to disease is equally open to ideas and advertising.
branches.cn: 心智线：对疾病敞开的人，同样对观念和广告敞开。

branches.en: THE HEART: the same openness, turned inward, makes a person easy to move.
branches.cn: 心灵线：同一种敞开转向内心，就让人容易被打动。

branches.en: THE FORMAL CHAIN: an open receiver can also admit a cure or a proof.
branches.cn: 正式用法线：敞开的接收器同样能接纳一种解决办法或证明。

intro.en: Susceptible is a Latin adjective that still keeps both of its original pieces: a prefix meaning under and a root meaning to take.
intro.cn: susceptible 是拉丁语形容词，原样的两个成分仍然保留：表示「在下」的前缀与表示「拿取」的词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin sub, capere and suscipere are all recorded, and the late adjective susceptibilis explains the English ending ible.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sub、capere 与 suscipere 均有文献记录，晚期拉丁语形容词 susceptibilis 解释了英语词尾 ible 的来源。

items.exampleCN: 这个前缀显示对象是从下方被接起的。

items.exampleCN: 这个词根与 capture 等词共享。

items.example: The two Latin pieces joined into this verb.
items.exampleCN: 两个拉丁语成分合成了这个动词。

items.exampleCN: 这个晚期形容词是英语词的直接来源。

items.example: It marks the adjective as able to be taken in.
items.exampleCN: 它标明这个形容词是「可以被接进去的」。

items.example: It forms the noun form of this adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它构成这个形容词的名词形式。

definition_zh: 悬念；悬而未决；忐忑不安的心情；紧张期待
definition_en: a feeling of excited uncertainty about what will happen next, especially while waiting for an unclear outcome
core_image: 一根细线悬着什么东西，下面还没有接住的手，你屏住呼吸盯着它
scene: 侦探刚就要说出凶手的名字，镜头却转去了窗外。The whole cinema sat in suspense as the detective opened the envelope.
sceneCN: 这里 suspense 是「悬念、悬而未决」（第 1 个义项：对接下来会发生什么的不确定而又紧张的感觉）；句意：侦探拆开信封时，整个影院的人都屏息以待。那根悬着的细线，就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 悬念；悬而未决；紧张期待

collocations.zh: 让某人焦急等待；吊人胃口
悬而未决地；忐忑不安地

forms.label: 复数（少数用法：悬念时刻）

derivatives.zh: 由 suspense 加形容词词尾 -ful 构成，义为「充满悬念的、扣人心弦的」
同根动词，「悬起、挂起」，引申为「暂停、使中止」
由 suspend 加 -ion 构成，义为「悬挂、暂停、停职」
加施动者词尾 -er，义为「吊带、悬吊物」
加 -ive 构成，义为「悬而未决的、使人焦虑的」

senses.title: The gripping wait before an answer
senses.definition: the tense, excited feeling of not yet knowing how something will end
senses.definitionCN: 还不知道事情会怎样收场时那种紧张又期待的心情
senses.example: The director keeps the audience in suspense until the final minute.
senses.exampleCN: 导演把观众的胃口吊到最后一分钟。
senses.why: The Latin verb suspendere means to hang up, and the mind hangs in the air without touching either answer.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词意为「悬吊」，心思也被吊在半空，既碰不到答案，也落不下来。

senses.title: An outcome still undecided
senses.definition: the state of an affair or a question that has not yet been settled either way
senses.definitionCN: 某件事或某个问题尚未有定论的状态
senses.example: The fate of the old library is still in suspense.
senses.exampleCN: 老图书馆的命运仍然悬而未决。
senses.why: If a thing is hung up, it is not yet placed down, so the word also names a question left open.
senses.whyCN: 挂起来的东西就是还没放下，所以这个词也指一个悬着没有结论的问题。

senses.title: Uneasy doubt about someone
senses.definition: a lingering feeling of doubt or anxiety, often about what another person feels or intends
senses.definitionCN: 一种迟迟不散的疑虑或不安，常常关乎别人的心意或打算
senses.example: She answered politely but with obvious suspense about his real motive.
senses.exampleCN: 她答得很客气，但显然对他的真实动机满腹疑虑。
senses.why: An older use of the word meant mental hesitation, when the judgement is held back between trust and doubt.
senses.whyCN: 这个词有一种较早的用法表示「心中迟疑」，判断在信任与怀疑之间被搁住。

senses.title: A genre of tense storytelling
senses.definition: a kind of fiction or drama built on making the audience nervous about what comes next
senses.definitionCN: 靠让观众对后续情节提心吊胆来吸引人的小说或戏剧类型
senses.example: Hitchcock was called the master of suspense.
senses.exampleCN: 希区柯克被称为悬念大师。
senses.why: Because the feeling is so powerful, the word came to name whole books and films that are sold on it.
senses.whyCN: 这种感受太强烈，于是这个词也成了整整一类靠它吸引人的书与电影的招牌。

senses.title: A short halt in time
senses.definition: a temporary pause or holding back of an action, now mostly found in formal legal and theatrical wording
senses.definitionCN: 动作的暂时停顿或搁置，如今多见于正式的法律与剧场用语
senses.example: The court ordered a suspense of the payments until the appeal was heard.
senses.exampleCN: 法院命令在听审上诉之前暂停付款。
senses.why: The hanging image also means being held up, so the noun once named a pause in any proceeding.
senses.whyCN: 悬着的意象也意味着「被搁起」，所以这个名词一度泛指任何进程中的停顿。

intro.en: Suspense comes from Latin suspendere, to hang up, through Old French. The modern sense of a nervous wait is recent.
intro.cn: suspense 经古法语来自拉丁语 suspendere（悬起、挂起）。表示「紧张等待」的现代义出现得很晚。

items.en: Pendere meant to hang or weigh, and sub- meant under, so suspendere pictured something hung up from below.
items.cn: pendere 意为「悬挂、称量」，sub- 表示「在下方」，suspendere 描绘的是从下面吊起的东西。

items.en: The noun suspensum named a hanging, literally or in a legal sense of delay.
items.cn: 名词 suspensum 指悬挂这一动作，在法律语境里也指延后。

items.en: Old French suspense kept the sense of being held back or postponed.
items.cn: 古法语 suspense 保留了「被搁住、被推迟」的含义。

items.en: Early English used suspense for an interruption or a halt, especially in law and in church matters.
items.cn: 早期英语用 suspense 表示中断或中止，尤见于法律与教会事务。

items.en: The sense of anxious uncertainty in a story grew with the novel, and critics later fixed the term as a genre label.
items.cn: 随着长篇小说兴起，「对情节的焦虑期待」这一义项成长起来，评论界后来把它固定为体裁名称。

note.en: Group one holds the pend- family and words that only look close; group two holds the states the word is compared with.
note.cn: 第一组是同一词根的 pend- 家族以及仅仅形近的词；第二组是与它常拿来比较的各种状态。

entries.definition: The verb behind the noun: to hang something up, and by extension to stop it for a time.
entries.definitionCN: 藏在名词背后的动词：把东西挂起来，引申为暂时停止。

entries.definition: The action or state of hanging or pausing: suspension of a licence, or the springs of a car.
entries.definitionCN: 悬挂或暂停的动作与状态：驾照暂停，或汽车的悬挂系统。

entries.definition: Looks very close because it shares the sus- opening, but it comes from suspicere, to look up at, not from hanging.
entries.definitionCN: 因开头同为 sus- 而形近，但它出自「向上看」，与「悬挂」词源不同。

entries.definition: From the same hanging root: a jewel or light that is meant to hang.
entries.definitionCN: 同一「悬挂」词根：特意用来垂挂的珠宝或灯具。

entries.definition: A stretched tightness, physical or emotional; the strain of waiting, without the sense of an open outcome.
entries.definitionCN: 拉紧的张力，或身体与情绪上的紧绷；侧重紧张而非结局未定。

entries.definition: A hopeful expectation of a good thing; it may be pleasant, while suspense is uneasy.
entries.definitionCN: 对好事的期盼，多半是愉快的；悬念则带不安。

entries.definition: A general worry that something may go wrong, often without any story to drive it.
entries.definitionCN: 担心出事的一般性忧虑，往往并没有故事在推。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin hanging image, the pend- family, and the fixed phrases built on the noun.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁「悬挂」意象、pend- 词族，以及由这个名词构成的固定搭配。

normal.en: Outside the -se ending sits Latin pendere, the same verb that hangs a pendant and keeps a pendulum swinging.
normal.cn: 词尾之前是拉丁语 pendere，同一个动词既让吊坠悬着，也让钟摆来回摆动。

normal.en: To keep someone in suspense is literally to hang them up in the air for a while.
normal.cn: 把某人留在悬念里，字面就是让他悬在半空一阵子。

normal.en: A suspense film or novel sells one thing: the audience not knowing the ending yet.
normal.cn: 悬念电影或小说卖的只有一样东西：观众还不知道结局。

normal.en: The family runs suspend, suspension, suspenseful, suspender.
normal.cn: 同族词有悬挂、暂停、充满悬念的、吊带。

normal.en: Compare doubt and uncertainty: they are quieter, while suspense carries an active pull toward the answer.
normal.cn: 对比怀疑与不确定：它们更安静，而 suspense 有一种拉着你等答案的力量。

abstract.en: Picture a rope that stops one hand width above the ground, with the bag still swaying.
abstract.cn: 想象一根绳停在离地一掌高的地方，袋子还在轻轻晃。

abstract.en: Picture a card held face down between two fingers, not yet turned over.
abstract.cn: 想象一张背面朝上的牌夹在两指之间，还没翻过来。

abstract.en: Picture a red light that has just turned on for a race nobody has started.
abstract.cn: 想象赛跑的红灯已经亮起，却还没人起步。

examples.en: The novelist held her readers in suspense for three chapters before the truth came out.
examples.cn: 小说家让读者揪心了三章，真相才浮出水面。

examples.en: News of the missing climbers left the whole village in suspense.
examples.cn: 失踪登山者的消息让整个村子都悬着心。

examples.en: Detectives of the old school are masters at building suspense with very little sound.
examples.cn: 老派侦探是善于用极少的声响营造悬念的大师。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「色喷死」——把颜色喷得到处都是，一片混乱，让人心里悬着；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 sub-（在下方）+ pendere（悬挂）→ suspendere（吊起、搁置）→ 名词 suspensum → 古法语 suspense → 英语 suspense；核心义「悬在半空、尚未落地」。

sensesIntro.en: Suspense starts with the image of something held in mid-air: the mind that hangs waiting, the question left open, and finally a whole genre named after that feeling.
sensesIntro.cn: suspense 起点是「悬在半空」的意象：心思悬着等待，问题悬而未决，最后整整一种体裁都以这种心情命名。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an object hung just out of reach, swaying while everyone below waits for it to drop.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件东西悬在够不着的地方摇晃，下面的人都等着它落地。

branches.en: THE WAIT: the mind is the hung object, and the audience cannot yet put it down.
branches.cn: 等待：被吊着的是读者的心思，还不能放下。

branches.en: THE OPEN QUESTION: a matter hung up is a matter not yet settled.
branches.cn: 悬案：被挂起来的事就是还没定下来的事。

branches.en: THE HELD JUDGEMENT: trust and doubt both hang free, so the word also names uneasy doubt.
branches.cn: 判断被搁住：信任与怀疑都悬着，于是这个词也指忐忑的疑虑。

branches.en: THE GENRE: the feeling became a shelf label for novels and films.
branches.cn: 体裁：这种心情成了小说与电影的名目。

branches.en: THE HALT AND THE WAIT share one image: something held in mid-course, briefly or for a long time.
branches.cn: 中断与等待共用一个意象：某物在途中被按住，或短或久。

intro.en: Suspense is built from a Latin prefix and a Latin verb stem, and the same two parts recur in English through the whole pend- family.
intro.cn: suspense 由一个拉丁前缀与一个拉丁动词词干构成，同样这两部分在英语的整个 pend- 词族里反复出现。

latinIntro.en: Latin sub- means under or from below, and pendere means to hang or weigh; suspended literally says hung from underneath.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sub- 表示「在下方、从下面」，pendere 表示「悬挂、称量」；合起来字面就是「从下面吊着」。

items.example: The prefix turns hanging into hanging from underneath.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「悬挂」变成「从下面吊着」。

items.example: Pendere gives the whole image of the suspended object.
items.exampleCN: pendere 提供整个「悬吊物」的意象。

items.example: The compound suspends a lamp over the table.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词表示把灯吊在桌子上方。

items.meaning: a hanging, a state held open
items.example: The noun names the state of being held in the air.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指被悬在空中的状态。

items.example: The suffix turns the noun into an adjective of fullness.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把名词变成表示「充满」的形容词。

items.example: The ending of that chapter is famously suspenseful.
items.exampleCN: 那一章的结尾出了名地扣人心弦。

items.example: The suffix builds the related noun from the verb stem.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾由动词词干造出相关名词。

items.example: The bridge rests on steel suspension cables.
items.exampleCN: 这座桥靠钢制悬索承重。

items.example: Pairs of suspenders hold a pair of trousers up.
items.exampleCN: 背带把裤子吊住。

items.example: The older word for a garter is suspender.
items.exampleCN: 吊袜带较旧的英文说法就是 suspender。

definition_zh: 食物；营养；维持生命的东西；生计
definition_en: the food and drink that keep a person or a living thing alive and strong
core_image: 一只手把一碗热汤托在一副摇摇欲坠的肩膀下面，碗没有翻
scene: 探险队在雪地里走了三天，背包里只剩下一点干粮和水。They carried enough sustenance for three days across the frozen pass.
sceneCN: 这里 sustenance 是「维持生命的食物」（第 1 个义项：让人活下去的食物与饮品）；句意：他们带着足够三天用的食物穿过冰封的山口。那只手托住的碗，就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 食物；营养；生计（不可数）

forms.label: 复数（少见，指多种养料或生计来源）

derivatives.zh: 同根动词，义为「支撑、维持、承受、供养」
由 sustain 加 -able 构成，义为「可维持的、可持续的」
sustain 的过去分词作形容词，义为「持续的、持久的」
现在分词作形容词，义为「维持生命的、起支撑作用的」
加 -er 构成，义为「维持者、供养者、助推器」

senses.title: Food that keeps body and soul together
senses.definition: the food and drink a person needs in order to stay alive and keep working
senses.definitionCN: 一个人活下去、干得动活所必需的食物与饮品
senses.example: The refugees received rice and oil as their only sustenance.
senses.exampleCN: 难民们只领到大米和油作为口粮。
senses.why: Latin sustinere means to hold up from below, and food is what holds a body up from day to day.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词意为「从下面托住」，而食物正是日复一日从下面托住这具身体的支撑。

senses.title: The nourishment inside that food
senses.definition: the nourishing quality of food, what a body actually takes in for strength and growth
senses.definitionCN: 食物里滋养身体的那种成分，身体真正用来增长气力的东西
senses.example: Roots and berries gave the animals enough sustenance to survive the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 根茎与浆果为这些动物提供了足以过冬的养分。
senses.why: Since the same word names the food and what the food gives, it slid from the meal to the nourishment in it.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词既指食物本身，也指食物给出的东西，于是从「餐饭」滑向其中的「养分」。

senses.title: The support of mind or spirit
senses.definition: something non-material, such as faith, art or company, that holds a person up in hard times
senses.definitionCN: 信仰、艺术或陪伴等非实物的东西，在艰难时托住一个人
senses.example: In the empty house, letters from her sister were her only sustenance.
senses.exampleCN: 在那座空房子里，姐姐的来信是她唯一的慰藉。
senses.why: The verb behind the noun also means to bear up under stress, so its noun could carry the sense of holding a spirit up.
senses.whyCN: 背后的动词也表示「在压力下支撑住」，所以它的名词也能指把精神托起来。

senses.title: What someone lives on
senses.definition: the means by which a person or a community earns a living
senses.definitionCN: 一个人或一个社区赖以为生的手段
senses.example: Fishing is still the chief sustenance of the islanders.
senses.exampleCN: 打鱼仍是岛民最主要的生计。
senses.why: From bread to livelihood is one step: the thing that keeps a life going widened from the plate to the whole household.
senses.whyCN: 从口粮到生计只差一步：让生活得以继续的东西，从碗里扩大到整个家庭。

senses.title: Support in a formal or technical register
senses.definition: a formal word for something that maintains strength, soundness or an institution
senses.definitionCN: 正式用语，指维持力量、健全或某个制度的支撑
senses.example: Free schooling is one of the main sustenances of a modern city.
senses.exampleCN: 免费教育是现代都市的主要支撑之一。
senses.why: Technical writers borrowed the lofty noun for anything that keeps a system upright, as food keeps a body upright.
senses.whyCN: 技术写作者借走这个庄重的名词，用来指一切让体系立住的东西，正如食物让身体立住。

intro.en: Sustenance comes from Latin sustinere, to hold up, through Old French sustenence. The core of holding something beneath has stayed in place.
intro.cn: sustenance 经古法语 sustenence 来自拉丁语 sustinere（从下面托住），「托住」这个核心一直没有变。

items.en: Tenere meant to hold, and sub- meant under, so the compound pictured holding something up from below.
items.cn: tenere 意为「握住」，sub- 表示「在下方」，这个复合词描绘的是从下面把某物托住。

items.en: Sustinere meant to bear up, to endure and to support, and also to sustain life with food.
items.cn: sustinere 意为「承受、忍受、支撑」，也指用食物维持生命。

items.en: The noun sustentation named the act of supporting or feeding someone.
items.cn: 名词 sustentation 指支撑或供养这一行为。

items.en: Old French shaped the word as sustenence, the form that English then borrowed.
items.cn: 古法语把它定型为 sustenence，英语随后借用了这个形式。

items.en: English first used it for livelihood and nourishment, and later gave it the lofty sense of moral and spiritual support.
items.cn: 英语早期用它表示生计与营养，后来发展出道德与精神支撑的高雅义。

note.en: Group one holds the ten-/tain- holding family and one near-twin by spelling; group two holds the words for what a body lives on.
note.cn: 第一组是含「握、持」词根的家族，以及一个拼写近似到几乎相同的词；第二组是表示「活命所需之物」的词。

entries.definition: Almost the same ending, built on the same holding verb: the act of keeping something in working order.
entries.definitionCN: 结尾几乎相同，出自同一个「握住」动词：使某物保持正常运转的行为。

entries.definition: One who holds land or a building from a landlord, from the same Latin verb to hold.
entries.definitionCN: 从房东那里「持有」土地或房屋的人，同出拉丁语「握住」。

entries.definition: To hold something within, the same hold-verb with a prefix meaning together.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物围在里面，与 sustenance 同源于「握住」，前缀表示「合在一起」。

entries.definition: To keep something going with effort, literally to hold it with the hand.
entries.definitionCN: 费力地让某物维持运转，字面是「用手一直握住」。

entries.definition: What food gives the body, with the emphasis on growth and health rather than on merely staying alive.
entries.definitionCN: 食物给身体的东西，侧重生长与健康，而不只是活下去。

entries.definition: Stocks of food gathered and carried in advance, especially by travellers or soldiers.
entries.definitionCN: 事先备好并携带的食物储备，尤指旅行者或士兵的。

entries.definition: A drink poured out in offering, used loosely for a drink in a ceremonial tone.
entries.definitionCN: 祭祀时浇洒的饮品，也轻松地戏称一杯酒。

entries.definition: The bare minimum needed to live, often used of farms and economies that only feed their own people.
entries.definitionCN: 维持生存的最低所需，常用于只能自给自足的农场与经济。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin hold-verb under the word, the ten-/tain- family, and the collocations it keeps.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：词里那个拉丁语「握住」动词、ten- 与 tain- 字母家族，以及它习惯用的搭配。

normal.en: Latin tenere, to hold, sits inside the word, so sustenance is literally the holding up of a life.
normal.cn: 词里藏着拉丁语 tenere（握住），所以 sustenance 字面就是「把一条命托住」。

normal.en: The noun keeps a formal flavour: governments and charities talk of providing sustenance rather than food.
normal.cn: 这个名词带点正式色彩：政府与慈善机构常说「提供 sustenance」而不说「提供食物」。

normal.en: Daily sustenance and spiritual sustenance are the two faces of the same support.
normal.cn: 日常口粮与精神养料是同一支撑的两面。

normal.en: The family runs sustain, sustainable, sustained, sustenant.
normal.cn: 同族词有维持、可持续的、持续的、提供营养的。

normal.en: Compare subsistence: subsistence is the bare minimum, sustenance can be richer and can even be mental.
normal.cn: 对比 subsistence：后者只是活命的最低限度，前者可以更丰足，甚至可以是精神上的。

abstract.en: Picture a sagging beam held up by one small wooden post.
abstract.cn: 想象一根下弯的横梁被一根小木柱从底下顶住。

abstract.en: Picture a bowl carried on an open palm through a long winter walk.
abstract.cn: 想象掌心平端着一只碗，走过一段漫长的冬路。

abstract.en: Picture an empty stomach drawn as a hollow drum that only bread can fill.
abstract.cn: 想象空胃被画成一只空鼓，只有面包能把它填满。

examples.en: Planting the fields early gave the family a year of sustenance.
examples.cn: 早早下地耕种，让这一家人有了一年的口粮。

examples.en: The monks drew sustenance from silence as much as from bread.
examples.cn: 修士们既从面包里，也从静默中汲取养料。

examples.en: For many coastal villages, selling shells was the only means of sustenance.
examples.cn: 对许多沿海村庄来说，卖贝壳是唯一的谋生手段。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「萨斯滕能死」——听起来像「少了它人会撑不住」，正对应「维持生命的东西」；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 sub-（在下方）+ tenere（握住、持住）→ sustinere（托住、承受、抚养）→ 名词 sustentatio → 古法语 sustenence → 英语 sustenance；核心义「从下面托住，使不倒」。

sensesIntro.en: Sustenance begins as the food that holds a body upright, passes to the nourishment inside it, then to what holds a spirit up, and ends as livelihood and formal support.
sensesIntro.cn: sustenance 先是托住身体的食物，再指其中的养分，然后指托住精神的养料，最后成为生计与正式用语中的支撑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand holding a bowl from underneath, so that nothing in it can drop.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手从底下托住碗，碗里的东西不会掉。

branches.en: THE BREAD: what holds the body up is named first, and it is food.
branches.cn: 面包：最先被命名的是托住身体的东西，也就是食物。

branches.en: THE NOURISHMENT: the word slips from the plate to what the plate gives.
branches.cn: 养分：词从餐盘滑到餐盘所给予的东西。

branches.en: THE SPIRIT: what holds up a body can hold up a mind, once the object is invisible.
branches.cn: 精神：托住身体的东西也能托住心灵，只是被托的对象变得看不见了。

branches.en: THE HOUSEHOLD: the same support widened from one meal to a whole way of earning.
branches.cn: 家庭：同一支撑从一顿饭扩大到一整种营生。

branches.en: THE ABSTRACT POST: the nourishing and the supporting senses both stand for a stay that keeps something upright.
branches.cn: 抽象支柱：养料之义与支撑之义都是让某物立住的倚靠。

intro.en: Sustenance is a Latin compound, sub- plus tenere, and that hold-verb recurs across English in contain, maintain, tenant and sustain.
intro.cn: sustenance 是拉丁语复合词，由 sub- 与 tenere 组成；这个「握住」动词在英语的 contain、maintain、tenant、sustain 里反复出现。

latinIntro.en: Latin tenere means to hold or keep, and its supine stem tent- gives the noun ending -tent- that we see in sustenance.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tenere 意为「握住、保持」，它的名词词干 tent- 给出了 sustenance 里的 -tent- 部分。

items.example: The prefix pictures support coming from underneath.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀描绘支撑来自下方。

items.example: Tenere is the holding hand in the word.
items.exampleCN: tenere 就是词里那只托着的手。

items.example: The columns sustain the weight of the roof.
items.exampleCN: 这些柱子托住屋顶的重量。

items.example: The suffix turns a holding act into a state.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把「托住」的动作变成一种状态。

items.example: The noun names both the bread and the upkeep.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词既指面包，也指供养。

items.example: A small fire sustains the warmth of the room.
items.exampleCN: 一小堆火维持着房间的暖意。

items.example: The suffix marks what can be supported in the long run.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾标出能在长远上被支撑的东西。

items.example: The same stem appears in words about bearing weight.
items.exampleCN: 同一词干出现在表示「承重」的词里。

items.example: Together with the hold-verb it makes a word for enclosing.
items.exampleCN: 与「握住」动词结合，构成表示「围住」的词。

items.example: The box can contain only one pair of shoes.
items.exampleCN: 这盒子只能装下一双鞋。

definition_zh: 一大群（蜂、蚁等昆虫）；蜂群；成群结队地移动；涌向；蜂拥而至
definition_en: a very large group of insects or small animals moving together, and the act of such a group crowding towards something
core_image: 一团黑色的点忽然从树洞里涌出来，在空中打成一个不停变换形状的球
scene: 养蜂人掀开蜂箱的盖子，空气立刻嗡嗡作响。The beekeeper lifted the lid and a swarm of bees rose into the sunlight.
sceneCN: 这里 swarm 是「蜂群、一大群昆虫」（第 1 个义项：成群飞动的许多小动物）；句意：养蜂人掀开箱盖，一群蜜蜂升到阳光里。那团不停变形的黑点，就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 一大群昆虫或小动物；蜂群；蜂拥的人群
成群移动；蜂拥而至

derivatives.zh: 由 swarm 加 -ing 构成，义为「成群聚集、蜂拥」或「成群的」
加形容词词尾 -y 构成，口语中形容「像蜂群一样拥挤的、乱糟糟的」
加 -er 构成，指「成群行动者」，也指某些有翅蚂蚁或蜜蜂
过去分词作形容词，义为「被成群占满的」

senses.title: A moving cloud of small animals
senses.definition: a large group of insects or other small creatures that travel together as one body
senses.definitionCN: 一大群一起移动、像一个整体似昆虫或其他小生物
senses.example: A swarm of bees settled on the low branch.
senses.exampleCN: 一群蜜蜂落到了那根低枝上。
senses.why: The Old English word first named a body of bees leaving the hive together, and that moveable cloud is the core image.
senses.whyCN: 古英语原指离巢一起飞走的一群蜜蜂，那团会移动的云彩就是核心意象。

senses.title: To fly or move in a dense crowd
senses.definition: to move in a large mass, especially insects, as if driven by one impulse
senses.definitionCN: 尤指昆虫以一大团的形式移动，好像被同一个冲动驱使
senses.example: Mosquitoes swarmed around the lamp until dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 蚊子在灯周围嗡嗡地转到天亮。
senses.why: Once the group was named, the act of forming and moving as that group took the same word as a verb.
senses.whyCN: 群体有了名字之后，形成并作为群体移动的动作就直接用这个词做动词。

senses.title: Of a place: teeming with
senses.definition: to be so full of people or creatures that they seem to be moving everywhere
senses.definitionCN: 塞满了人或生物，看上去处处都在动
senses.example: The market swarmed with traders shouting prices.
senses.exampleCN: 市场上挤满了大声叫价的商贩。
senses.why: A full market looks exactly like a hive: too many small movers for the eye to follow one.
senses.whyCN: 热闹的市场和蜂箱一模一样：小动作太多，眼睛跟不上任何一个。

senses.title: Of people: to crowd round
senses.definition: to come in a crowd, often towards someone or something exciting
senses.definitionCN: 成群地来，常常涌向某个热闹或惹眼的目标
senses.example: Reporters swarmed towards the car with their cameras up.
senses.exampleCN: 记者们举着相机蜂拥冲向那辆车。
senses.why: People who rush at a single point share the bees instinct: they stop being individuals for a moment.
senses.whyCN: 涌向同一点的人带着蜜蜂的本能：那一刻他们不再是一个个人。

senses.title: A vast number, as a measurement
senses.definition: a very large number of things of one kind, used loosely as a count
senses.definitionCN: 同类事物中数量极大的一个群体，用作宽泛的量词
senses.example: A swarm of tiny satellites now circles the planet.
senses.exampleCN: 如今有一大批微型卫星绕着地球运行。
senses.why: From insects the word widened to any mass of small similar units, and then to satellites and particles.
senses.whyCN: 从昆虫扩展到了任何由众多相似小单位组成的团块，后来又指卫星和粒子。

senses.title: A group that thinks as one
senses.definition: an engineered group of simple agents that act well together without a central leader
senses.definitionCN: 人为设计的一组简单个体，在无中心领导的情况下协同行动
senses.example: The engineers tested a swarm of small robots in the warehouse.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师们在仓库里测试了一群小型机器人。
senses.why: Biologists borrowed the bee word for collective behaviour, and robotics borrowed it again for machines that behave like insects.
senses.whyCN: 生物学家借蜂群之名称呼集体行为，机器人学界又借用它称呼那些像昆虫一样行动的机器。

intro.en: Swarm is an inherited Germanic word, recorded in Old English as swearm. Its deeper ancestry is uncertain.
intro.cn: swarm 是日耳曼语系继承词，古英语记作 swearm。它更早的来源不确定。

items.en: A reconstructed form such as swarmaz is usually proposed, and scholars connect it cautiously with the Latin word for a crowd of bees; the link is not settled.
items.cn: 一般重构为类似 swarmaz 的形式，学者谨慎地把它与拉丁语中表示蜂群的词联系起来；这一联系尚无定论。

items.en: Swearm named a body of bees, and by extension any dense crowd of small creatures.
items.cn: swearm 指一群蜜蜂，进而泛指任何密集的小生物集团。

items.en: The spelling settled towards swarm, and the word took on the verb sense of moving in a crowd.
items.cn: 拼写逐渐固定为 swarm，并发展出「成群移动」的动词义。

items.en: Writers used the word for people, crowds and even armies, so that swarming meant rushing in great numbers.
items.cn: 作家用它指人、人群甚至军队，于是 swarming 表示「大批地涌」。

items.en: Science reused the old bee word for collective behaviour: swarm intelligence, then drone swarms, particle swarms and satellite swarms.
items.cn: 科学界重新启用这个古老的蜂群词来指集体行为：群体智能，随后又有无人机群、粒子群与卫星群。

note.en: Group one holds close relatives and a look-alike trap; group two holds other words for a crowd of moving things.
note.cn: 第一组是近亲词与一个容易看错的形近词；第二组是其他表示「一群动的东西」的词。

entries.definition: The Old English spelling of the word, naming a body of bees before the s was lost in pronunciation.
entries.definitionCN: 这个词的古英语拼法，当年就指一群蜜蜂，后来读音里的这个拼写被简化。

entries.definition: An informal adjective from the noun, meaning crowded like a swarm.
entries.definitionCN: 由名词派生出的非正式形容词，义为「像蜂群一样拥挤的」。

entries.definition: Differs only by the initial s: a temperature word, with an entirely different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 只差开头的 s：表示温度的形容词，词源完全不同，只是拼写相近。

entries.definition: Shares the opening sw- sound but no meaning, and comes from a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 开头 sw- 的读音相近，但意思无关，词源也不同。

entries.definition: The usual word for a group of birds or sheep moving together, less frantic than a swarm.
entries.definitionCN: 鸟群或羊群一起移动的常用词，不如 swarm 那样乱而躁。

entries.definition: A group of large animals such as cattle, kept or moving together.
entries.definitionCN: 牛等大型动物聚成的一群，常被一起照料或一起移动。

entries.definition: A densely packed crowd of people, close to swarm when the subject is human.
entries.definitionCN: 挤得很密的人群，主语是人时与 swarm 最近。

entries.definition: A great crowd, often used with a hint of disorder or threat.
entries.definitionCN: 一大群人，常带一点无序或来势汹汹的意味。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the hive image inside the Old English word, the fixed phrases, and the family of forms.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：古英语原词里的蜂箱意象、固定搭配，以及它的形式家族。

normal.en: Swarm with is the fixed pattern for a place full of moving things: the road swarms with cyclists.
normal.cn: 「swarm with」是固定句式，用于满是活动物的场所：路上满是骑自行车的人。

normal.en: The word covers both the group and its motion: a swarm of bees, and the bees swarm.
normal.cn: 这个词同时覆盖群体与运动：一群蜜蜂，以及蜜蜂成群飞。

normal.en: Swarm intelligence takes the bee idea to engineering: many simple agents, no leader.
normal.cn: 群体智能把蜜蜂的思路带进工程：许多简单个体，没有领头者。

normal.en: Other crowd words keep their owners: a flock of birds, a herd of cattle, a swarm of bees.
normal.cn: 其他群体词各有归属：鸟用 flock，牛用 herd，蜂用 swarm。

normal.en: Beware of warm and sword: same opening sound, different origins.
normal.cn: 小心 warm 与 sword：开头声音像，词源不同。

abstract.en: Picture a single dot on a window, then a hundred dots turning it grey.
abstract.cn: 想象窗上只有一个黑点，接着一百个黑点把窗涂成灰色。

abstract.en: Picture a bowl of soup that suddenly lifts off and reforms as a cloud.
abstract.cn: 想象一碗汤忽然腾空，重新聚成一朵云。

abstract.en: Picture a mob of fans moving like one wave over a fence.
abstract.cn: 想象一群粉丝像一道浪一样翻过围栏。

examples.en: When the hive is too crowded, the bees swarm and find a new home.
examples.cn: 蜂箱太挤时，蜜蜂就会成群分家去找新住处。

examples.en: After the concert, the square swarmed with young fans.
examples.cn: 音乐会散场后，广场上挤满了年轻的粉丝。

examples.en: A dark swarm of locusts moved across the fields in minutes.
examples.cn: 一大片黑压压的蝗群几分钟就扫过了田野。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死窝母」——蜂群护巢时真的会「死守蜂窝」，一听就是一大群蜂；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 swearm（一群蜜蜂）→ 中古英语 swarm → 现代英语 swarm；一般认为与日耳曼语同源形式有关，更早来源不确定，部分学者谨慎联系拉丁语表示蜂群的词，但未见定论。

sensesIntro.en: Swarm starts from the picture of a bee colony leaving home as one moving cloud, then grows into the verb of such movement, the teeming place, the rushing crowd and finally technical groups of agents.
sensesIntro.cn: swarm 起于蜂群离巢、合成一团移动云彩的画面，再长成描述这种移动的动词、挤满的场所、涌来的人潮，最后进入技术领域的群体概念。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dark cloud of tiny movers that changes shape as it travels.
core.cn: 核心意象：一团会随移动而变形的微小生物黑云。

branches.en: THE CLOUD: the group itself is the oldest and simplest sense.
branches.cn: 黑云：群体本身就是最古老也最单纯的义项。

branches.en: THE MOTION: forming the cloud became a verb, and anything may be said to swarm.
branches.cn: 移动：合成黑云的动作变成动词，任何东西都可以说群飞。

branches.en: THE FULL PLACE: a place that looks like a hive swarms with small things.
branches.cn: 挤满之地：像蜂箱一样的地方会「满是」小东西。

branches.en: THE WAVE: people who rush at one point, and any mass of similar small units, share the shape of a swarm.
branches.cn: 浪潮：涌向一点的人，以及任何众多相似小单位，都带着蜂群的形状。

branches.en: THE NETWORK: the bee group became a model for machines and algorithms that work without a leader.
branches.cn: 网络：蜂群成了无领导者协同工作的机器与算法的范本。

intro.en: Swarm is a Germanic word with no Latin ancestry, so its parts are English forms built on the stem rather than classical affixes.
intro.cn: swarm 是日耳曼语词，没有拉丁语血统，因此它的组成部分都是围绕词干构造的英语形式，而不是古典词缀。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin cognate of swarm that can be relied on. Latin had words for a crowd of bees and for swarming honey, but no secure link to this English word is established.
latinIntro.cn: swarm 没有可以依据的拉丁同族词。拉丁语里虽有表示蜂群和群蜂蜂蜜的词，但与这个英语词之间尚无可靠的联系。

items.meaning: a moving mass of small creatures
items.meaningCN: 成群移动的小生物群体
items.example: A swarm leaves the hive when it grows too large.
items.exampleCN: 蜂巢太大时就会有蜂群离巢。

items.meaning: to move as such a mass
items.example: Locusts swarm across a field within minutes.
items.exampleCN: 蝗虫几分钟内就成群越过田野。

items.meaning: the act, or a continuing process
items.meaningCN: 表示动作或持续过程的词尾
items.example: The river bank was swarming with ants.
items.exampleCN: 河岸上爬满了蚂蚁。

items.example: Swarming is how honeybees reproduce a colony.
items.exampleCN: 分蜂是蜜蜂繁殖蜂群的方式。

items.example: The suffix makes a loose adjective from the noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾由名词造出一个松散的形容词。

items.example: The old market felt warm and swarmy at noon.
items.exampleCN: 正午的老市场又热又挤。

items.example: The suffix names the creature that swarms.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾指成群行动的那一方。

items.meaningCN: 分蜂的蜜蜂；有翅迁飞的蚂蚁
items.example: Male ants become swarmers before the summer rains.
items.exampleCN: 夏雨之前，雄蚁会变成迁飞个体。

items.meaningCN: 无中心领导的群体问题解决能力
items.example: Engineers copied swarm intelligence from the hive.
items.exampleCN: 工程师从蜂箱里借来了群体智能。

definition_zh: 热得难受；闷热难熬；（热得）汗流浃背，疲惫不堪；闷热
definition_en: to be so hot that you feel faint and heavy, or to feel crushed by heat and hard work
core_image: 正午的屋顶下，一个人坐着不动，汗水顺着脖子往下淌，空气像蒸笼一样压在身上
scene: 七月的港口没有一丝风，集装箱铁皮被晒得烫手，工人们靠在阴影里大口喘气。The dockworkers sweltered under the tin roof all afternoon.
sceneCN: 这里 swelter 是「热得难受、闷热难熬」（第 1 个义项：在闷热中受煎熬）；句意：码头工人整个下午都在铁皮屋顶下热得难受。

pos.zh: 热得难受；闷热难熬；（热得）汗流浃背
闷热；闷热难熬的状态

derivatives.zh: 动词加 -ing 转形容词，义为「闷热的；使人热得发昏的」
过去分词转形容词，义为「被酷热熬得疲惫不堪的」
古旧变体，义为「闷热的」，今多写作 sultry，属同源异体

senses.title: To suffer in oppressive heat
senses.definition: to be in a place so hot and humid that the body feels heavy and the air seems to press down
senses.definitionCN: 身处又热又潮的地方，感到身体沉重、空气像压下来一样难受
senses.example: The passengers sweltered in the stalled bus for an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 乘客们在抛锚的公共汽车里闷热难熬地等了一个小时。
senses.why: The oldest core of the word is a heat so heavy that the body slows down, which is why swelter always carries discomfort and never pleasant warmth.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最古老的语义中心是「重得让人身体变慢的炎热」，所以 swelter 总带难受感，从不表示舒服的温暖。

senses.title: To be soaked and exhausted by heat
senses.definition: to be dripping with sweat and worn out by heat or by hot, hard work
senses.definitionCN: 因酷热或酷热中的苦干而汗流浃背、筋疲力尽
senses.example: The miners sweltered in the tunnel with no air moving at all.
senses.exampleCN: 矿工们在毫无空气流动的坑道里汗流浃背、疲惫不堪。
senses.why: Later English use added sweat and exhaustion to the mere feeling of heat, matching an older related form that meant to be soaked.
senses.whyCN: 后来的英语用法在「热」之上加了「汗」与「累」，这与同源的另一个古旧形式「被浸透」义相呼应。

senses.title: Oppressive heat as a condition
senses.definition: a state of hot, damp, still air in which people feel heavy and uncomfortable
senses.definitionCN: 又热又潮、空气停滞、令人喘息不畅的状态
senses.example: We left the swelter of the kitchen and stepped onto the cool balcony.
senses.exampleCN: 我们离开闷热的厨房，走上凉爽的阳台。
senses.why: The verb turned into a noun naming the condition itself, so the heat can now be a place one steps out of rather than something one endures.
senses.whyCN: 动词名词化后，闷热本身成了一种处境，于是它可以是「走出来的地方」，而不只是「忍受的状态」。

senses.title: To boil or seethe like something on a fire
senses.definition: an older use meaning to boil, seethe, or bubble over, said of liquids on a fire
senses.definitionCN: 较古老的用法，指液体在火上沸腾、翻滚、冒泡
senses.example: In that old recipe the broth is left to swelter over a low fire.
senses.exampleCN: 在那份古旧的食谱里，肉汤要用小火慢慢翻滚。
senses.why: The heat image of this word family first described liquids bubbling on a fire, and this sense survives only in old texts.
senses.whyCN: 这个词族的热意象最初描写的正是火上翻滚的液体，这一义项只保存在古旧文本中。

intro.en: Swelter comes from a Germanic verb for dying or burning up, probably from Old English sweltan, and its first record is uncertain.
intro.cn: swelter 来自日耳曼语中表示「死去、烧尽」的一族动词，一般认为源自古英语 sweltan；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: *sweltan is generally reconstructed as a verb meaning to die or to burn up. The deeper Proto-Indo-European source is uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始日耳曼语 *sweltan 表示「死去、烧尽」；更早的原始印欧语来源不确定。

items.en: Sweltan is recorded in Old English meaning to die or to perish, so heat was not yet its main sense.
items.cn: 古英语 sweltan 意为「死、消亡」，此时「热」还不是它主要的含义。

items.en: From about the thirteenth century the word is recorded with meanings of burning up and perishing of heat; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 约自十三世纪起，该词有「烧尽、被热折磨而死」等义，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Swelter is recorded from the sixteenth century with the modern idea of sweating under heavy heat.
items.cn: swelter 自十六世纪起有记录，带上了「在酷热中流汗」的现代含义。

items.en: Nineteenth-century writing popularised sweltering as a description of tropical and city heat.
items.cn: 十九世纪的作品让 sweltering 成为描写热带与城市酷热的常用词。

items.en: The word is now almost always about discomfort in humid heat, and the boiling sense survives only in old texts.
items.cn: 如今这个词几乎只用于潮湿酷热中的难受感，沸腾义只留存在古旧文本里。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers kin and near spellings of the same heat family; the near-meaning group gathers the main heat words by how bright, how hot, and how sticky they are.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「热」词族的亲族词与近形拼写；近义组按亮、热、潮湿三种程度收主要的「热」词。

entries.definition: an Old English verb meaning to die or to perish, the probable ancestor of the modern word.
entries.definitionCN: 古英语中意为「死去、消亡」的动词，是现代词的祖先这一说法较可信。

entries.definition: an old spelling variant meaning sultry or sweltering, now rare.
entries.definitionCN: 表示「闷热的」的古旧拼写变体，今罕见。

entries.definition: slim and elegant; merely spelled alike, from French, with a different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「苗条优雅的」；只是拼写相近，来自法语，词源不同。

entries.definition: hot and humid in a heavy, still way that tires people out.
entries.definitionCN: 闷热而潮湿、空气停滞、令人疲乏的。

entries.definition: so hot and airless that breathing becomes hard.
entries.definitionCN: 热得令人透不过气、呼吸困难的。

entries.definition: extremely hot, usually of dry heat that burns exposed skin.
entries.definitionCN: 极热的，多指干燥、会灼伤皮肤的热。

normalIntro.en: Swelter is a heavy sweating heat, tied to an old word for dying, so the body is worn down rather than merely warm.
normalIntro.cn: swelter 是令人冒汗的沉重酷热，联系着一个表示「死」的古老词根，所以重在身体被熬垮，而不只是暖和。

normal.en: The workers sweltered in the heat all week.
normal.cn: 工人们整整一周都在酷热中熬着。

normal.en: A sweltering July afternoon is hot, wet, and still.
normal.cn: sweltering 的七月下午是又热又潮又闷的。

normal.en: To swelter is to sweat and feel faint at the same time.
normal.cn: swelter 就是一边出汗一边头晕。

normal.en: The word keeps no pleasant warmth; it always means misery.
normal.cn: 这个词不保留「暖和」的愉快感，总指难受。

normal.en: Compare sultry, which is close but heavier on stillness and slower to say.
normal.cn: 对比 sultry：意思接近，但更强调空气停滞，语感也更沉。

abstract.en: Picture a glass roof pressing down on a crowded market at noon.
abstract.cn: 想象正午的玻璃顶压着一座拥挤的市场。

abstract.en: Imagine taking off your jacket and finding that it is already soaked.
abstract.cn: 想象脱下外套，发现它早已湿透。

abstract.en: Think of opening a door onto a rush of hot air and closing it again at once.
abstract.cn: 想象推门时一团热气扑面而来，又立刻把门关上。

examples.en: The whole class sweltered in the windowless room while the fans were broken.
examples.cn: 风扇坏着，全班在无窗的屋子里热得难受。

examples.en: Tourists sweltered in the crowded museum on the hottest day of the year.
examples.cn: 一年中最热的那天，游客们在拥挤的博物馆里闷热难熬。

examples.en: Sweltering nights kept the whole street awake, so the family drove to the coast.
examples.cn: 闷热的夜晚让整条街都睡不着，一家人便开车去了海边。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死围了特」——一群人被热浪死命围住，特难受；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 日耳曼语 *sweltan（死去、烧尽）→ 古英语 sweltan（死、消亡）→ 中古英语「烧尽、被热折磨」→ 英语 swelter（闷热难熬）；核心义「被酷热熬垮」。

sensesIntro.en: Swelter starts from suffering in heavy heat, adds sweat and exhaustion, then becomes the name of the condition itself, with an old boiling sense kept only in old texts.
sensesIntro.cn: swelter 从「在酷热中受苦」出发，加上汗水与疲惫，再名词化为闷热本身，古老的沸腾义只留存在旧文本里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a man under a tin roof at noon, sweat running down his neck.
core.cn: 核心意象：正午铁皮屋顶下，汗水顺着脖子流下的人。

branches.en: The everyday sense is suffering in heat that presses down.
branches.cn: 日常义就是被压下来的酷热折磨。

branches.en: Sweat and tiredness turn the heat into physical labour.
branches.cn: 汗水与疲惫把热变成了体力上的煎熬。

branches.en: The condition sense lets heat be a place you leave.
branches.cn: 处境义让闷热成为可以离开的地方。

branches.en: The verb and the noun differ only in whether the heat is an experience or a surroundings.
branches.cn: 动词与名词的差别只在于热是体验还是周围的环境。

branches.en: Soaked with sweat and bubbling on a fire come from the same hot-water image.
branches.cn: 汗湿透衣与火上翻滚出自同一个「滚热的水」的意象。

intro.en: Swelter sits in a Germanic heat family with no Latin root; English built sweltering, sweltered, and the rare sweltry around it.
intro.cn: swelter 属于日耳曼语系的「热」词族，没有拉丁词根，英语围绕它构成 sweltering、sweltered 与少见的 sweltry。

latinIntro.en: No Latin source is attested; the word belongs to a Germanic family and Latin kin should not be invented.
latinIntro.cn: 没有证据支持任何拉丁语来源；该词属于日耳曼语族，不应杜撰拉丁同族词。

items.example: Sweltan is the probable ancestor of the modern word.
items.exampleCN: sweltan 很可能是现代词的祖先。

items.example: Swelter is the everyday verb of steamy heat.
items.exampleCN: swelter 是表示湿热难受的日常动词。

items.meaning: forming a participle or an adjective
items.meaningCN: 构成分词或形容词的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ing forms sweltering.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 sweltering。

items.meaningCN: 闷热的；热得让人发昏的
items.example: Sweltering describes the air itself.
items.exampleCN: sweltering 描写空气本身。

items.meaning: forming a participle or an adjective
items.meaningCN: 构成分词或形容词的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ed forms sweltered.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 sweltered。

items.example: Sweltered leads mostly to be sweltered, as in British use.
items.exampleCN: 英式用法中 sweltered 多写作 be sweltered。

items.example: Sweltry is a rare old variant.
